The core flow is payment-gated access: `POST /sessions/:id/enroll` creates a `PENDING_PAYMENT` enrollment plus a Razorpay order, and `POST /enrollments/:id/verify` flips it to `PAID` only after an order-id match against the persisted `razorpayOrderId` and a timing-safe signature check; the Jitsi `roomUrl` is stripped from public listings and revealed only to the instructor, admins, or `PAID` enrollees. A notable branch is the demo mode (`isDemoPayment` when `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` is unset), which synthesizes order ids and skips signature verification so the whole flow runs in dev, and free "satsang" sessions (`isFree`, price forced to 0) enroll instantly as `PAID` with no payment step as a top-of-funnel strategy. Capacity is enforced by counting `PAID` plus `PENDING_PAYMENT` enrollments (pending rows hold a slot), and re-enrolling an existing pending row is idempotent so retries don't double-book. After a successful verify, `writeWellnessCommissionOnPaid` fire-and-forgets a `PENDING` `commission` row for the instructor's share (price × (1 − `WELLNESS_PLATFORM_COMMISSION`, default 0.20)); it is idempotent against duplicate verifies and intentionally cannot roll back the PAID flip, as is the invoice email. Smaller gotchas: `scheduledAt` cannot be in the past on create (the public list only shows future sessions, so a past row would be silently invisible) but the refine is relaxed on update for cancellation cleanup, `priceInr` is serialized to a string because it is a Prisma Decimal, and session delete manually cascade-removes enrollments first to avoid FK violations.

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\wellness.ts.summary: This file is the wellness module of the Fastify API (`apps/api`): it defines the route plugin for the wellness domain (the `FastifyInstance` import signals a standard Fastify route-registration export) and, in the visible portion, consists almost entirely of hardcoded seed data served by those routes. The two main in-module constants are `instructors` — ten wellness teacher profiles (e.g., Aarav Sharma, Dr. Kavita Nair, Acharya Goenkaji) spanning the `yoga`, `meditation`, `vipassana`, and `ayurveda` categories, each with slug, bio, certifications, languages, `availableSlots`, embedded `reviews`, rating, and per-session pricing in INR — and `programs`, a catalog of multi-week offerings such as the "21-Day Meditation Kickstart", "Ashtanga Primary Series Intensive", "Vipassana 10-Day Residential Retreat", and "Corporate Mindfulness — 8-Week MBSR", each linking back to an instructor via `instructorId` and carrying duration, level, start dates, and spot availability. The only external dependency is Fastify itself; there is no database, ORM, or service layer — all content is static module-level data, which means any write operations (bookings, new reviews) have no persistence behind them. Notable gotchas: instructor photos are hotlinked Unsplash URLs reused across multiple profiles, several instructor bios reference an external "Darshya" app, prices are bare numbers with implicit rupee currency, and one program is donation-based with `price: 0`, so consumers should not assume price is always meaningful. Because the data is embedded in the route file, the module doubles as both API layer and fixture store, and adding or editing content requires a code change and redeploy.

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\yatra-inquiry.ts.summary: This Fastify route file handles yatra (pilgrimage tour) package commerce for the Darshya API, exposing both a legacy inquiry-intake flow and a real Razorpay checkout for five packaged tours with confirmed availability (Char Dham, Vaishno Devi, Tirupati, Kashi, Shirdi). The exported `yatraInquiryRoutes(server)` registers three endpoints: `POST /` sends admin and buyer confirmation emails plus WhatsApp template notifications for manual booking handoff; `POST /create-order` creates a Razorpay order and persists a `pending_payment` row in the `yatra_bookings` table; and `POST /verify-payment` validates the Razorpay HMAC-SHA256 signature with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` before flipping the booking to `confirmed` and emailing a receipt. It depends on internal modules `prisma`, `sendEmail`, `sendWhatsappTemplate`/`whatsapp`, and `assertNotProductionDemo`, plus the external `razorpay` SDK and `zod` for request validation. Notable design choices: a demo-payment mode (triggered when `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` is missing or `rzp_test_demo`) synthesizes fake order IDs so dev and e2e environments work without real credentials, with `assertNotProductionDemo` guarding against that leaking into production. The `yatra_bookings` table is created lazily via raw `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` SQL rather than a Prisma migration, and all persistence uses `$queryRawUnsafe`/`$executeRawUnsafe` with parameterized queries. A flagged gotcha is that `totalInr` comes from the client with only a sanity bound (500–2,000,000 INR), with a comment noting server-side price verification is deferred to the next iteration; demo mode also skips signature verification entirely.

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\whatsapp-otp.ts.summary: This Fastify route module implements WhatsApp-based phone OTP authentication as a cheaper, higher-delivery alternative to SMS in India, exposing POST /request (sends a 6-digit code via the approved "otp_login" template) and POST /verify (validates the code, finds-or-creates the user, and issues a session token). The sole export, `whatsappOtpRoutes(server: FastifyInstance)`, registers both handlers; internally it relies on `generateOtp` (crypto-based), `normalisePhone` (assumes +91 for 10-digit Indian numbers), and an in-memory `otpStore` Map keyed by phone holding `OtpRecord` entries with a 5-minute TTL and 3-attempt limit. It depends on `prisma` from ../lib/prisma.js for user lookup/creation and on `sendWhatsappTemplate` plus the `whatsapp` client from ../lib/whatsapp.js for message delivery, using node:crypto for code and token generation. Notably, the returned session token uses the same `email-<userId>-<32hex>` format as magic-link auth so the existing auth middleware accepts both without changes. Both endpoints carry a 10/min per-IP rate limit (comment P1-1) mirroring /auth/send-otp and /auth/login, since the global 100/min cap previously left the pair open to template spam and phone enumeration. A security fix (comment P0-4) gates the `devCode` response field on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` rather than just `whatsapp.enabled` — previously, missing WHATSAPP_* env vars in prod caused /request to echo the live code, enabling instant takeover of any phone number since /verify creates users on the fly. Gotchas: the in-memory store means OTPs don't survive restarts or work across multiple instances, and new users are auto-created with placeholder defaults (fullName 'Devotee', preferredLanguage 'hi').

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\yatra-packages.t.summary: This file defines `yatraPackagesRoutes`, a Fastify plugin implementing "Layer AU" — directly bookable, vertically-integrated yatra (tour) packages that carry 20–30% margins, in contrast to the M1 layer's affiliate redirects to MMT/Goibibo/IRCTC. It exposes three endpoints: `GET /` lists active packages with optional `destination` and `maxPrice` query filters, `GET /:slug` returns a single package detail, and `POST /:slug/book` (guarded by the `authenticateUser` middleware and validated with a zod `bookSchema`) creates a booking and returns a generated `bookingNumber` with status `pending_payment`. The module depends on the shared `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js` and two PostgreSQL tables, `yatra_packages` and `yatra_bookings`, which are provisioned lazily at route registration via `ensureTables()` using raw `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statements rather than Prisma migrations — initialization failures are only logged as warnings. The booking flow is deliberately wrapped in a `prisma.$transaction` with a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` row lock on the package, so concurrent bookings serialize and a crash cannot leave an orphan booking or oversell `max_group_size`; full groups return 409. Notable gotchas: all queries use `$queryRawUnsafe`/`$executeRawUnsafe` (parameterized, but bypassing Prisma's model layer), the `razorpay_order_id` column anticipates a Razorpay payment step that isn't implemented here, `bookingNumber()` relies on `Math.random()` for uniqueness (backstopped by a unique constraint), the list endpoint silently swallows errors by returning an empty array, and `maxPrice` is coerced with `Number()` without validation.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\admin.service..summary: This Vitest suite verifies AdminService from apps/api/src/services/admin.service.ts by substituting the real Prisma client with prismaMock from lib/__mocks__/prisma.js, letting each test assert the exact query shapes the service emits. It covers getUsers (case-insensitive search OR-ed across fullName, email, and phone; skip/take pagination; enrichment with roles from userRoleAssignment where users default to DEVOTEE; and post-query role filtering), getUserById (null passthrough plus attachment of role names and per-type profiles: panditProfile, storeProfile, astrologerProfile, wellnessProfile, gaushalaProfile, templeProfile), and updateUser (role replacement via deleteMany plus createMany with the first role flagged isPrimary, and approval routed to the updateMany of whichever profile table matches the user's role). It also tests getDashboard's aggregation of user counts, usersByRole tallies, marketplaceSubscription and transaction revenue, and pendingApprovals summed across the six profile tables, and getRevenue's split of PAID versus PENDING commission rows plus subscription grouping by plan and role. The key gotcha, documented by inline comments dated 2026-07-17, is that getUsers and getDashboard must now rethrow database errors rather than mask outages behind MOCK_USERS or fake dashboard metrics, and the tests pin that behavior. In contrast, getRevenue is explicitly expected to fall back to positive demo numbers when its queries fail, an intentional inconsistency the suite locks in. Everything runs through vi.mock hoisting and vi.clearAllMocks in beforeEach, so no real database is touched.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\ai.service.tes.summary: This Vitest suite exercises `AiService` from `apps/api/src/services/ai.service.ts`, covering its chat, recommendation, and conversation-management behavior without touching a real database or LLM. It mocks the Prisma client via `prismaMock` from `lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` and stubs the `integrations/claude.js` module with hoisted `generateTextMock` and `streamChatMock` functions, notably overriding `MODELS` with Llama model names, which reveals the "claude" integration actually points at Groq-hosted models. The tests verify that `chat` treats `demo-*` and `anon-*` user IDs as synthetic users: it returns a generated `conv-` prefixed conversation ID, skips all `aiConversation` database writes, makes `saveConversation` a no-op, and still returns a `citations` array from RAG-retrieved verses. For real users, it asserts that `chat` creates a new conversation when none is given, throws "Conversation not found" for a bad `conversationId`, and that `saveConversation` appends the user and assistant messages onto the existing message array via `prisma.aiConversation.update`. The `recommendPujas` tests confirm that a successful `generateText` call yields the LLM explanation while a failure falls back to a deterministic "Based on your spiritual profile" message. Finally, `listConversations` is checked for empty results without DB access for demo users and correct pagination math (page 2, limit 5 → `skip: 5`, ordered by `updatedAt desc`), while `getConversation` and `deleteConversation` are verified to short-circuit for demo users and to enforce ownership by scoping `findFirst` lookups before deleting.

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\whatsapp-otp.tes.summary: This Vitest suite tests the `whatsappOtpRoutes` authentication endpoints (`POST /request` and `POST /verify`, mounted at `/api/v1/auth/whatsapp-otp`) in isolation, mocking `../lib/prisma.js` (stubbing the find-or-create user path so `/verify` never touches a DB) and `../lib/whatsapp.js` (forcing `whatsapp.enabled = false` with a controllable `sendWhatsappTemplate`). A `buildApp()` helper assembles a Fastify instance with the `@fastify/rate-limit` plugin registered, then drives all requests through `app.inject()` rather than real HTTP. The suite locks in two security fixes: P0-4, verifying the six-digit `devCode` is never leaked in responses when `NODE_ENV=production` (fail-closed even when WhatsApp delivery is disabled) while it is intentionally exposed in dev/test mode for local QA; and P1-1, verifying the route's sensitive-auth limit of 10 requests/minute returns 429 on the eleventh call despite the plugin's looser 100/min global default. Additional cases cover phone validation rejecting numbers under 10 digits with 400, a full request→verify round-trip that issues a session whose `accessToken` matches the pattern `email-{userId}-{32 hex chars}` (suggesting shared session-issuing logic with the email OTP flow), and a wrong code returning 400 with `attemptsLeft: 2`, implying a three-attempt budget. Test isolation relies on toggling `process.env.NODE_ENV` per test with save/restore in `afterEach` and clearing mocks in `beforeEach`.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\apollo.service.summary: This file implements a resilient client for the Apollo.io people-search API, used to surface sales leads as part of the leads pipeline. Its single public entry point is `searchPeople`, which takes an `ApolloPersonQuery` (organization keyword tags, person titles, locations, pagination) and returns a normalized array of `ApolloPerson` records containing name, email, title, organization, and a location string assembled from city/state/country. It posts to `https://api.apollo.io/v1/mixed_people/search` with the `APOLLO_API_KEY` header, validates the response with zod schemas (`ApolloSearchResponse`, `ApolloPersonRaw`), and merges the `people` and `contacts` result arrays into one flat list. The defining design choice is that the service never throws: any failure — missing API key, non-2xx status, validation error, or network exception — logs a `console.warn` and returns an empty array, so callers can treat it as an optional enrichment source. For compliance, phone numbers from Apollo are deliberately dropped (email-only persistence per `docs/leads-pipeline.md`), and `isUsableEmail` rejects Apollo's paywalled placeholder addresses like `email_not_unlocked@domain.com`. Credit consumption is a documented constraint: the free tier allows 60 credits/month, and the default of `per_page: 10, page: 1` means one call can burn up to 10 credits. Private helpers (`buildName`, `buildLocation`, `isUsableEmail`, `ApolloSearchResponse`) are exposed via the `__test__` export for unit testing.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\admin.service..summary: This file implements `AdminService`, the backend for the admin console of a spiritual-services marketplace: it lists and searches users, manages role assignments and provider approvals, and aggregates dashboard, revenue, and reporting metrics. Its key methods are `getUsers` (paginated search with role enrichment from `UserRoleAssignment`), `getUserById` (fetches a user plus all six provider profiles: `panditProfile`, `storeProfile`, `astrologerProfile`, `wellnessProfile`, `gaushalaProfile`, `templeProfile`), `updateUser` (rewrites role assignments, seeds stub provider profiles via upsert so the approvals queue isn't silently empty, toggles `approved` flags per role, and sends best-effort `providerApprovedEmail`/`providerRejectedEmail`), plus `getDashboard`, `getRevenue`, and `getReports` (6-month user growth, MTD-vs-prior-month booking stats, top pujas, popular wellness/astrology services, and state-level geographic distribution). It depends on the internal `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js`, the email helpers in `../lib/email.js` (backed by Resend, no-op without `RESEND_API_KEY`), and the `BookingStatus` enum from `@prisma/client`. Notable gotchas: the `status` filter in `UserFilters` is deliberately ignored because `User` has no status column (applying it would 500 every request), and `Commission.bookingId` is nullable since a commission may instead reference a store order via `storeOrderId`. Error handling is intentionally inconsistent by design evolution — `getUsers` and `getDashboard` were converted from silent mock-data fallbacks to fail-loud rethrows so operators see real DB errors, while `getRevenue` still returns hardcoded mock revenue and `updateUser` still swallows errors into a "User updated (mock)" response. Approval emails and profile-upsert failures are wrapped so they never roll back the underlying role or approval change, and dashboard `totalRevenue` is a true month-to-date aggregate rather than the older misleading sum of the last 10 transactions.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\ai.service.ts.summary: This file is the AI service layer for the Darshya platform, exporting the `AiService` class (and singleton `aiService`) that powers the "Pandit Ji" spiritual chatbot, puja recommendations, sankalp generation, content personalization, and translation. Its `chat` method implements RAG by calling `findRelevantVerses` from `../lib/scripture-data.js` to inject up to five scripture citations into the `PANDIT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, then streams a response via `streamChat` from `../integrations/claude.js` and returns a `saveConversation` callback so the route handler can persist the exchange after SSE streaming completes. `recommendPujas` combines rule-based logic from `../lib/astro-mappings.js` (`getComprehensiveRecommendation`, `RASHI_MAP`, `NAKSHATRA_DEITY_MAP`) with a Claude-generated explanation, while `generateSankalp` prompts for strict four-key JSON and `personalizeContent` is purely rule-based, bucketing the day into periods like Brahma Muhurta and optionally enriching with the user's rashi/nakshatra via `getRecommendedDeity`. `translate` uses the cheaper `MODELS.HAIKU` (versus `MODELS.SONNET` for chat and sankalp) and caches results in the `aiTranslationCache` Prisma table keyed by a sha256 `contentHash`, with fire-and-forget cache writes. Persistence goes through the shared `prisma` client (`../lib/prisma.js`) against `aiConversation` and `user` models. A key gotcha is the deliberate DB bypass: in `DEMO_MODE`, when `DATABASE_URL` is unset, or for synthetic user ids prefixed `demo-`/`anon-` (which would violate Prisma's UUID column), chat still works but conversations are never saved. Another notable defensive measure is the sankalp JSON parser, which extracts the first `{...}` block from prose-wrapped output and unwraps double-nested JSON attributed to Llama 3.3 quirks. The system prompts also enforce constraints worth knowing downstream: no emojis, Sanskrit terms transliterated rather than translated, and JSON-only output for sankalps.

apps\\api\\src\\routes\\yatra.ts.summary: This Fastify route module powers the "Dharmic Yatra" pilgrimage feature: it serves a hardcoded catalog of 14 yatra packages (the `YATRAS` array, e.g. Char Dham, Amarnath) and 8 travel companions (`COMPANIONS`), and persists user bookings to Postgres. The single export, `yatraRoutes(server)`, registers GET `/list`, GET `/:slug`, POST `/:slug/book`, GET `/bookings` (the latter two gated by the `authenticateUser` middleware from `../middlewares/auth.js`), and GET `/companions` with optional `language`/`availability` query filters; companion bookings live in the truncated remainder per the header comment. It depends only on Fastify and the shared `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js`, using raw `$executeRawUnsafe`/`$queryRawUnsafe` SQL rather than Prisma models. A key design decision is the memoized `ensureSchema()` helper, which lazily runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for `yatra_user_bookings` at runtime instead of a migration—an explicit fix for bookings previously lost on every Render free-tier restart when they were held in an in-memory Map. The full booking object is stored in a JSONB `payload` column alongside indexed `user_id`/`status` columns, with booking numbers minted by `makeBookingNumber()` as `BS-YYYYMMDD-random`. Notable gotchas: the catalog and pricing are static in-file data, the client-supplied `total` is trusted without server-side recomputation, validation is minimal (travelers capped at 1–12), and GET `/bookings` silently swallows database errors and returns an empty list rather than failing.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\astrologer.ser.summary: This Vitest suite verifies the two responsibilities of the `astrologer.service` module in the API app: commission splitting and online presence tracking. For commissions, it pins the constants `ASTROLOGER_PLATFORM_RATE` (0.2) and `ASTROLOGER_SHARE` (0.8)—explicitly aligned with the priest payout cut—and checks that `computeAstrologerSplit` returns `platformAmount` and `astrologerAmount` that always sum back to the input total, even for fractional amounts like 999.99, confirming the split is rounding-safe. For presence, it confirms that `getAstrologerPresence` reports unknown users as offline by default, that `setAstrologerOnline` flips the `online` flag and stamps a `lastSeenAt` heartbeat, that astrologers can toggle back offline, and that per-mode availability (`mode.chat` / `mode.call`) is tracked independently. The only dependencies are `vitest` and the service under test, with no database or cache mocks, which implies the presence state is held in-memory inside `astrologer.service`—a likely gotcha for multi-instance deployments or restarts, though the tests themselves don't enforce persistence semantics.

This service module supports Darshya's astrologer portal with three concerns: commission splitting, online presence tracking, and consult notifications. It exports the constants ASTROLOGER_PLATFORM_RATE (0.2) and ASTROLOGER_SHARE (0.8) — a deliberately supply-competitive 20% take versus incumbents' 45–55% — plus computeAstrologerSplit for paise-rounded fee division, setAstrologerOnline/getAstrologerPresence for presence with per-mode (chat/call) flags, and astrologerContact, notifyAstrologerNewConsult, and notifyDevoteeConsultConfirmed for messaging. It depends on the shared prisma client from lib/prisma.js and notifyUser from routes/notifications.js; note that notifyDevotee is imported from booking-notify.service.js but never actually used, making it a dead import. Two design gotchas stand out: presence lives in an in-memory Map keyed by userId (with a 15-minute ONLINE_FRESH_MS heartbeat decay) because AstrologerProfile lacks an isOnline column, so online state is lost on restart and breaks under multi-instance deployment; and astrologerContact resolves a profile by UUID (id or userId) or displayName, then queries User separately for phone since AstrologerProfile has no direct User relation. All notification helpers are fire-and-forget, swallowing errors so a failed ping can never break the booking flow.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\astrology.serv.summary: This Vitest suite (`astrology.service.test.ts`) unit-tests the singleton `astrologyService` from the sibling module `astrology.service.js`, exercising its full public API: `getAstrologers` (pagination, case-insensitive specialization and language filters, `priceRange` strings like "20-40", rating/price sorting, `isOnline`), `getAstrologerById`, `getAstrologerByIdOrSlug`, `getSpecializations`, `startConsultation`, `getKundli`, `getDailyHoroscope`, `getAllHoroscopes`, and `getCompatibility`. The tests reveal that the service currently runs on in-memory fixture data rather than a database, with hard-coded fixture IDs like `astro_001` (available), `astro_003` (busy), and `astro_005` (offline) driving the consultation error-path expectations. A notable forward-compatibility decision is captured in the `getAstrologerByIdOrSlug` block (tagged R-Q1-E-010): well-formed UUIDs deliberately resolve to null (future 404) instead of throwing until a DB-backed Astrologer table ships, and empty input returns null. Behavioral contracts pinned by the suite include 5 free minutes on new consultations, sessions starting in `waiting` status with IDs prefixed `session_`, kundli output of exactly 9 planetary positions and 12 houses, horoscope lookup accepting both Hindi Devanagari and English rashi names, and compatibility scores bounded 0–98 with deterministic output for identical inputs.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\booking-notify.summary: This service sends WhatsApp and push notifications for every stage of the puja booking lifecycle, existing because push notifications are unreliable in India (battery savers kill them) while WhatsApp is the channel devotees actually read — previously the booking flow only used web-push and never touched WhatsApp. Its core exports are the `BookingCtx` context interface, the `BookingEvent` union type (covering `confirmed`, `assigned`, `offer`, `offer_timeout`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `video_ready`, `cancelled`, `refund`, `eta`, and more), and the notifier functions `notifyDevotee` and `notifyPriest`, which send both a push via `notifyUser` (imported from `../routes/notifications.js`) and a WhatsApp template message via `sendWhatsappTemplate` from `../lib/whatsapp.js`. `sendOfferToPriest` handles the instant-dispatch case with a free-text `sendWhatsappText` message containing a one-tap accept deep-link, while `buildBookingCtx` and `priestContact` (which queries `prisma.priest` for userId and phone) are helpers that assemble notification payloads from booking records. It depends internally on the whatsapp lib, the notifications route module, and the Prisma client, and externally on Meta's WhatsApp Business API. The design is strictly best-effort and fire-and-forget: every public function swallows its own errors and logs rather than throwing, so a WhatsApp failure can never break the booking flow. Template names in the `TEMPLATE` map are conventions that must be created and pre-approved in WhatsApp Manager before going live (Meta requires approved templates outside the 24-hour window), and if the `WHATSAPP_*` env vars are unset the underlying lib returns `{skipped:true}`, making all of this a safe no-op in dev and demo environments.

apps\\api\\src\\server.ts.summary: This file is the API entry point: it runs `initSentry()` before any other import so module-load errors are captured, triggers boot-time env validation via `./lib/env.js` (fail-fast on missing `JWT_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGIN`), then builds the Fastify server in `bootstrap()`, which first calls `ensureSchemaInvariants` to replay non-idempotent migrations before registering roughly ninety route modules (`authRoutes`, `bookingRoutes`, `paymentRoutes`, `gaushalaPortalRoutes`, `voicePanditRoutes`, `marketplaceV2Routes`, etc.) under `/api/v1` prefixes. Security hardening layers `@fastify/helmet` with a strict JSON-only CSP (`defaultSrc 'none'`), `@fastify/cookie` backing the httpOnly `darshya_session` auth cookie, CORS that throws at startup if `CORS_ORIGIN` is unset in production, and `@fastify/rate-limit` with a global per-user/per-IP `keyGenerator` plus an `onRoute` override hook that tightens limits for `/auth`, `/ai/*`, `/astrology/ask`, and order-creation endpoints — the hook must be registered before the rate-limit plugin, a noted prior bug where post-registration made it a no-op. `fastify-raw-body` is registered with `global: false` so only opt-in routes (Razorpay webhooks needing signature verification against raw bytes) buffer raw bodies, avoiding double-buffering every request. Observability is deliberately infra-free: `/health` is a cheap liveness probe exempted from rate limiting via `allowList`, while `/ready` actually probes Postgres with `prisma.$queryRaw\`SELECT 1\`` and Redis through a dynamically imported `ioredis` connection (returning 503 on failure), and also reports queue degradation via `isJobQueueAvailable` from `services/job-queue.service`. An `onRequest`/`onResponse` hook pair feeds in-memory p50/p95/p99 latency stats through `recordLatency` from `lib/route-metrics`, exposed at `/api/v1/admin/metrics/latency` behind `authenticateUser` and `requireRole('admin')`, while `instrumentPrisma` and `registerNPlusOneRequestScope` add slow-query logging and AsyncLocalStorage-based N+1 detection. Auth plumbing (`registerAuthDecorators`, `authenticateUser`, `requireRole`) comes from `middlewares/auth`, and one documented gotcha is that `cron.ts` also declares a `/health` route but under the `/api/v1/cron` prefix, so no root-level duplicate exists.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\cancellation.s.summary: This Vitest test file validates the pure-function refund math in `CancellationService` (from `cancellation.service.js`), deliberately leaving DB-touching methods like `snapshotPolicy` and `panditCancel` to integration tests elsewhere. It exercises `computeDevoteeRefund` against `DEFAULT_CANCEL_POLICY` to lock the tier boundaries of the refund ladder: 100% at or beyond 48 hours before the slot (with the 48-hour boundary inclusive), 75% for 24–48 hours, 50% for 4–24 hours, and 25% under 4 hours — a policy explicitly framed as more generous than competitor SmartPuja's zero-refund window. It also covers `computePanditFaultRefund`, which returns a full refund flagged `isPanditFault` with the platform absorbing the cost, and `computeNoShowRefund`, which yields zero refund under the default policy. A final case confirms that a custom `CancelPolicy` snapshot overrides the default tiers. Notable design points are the money-math rounding check to two decimals for odd amounts, the use of a fixed `SLOT` date with a `hoursBefore` helper for deterministic time arithmetic, and the file's stated intent that these tests serve as the safety net for the financially critical parts of the cancellation engine.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\booking.servic.summary: This Vitest suite verifies `BookingService` (from `apps/api/src/services/booking.service.js`) by mocking Prisma via `prismaMock` from `lib/__mocks__/prisma.js`, covering `createBooking`, `updateBookingStatus`, `cancelBooking`, `getBookingById`, and `getUserBookings`. For `createBooking` it pins the validation order and pricing rules: the past-date guard runs before any DB call, offerings must exist, be active, and match the temple/puja IDs, slots must be in `availableSlots` and under `maxBookingsPerSlot`, NRI users get `nriPrice` in USD while domestic users get `basePrice` in INR, and the charged total adds a ₹51 platform fee plus a ₹150 prasad fee when delivery is requested (regression #PBO-3), while `platformCommission` and `priestPayout` are split 20/80 of the puja price only. For `updateBookingStatus` it enforces the state machine (e.g. `pending_payment` → `confirmed`, terminal `refunded` rejects everything), verifies the denylist that strips smuggled financial/identity fields like `priestPayout`, `priceAmount`, and `userId` from status PATCH payloads (#pp-01), and confirms a `PriestPayout` row is minted only on `video_uploaded`/`delivered` transitions, not on `completed` (#pp-02). `cancelBooking` tests cover ownership authorization, the 24-hour cutoff for `confirmed` bookings (waived for `pending_payment`), and the `requiresRefund`/`capturedPaymentId` signal when a payment exists, while `getBookingById` tests the optional owner check and `getUserBookings` covers pagination. A notable gotcha documented in the suite: `createPriestPayout` is fire-and-forget and re-fetches the booking, so tests queue sequential `findUnique` resolutions and flush the microtask queue with `setImmediate` before asserting payout creation.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\conversation.s.summary: This Vitest test suite verifies the behavior of `ensureConversationForBooking` from `apps/api/src/services/conversation.service.ts`, which is responsible for guaranteeing a chat conversation exists for a given booking. It mocks the Prisma client via `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` (substituted for `../lib/prisma.js`) and stubs `notifyUser` from `../routes/notifications.js` using a hoisted `vi.fn()` so notification side effects can be asserted without real delivery. The tests confirm the function is idempotent — returning an existing open conversation without creating messages or notifying — and that on creation it inserts a `chatConversation` row linked to the booking, seeds a `system` chat message attributed to the provider with `bookingId` metadata, increments `devoteeUnread`, bumps `lastMessageAt`, and sends the devotee a push notification titled "Your provider is ready" linking to `/messages/{id}`. A notable design constraint surfaced by the tests is failure tolerance: if `notifyUser` rejects (e.g., FCM is down), the conversation is still returned rather than the operation failing. The suite also exercises all supported conversation `kind` variants (`puja_booking`, `astrology`, `wellness`, `store_order`, `temple`, `gaushala`) to ensure the kind is passed through to the created record.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\content.servic.summary: This Vitest suite verifies the read paths of `ContentService` (apps/api/src/services/content.service.ts) using a mocked Prisma client. It imports `prismaMock` from `lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` and registers it via `vi.mock` so the service's `contentItem` queries can be inspected without a database. The `findAll` tests pin down four behaviors: every query is forced to `where.status = 'published'` regardless of caller input, free-text search is lowercased before being matched against the `tags` array with Prisma's `has` operator, the `isPremium` flag is passed through as an exact boolean filter, and results come back in a `{ data, pagination }` envelope defaulting to page 1 and limit 20. The `search` tests confirm that an empty query short-circuits, returning an empty result set without ever touching `prisma.contentItem.findMany`. Effectively this file documents the service's public contract — published-only visibility, case-insensitive tag matching, and pagination defaults — making it a useful reference for how listing and search endpoints behave.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\astrology.serv.summary: This is the MVP backend service for the app's astrology marketplace, supplying the domain types and stub data behind astrologer discovery, consultation sessions, kundli generation, daily horoscopes, and compatibility scoring. It exports the core interfaces — `Astrologer`, `AstrologerDetail`, `Review`, `Specialization`, `ConsultationSession` (with chat/call/video modes, per-minute rates, and a `freeMinutes` allowance), `KundliResult`, `DailyHoroscope`, `CompatibilityResult`, and the `AstrologersParams` filter/sort/pagination type — while the actual exported service functions sit below the truncation point. Instead of a database, everything is hardcoded: a 15-entry `ASTROLOGERS` roster with Unsplash placeholder photos, a `REVIEWS` map synthesized by cycling 10 review templates across astrologers, a `SPECIALIZATIONS` list with manually maintained counts, and a per-rashi `RASHIS` horoscope array with Hindi/English/matra fields. Its imports — `generateText`, `MODELS`, and `DEMO_MODE` from the internal `integrations/claude` module, plus `computeVedicContext` and the `VedicContext` type from `lib/vedic-context` — indicate the unseen lower half uses Claude to generate astrological content grounded in computed Vedic chart data. Two gotchas stand out: `DailyHoroscope.date` and review dates are computed from `new Date()` at module load, so they go stale until server restart, and all ratings, consultation counts, and online/busy flags are fabricated mock data that must be replaced with real persistence before launch.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\booking.servic.summary: This file is the core lifecycle service for puja bookings: `BookingService` creates bookings, drives them through a status state machine, and handles cancellation, rescheduling, and retrieval. It builds on the shared `prisma` client from `lib/prisma.js` and collaborates with `paymentService` (for `createPriestPayout`), `notifyUser` from `routes/notifications.js` (web-push on key transitions), and `ensureConversationForBooking` from `conversation.service.js` (auto-creating a devotee–priest chat thread on `priest_assigned`); Razorpay is referenced indirectly since the checkout order is created from the computed `priceAmount`. Key exports include the `CreateBookingInput`, `UserBookingsFilters`, and `SlotAvailability` types plus fee/split constants `PLATFORM_FEE_INR` (₹51), `PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE_INR` (₹150), `DEFAULT_PRIEST_SHARE` (0.8), and `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_SHARE` (0.2). `createBooking` validates the `TemplePujaOffering`, enforces slot capacity against non-cancelled bookings, applies NRI pricing (`nriPrice`, USD currency), folds the platform and prasad fees into `priceAmount` (a P0 fix for fees that were displayed but never charged), and computes `priestPayout` and `platformCommission` on the puja price only, honoring a pinned priest's `Priest.commissionRate`. `updateBookingStatus` enforces the `VALID_TRANSITIONS` state machine, strips server-authoritative financial fields via a `FORBIDDEN_DATA_KEYS` denylist, and writes idempotent `Commission` and `TemplePayout` ledger rows (the latter at `TEMPLE_SHARE_RATE`, default 5%) when a booking is confirmed. Notable gotchas: side effects (priest payout, push, conversation creation) are fire-and-forget so failures never block a status flip; the past-date guard is duplicated in-service because cron/admin/test paths bypass route-layer Zod validation; cancellation and rescheduling both enforce a 24-hour window, and rescheduling a priest-assigned booking clears `priestId` and resets status to `confirmed` so it re-enters the assignment queue. The file is truncated, so `getBookingById` (ownership-checked detail fetch with payments, temple, puja type, and priest relations) and likely list/availability methods below it are only partially visible.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\content-draft..summary: This service implements "Layer O," an organic-outreach content seeding pipeline for darshya.online that uses an LLM to draft genuine, non-promotional Hindu devotional posts for Reddit and Quora, all of which must pass through an admin approval queue and are never auto-posted. It exports the constants `TOPIC_POOL` (a 30-topic rotation), `REDDIT_TARGETS`, and `QUORA_TOPICS`; the types `RedditPostDraft`, `QuoraAnswerDraft`, and `ContentDraftRow`; the generators `generateRedditPost` and `generateQuoraAnswer`; and the persistence functions `saveDraft`, `listDrafts`, and `updateDraftStatus`, which manage a draft lifecycle of DRAFT → APPROVED/REJECTED → POSTED. Generation goes through `generateText` with `MODELS.SONNET` from `../integrations/claude.js`, while persistence uses the shared `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js`. A notable quirk is that generation is gated on the `HAS_GROQ` check of `GROQ_API_KEY` (returning null when unset) even though the actual model call flows through the Claude integration, suggesting a copy-paste leftover or shared provider gate. The system prompts (`REDDIT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `QUORA_SYSTEM_PROMPT`) enforce strict JSON-only output, word limits, anti-marketing rules, and at most one optional organic mention of darshya.online, with `safeParseJson` tolerantly extracting the first-to-last-brace substring before parsing. Because the Prisma schema may not be migrated in every environment, all persistence uses raw SQL (`$executeRawUnsafe`/`$queryRawUnsafe`) against a `content_drafts` table that `ensureTable` lazily creates once per process (with a pgcrypto extension fallback), and every database failure is swallowed to `console.warn` so a calling cron tick can never crash.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\content.servic.summary: This file implements the content-read layer of the API: the `ContentService` class (exported as the singleton `contentService`) provides all queries against the Prisma `contentItem` model for devotional content such as aartis, mantras, chalisis, and articles. Its methods cover a paginated, filterable listing (`findAll`, driven by the `ContentListParams` interface with type/deity/language/isPremium/search filters), single-item retrieval (`findBySlug`), deterministic daily curated picks (`getDailyContent`), a contains-based search (`search`), and per-type counts (`getCategories`). It depends only on the shared Prisma client from `../lib/prisma.js` and the generated `@prisma/client` types (`Prisma.ContentItemWhereInput`, `ContentType`, `Language`), with no external services involved. A hard constraint across all methods is that only items with `status: 'published'` are visible; `findBySlug` returns null for anything else. Notable gotchas: `findBySlug` increments `viewCount` fire-and-forget (errors silently swallowed) and returns an optimistic `viewCount + 1` that may not reflect the database; `getDailyContent` rotates picks via day-of-year modulo per-type counts, which fires an extra count query per type inline within its `Promise.all` (eight queries total) and can shift results if content is added mid-day; and "search" is simple case-insensitive `contains` matching plus exact tag-array membership on the lowercased query, not true full-text search.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\cancellation.s.summary: This file is the policy engine for booking cancellation refunds, replacing an older binary cancel-with-full-refund model with a tiered, per-booking policy. Its core design decision is snapshotting: `CancellationService.snapshotPolicy` stores a `CancelPolicy` (a ladder of `CancelPolicyTier` entries plus pandit-cancel, no-show, and priest-compensation fractions) onto the booking's `cancelPolicyJson` at confirm time, so `DEFAULT_CANCEL_POLICY` can evolve (full at 48h+, 75% at 24–48h, 50% at 4–24h, 25% under 4h) without retroactively changing existing bookings, and `getPolicy` falls back to the default for legacy rows. The class exposes three pure refund calculators returning `RefundComputation`: `computeDevoteeRefund` applies the ladder to the puja price only (platform/prasad fees excluded unless the pandit is at fault), while `computePanditFaultRefund` and `computeNoShowRefund` refund the full amount paid or nothing, respectively, per the platform-bears-pandit-fault norm. `panditCancel` handles the pandit-initiated path: it validates the booking belongs to the priest and is in `confirmed`/`priest_assigned` status, then re-queues it by nulling `priestId`, stamping `cancellationReason`, and setting `offerExpiresAt` to now to force immediate re-broadcast, before notifying the devotee via `notifyDevotee`/`buildBookingCtx` from `booking-notify.service.js` with notification errors deliberately swallowed. It depends on the shared `prisma` client from `lib/prisma.js` and exports a `cancellationService` singleton. Two gotchas: tier matching uses `Array.find` on `hoursUntil >= minHoursBefore`, so tiers must stay in descending order to resolve correctly, and the comments note the ladder is market-anchored to undercut competitors like SmartPuja and Urban as a trust differentiator.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\conversation.s.summary: This file provides a single helper, `ensureConversationForBooking`, that automatically opens a chat conversation between a devotee and a provider whenever a booking reaches a state where the provider must deliver the service — for example when a puja booking moves to `priest_assigned`, or when astrology and wellness bookings are confirmed. The function is idempotent: it first looks up an existing open `chatConversation` for the (devoteeId, providerId, linkedBookingId) tuple and returns it rather than creating a duplicate. On creation it also seeds the thread with a `system`-kind `chatMessage` attributed to the provider (so it renders on the provider's side of the UI), bumps `lastMessageAt` and the `devoteeUnread` counter, and fires a best-effort push notification via `notifyUser` with a deep link to `/messages/{conversationId}`. Its dependencies are the shared Prisma client from `../lib/prisma.js` (using the `chatConversation` and `chatMessage` models) and the `notifyUser` helper exported from `../routes/notifications.js`, and it is called from `booking.service.ts` plus the astrology and wellness booking flows. Notable design choices: the `kind` field is a fixed union covering puja, astrology, wellness, temple, gaushala, and store_order conversations; notification failures are deliberately swallowed (`.catch(() => undefined)`) so messaging setup never breaks the booking flow; and the caller is responsible for supplying the human-readable `systemMessage` text, since the function contains no templating of its own.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\onboarding.ser.summary: This is the Vitest test suite for `OnboardingService` in the API app, verifying the multi-role provider onboarding flow. It mocks the Prisma client via `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` (wired in with `vi.mock`) so all database calls on models like `userRoleAssignment`, `onboardingStep`, `panditProfile`, `storeProfile`, `astrologerProfile`, `wellnessProfile`, and `templeProfile` are stubbed. The tests cover `getStepsForRole` (five onboarding steps per role — PANDIT, STORE_OWNER, ASTROLOGER, GAUSHALA_MANAGER, TEMPLE_MANAGER — and an empty list for unknown roles), `startOnboarding` (role validation, upserting a role assignment plus five step records), `getProgress` (null when no assignment or steps exist, currentStep computation, submitted=true when all steps complete), `submitForApproval` (error paths plus profile creation on success), and `upsertProviderProfile`/`getProviderProfile` (role-based routing to the correct profile table). Notable behaviors locked in by these tests: the service falls back to in-memory state when Prisma throws, the ASTROLOGER profile defaults `pricePerMinute` to 10 when omitted, and `getProviderProfile` returns null for unrecognized roles rather than throwing.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\gaushala.servi.summary: This Vitest suite verifies `GaushalaService` (imported from `./gaushala.service.js`), the API layer's cow-sanctuary domain service, exercising its read methods `getGaushalas`, `getGaushalaById`, `getCows`, `getCowById`, `getAdoptionPlans`, `getMyAdoptions`, and `getAdoptionUpdates`, plus the mutating `adoptCow`. The tests pin down key business rules: `availableCows` must be computed dynamically from the count of un-adopted cows rather than a static field, `getCows` filters by `gaushalaId` and adoption availability, and the catalog contains exactly four `AdoptionPlan`s priced in INR with exactly one flagged `popular`. For `adoptCow`, the suite asserts errors for unknown cows, unknown plans, and already-adopted cows, and confirms that a successful adoption marks the cow's `isAdopted` flag, produces a certificate containing the cow id, records `totalPaid`, sets `nextRenewalDate` to null for lifetime plans and roughly one year out for annual plans. A notable design implication is that the service holds mutable in-memory seed data (the tests rely on `vi.resetModules()` and dynamic re-import via `loadService()` to get a fresh instance per test, since adoptions persist within a service instance). The only dependency is Vitest itself (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi`); no mocks, database, or HTTP layer are involved, confirming the service is currently a self-contained stub rather than a repository-backed implementation.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\onboarding.pan.summary: This Vitest regression suite verifies that `OnboardingService.upsertProviderProfile` in `apps/api/src/services/onboarding.service.ts` mirrors a `Priest` row whenever a `PANDIT` provider profile is created, fixing a P1 audit bug where pandit signups only produced a `panditProfile` record. The bug mattered because every priest-route guard resolves identity via `getPriestId()` calling `prisma.priest.findUnique({ where: { userId } })`, so missing `Priest` rows left new pandits unable to reach the dashboard, accept bookings, or receive payouts. Tests cover the display-name fallback chain — explicit `displayName` wins, then `user.fullName`, then the literal `"Pandit"` — plus field mapping (`specialties`→`specializations`, `experience`→`experienceYears`) and a guard that non-PANDIT roles like `STORE_OWNER` never touch `prisma.priest`. The suite mocks Prisma via `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` with a `vi.mock` on `../lib/prisma.js`, and reloads the service per test through `vi.resetModules()` and dynamic import to keep module state isolated. A notable convention is the upsert-based mirror keyed on `userId`, meaning repeated onboarding calls update rather than duplicate the `Priest` row.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\job-queue.serv.summary: This Vitest suite unit-tests `job-queue.service.ts` in its degraded "noop" mode, deliberately deleting `process.env.REDIS_URL` and setting `JOB_QUEUE_DISABLED='true'` before the module is loaded via top-level await import, since the service reads its configuration at import time. It verifies that `enqueue` never throws and returns synthetic results (`noop: true`, a `noop-`-prefixed `jobId`, and the originating queue name) across the four canonical queues `email`, `whatsapp`, `payout`, and `notification`, and that `getQueueHealth` reports all four queues as disabled with undefined job counts. It also exercises internals exposed through the `__INTERNAL` escape hatch: `parseRedisUrl` is checked for `rediss://` TLS detection, port and host extraction, URL-encoded password decoding, and a fallback to `127.0.0.1:6379` on unparseable input, while the `QUEUE_DISABLED` flag is asserted true under the env override. The only external dependency is `vitest`; the suite intentionally avoids real Redis/BullMQ connections by design, closing with `closeAllQueues()` in `afterAll` as a safety net. A notable gotcha documented in a comment is that re-importing the module is expensive, so the suite relies on a single suite-wide noop mode rather than per-test env resets.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\dispatch.servi.summary: This file is the booking dispatch engine for the 2026 booking revamp, replacing the old passive priest-assignment flow with a tiered broadcast model (instant, one_hour, senior tiers configured in `TIER_CONFIG`, with a fourth "scheduled" tier deliberately left as self-pick and untouched here). It exports the `DispatchService` class and a singleton `dispatchService`, whose methods cover the full offer lifecycle: `selectCandidates` (ranked priest pool using haversine geo-filtering within `serviceRadiusKm`, on-duty freshness, acceptance rate, and rating), `broadcast` (writes `DispatchOffer` rows, sets `offerExpiresAt`, fires WhatsApp/push accept links), `accept` (transactional first-priest-wins assignment that supersedes sibling offers and transitions the booking to `priest_assigned`), `decline`, `updateAcceptanceRate` (rolling rate over the last 100 resolved offers, with superseded offers excluded as neutral), and `sweepExpiredOffers` (a cron entry point that expires stale offers, rebroadcasts within bounded `maxRounds`, then escalates to admin with a devotee re-match/refund notification). It builds on the shared `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js` and delegates all messaging to `booking-notify.service.js` helpers (`notifyDevotee`, `sendOfferToPriest`, `buildBookingCtx`, `priestContact`), treating notifications as fire-and-forget so they never block transactions. Notable design choices include over-fetching candidates 3x before geo-filtering in memory, falling back to city matching when coordinates are missing, and reusing the double-booking guard semantics from `priest.service` inside the accept transaction. Gotchas worth flagging: `ACCEPTANCE_FLOOR` (0.85) is declared as an anchor but never actually enforced anywhere, the sweep's escalation-notification condition references the cumulative `escalated` counter rather than a per-booking flag so its firing logic is looser than the comment implies, and the sweep clears `offerExpiresAt` after escalation specifically to prevent infinite rebroadcast loops.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\panchang.servi.summary: This is the Vitest test suite for PanchangService, verifying the service's tiered data strategy for Hindu calendar (panchang) lookups. It mocks the Prisma client via prismaMock from lib/__mocks__/prisma.js (with vi.mock intercepting lib/prisma.js) so all DailyPanchang table interactions are stubbed. The suites cover getToday (exact DB hit, fallback to the closest row within a 7-day window with a "most recent" note, and dynamic computation flagged with computed: true when the DB is empty or stale), getByDate (null on invalid input, DB match, computed fallback), getUpcomingFestivals (merging DB rows with a hardcoded FESTIVALS_DB, deduping by date-plus-festival key, sorted output), getUpcomingVrats (combining DB vrats with computed Ekadashi/Purnima observances), and getRange (empty array on bad dates, gap-filling partial DB coverage with computed entries in ascending order). A notable convention is the computed flag used throughout to distinguish dynamically calculated results from persisted rows, and tests assert result shapes rather than exact astronomical values since real computation is exercised against live logic.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\job-queue.serv.summary: This file is the API's background job dispatch layer, wrapping BullMQ queues backed by Upstash Redis for four named lanes — `email`, `whatsapp`, `payout`, and `notification` (the `JobQueueName` union type) — while the actual consumer worker lives separately in `apps/api/src/workers/job-worker.ts`. Its central design decision is an env-or-noop pattern: when `REDIS_URL` is unset (or `JOB_QUEUE_DISABLED=true`), `enqueue()` returns a synthetic `noop-*` job id and logs once rather than throwing, so request paths survive local dev and CI; when configured, BullMQ `Queue` instances are built lazily via dynamic import, cached per name in `queueCache`, and given default retry (3 attempts, exponential backoff) and retention options. The critical gotcha is that payouts must never use `enqueue()` — `enqueuePayout()` throws loudly when the queue is unavailable so a priest payout is never silently dropped, whereas other queues emit a structured `queueNoop` JSON console event via `emitQueueNoopEvent` for observability. Supporting exports include `isJobQueueAvailable()` (a cheap flag consumed by the `/ready` endpoint to report `queue: 'ok' | 'degraded'`), `getQueueHealth()` (per-queue job counts for the `/api/v1/admin/ops` dashboard), `closeAllQueues()` for graceful shutdown, and an `__INTERNAL` escape hatch exposing `parseRedisUrl` and the disabled flag for consumers building their own BullMQ `Worker`. Dependencies are bullmq (dynamically imported to avoid paying the ioredis cost on noop paths) and an Upstash Redis connection parsed from `REDIS_URL`, with `parseRedisUrl` handling `rediss://` TLS and credential extraction. Capacity constraint: the code assumes the Upstash free tier (10k commands/day, 256 MB) is sufficient for baseline email/WhatsApp/payout volume, per `docs/free-tier-budgets.md`.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\onboarding.ser.summary: This file implements `OnboardingService` (exported as the `onboardingService` singleton), which runs the multi-step signup flow for the six provider `RoleType`s (PANDIT, STORE_OWNER, ASTROLOGER, WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR, GAUSHALA_MANAGER, TEMPLE_MANAGER) using the fixed five-step sequences defined in `ROLE_STEPS`. It persists per-step progress through Prisma (`../lib/prisma.js`) via the `userRoleAssignment` and `onboardingStep` models, with `startOnboarding`, `getProgress`, `completeStep`, and `submitForApproval` covering the stepwise flow, and it resolves a user's role by querying their most recent non-DEVOTEE `userRoleAssignment`. The private `createProviderProfile` switch upserts the role-specific profile row (`panditProfile`, `storeProfile`, `astrologerProfile`, `wellnessProfile`, `gaushalaProfile`, `templeProfile`), and for PANDIT it additionally mirrors into the `Priest` table so `getPriestId()` in the priest routes and payout code resolves instead of throwing "Priest account not found". `upsertProviderProfile` provides the idempotent single-shot signup path used by `/auth/signup`, while `approveProviderProfile` flips `approved=true` (plus `approvedAt` only on `PanditProfile`, the sole model with that field) for the lead-CONVERTED path (PBO-6) without the role re-seed or approval-email side effects of `AdminService.updateUser`. New profiles default to `approved=false` via schema defaults so they surface in `/admin/approvals`, and re-posting overwrites editable fields without resetting approval state. A notable gotcha is that nearly every method wraps its Prisma calls in a catch-all that silently falls back to an in-memory `mockOnboarding` Map (or a "demo" success response in `submitForApproval`), which keeps the API working without a database but also swallows real errors and produces state that dies with the process.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\gaushala.servi.summary: This file is the in-memory data service for the API's gaushala (cow shelter) and cow-adoption domain: it defines the core domain types and seeds them with hardcoded fixture data rather than querying a database. It exports the interfaces `Gaushala`, `Cow`, `MonthlyUpdate`, `AdoptionPlan`, and `Adoption`, which model shelters, individually adoptable cows, per-cow monthly photo updates, subscription-style adoption plans (typed as `daily_feeding`, `monthly`, `annual`, or `lifetime`), and a user's adoption record linking a user, cow, and plan with status and renewal tracking. Below the types it declares two large static arrays, `GAUSHALAS` (five verified Indian shelters such as Shri Krishna Gaushala and Pathmeda Gauseva Sansthan, with coordinates, facilities, and contact details) and `COWS` (roughly fifteen cows denormalized with `gaushalaId`/`gaushalaName`, health status enums like `healthy`/`under_treatment`/`senior_care`, adoption state, and embedded `monthlyUpdates`). The module has no external dependencies or imports visible — no ORM, HTTP client, or database — so all data is static and resets on every restart, which is the key gotcha for anyone expecting persistence. Images are hotlinked Unsplash URLs rather than hosted assets, and some fields are presentation-ready (e.g. `AdoptionPlan.nameHindi`, `priceLabel`, `popular`), showing the data is tailored to feed a UI directly. Breed-conservation and panchagavya details baked into descriptions indicate this doubles as demo/seed content for a cow-adoption product. Callers downstream should treat these arrays as read-only mock state unless mutation helpers are defined further down the file.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payment.demo-f.summary: This Vitest file is a regression lock for production-safety incident "P0 #7": it verifies that the API's demo payment proxies (synthetic `order_demo_*` Razorpay orders and stubbed Stripe `paymentIntents`) can never silently activate in production, where they would mark bookings paid without real money moving. It tests two units under varying environment configurations: `payment.service.js`, which must throw at module load when `NODE_ENV=production` and `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID` is missing or set to the `rzp_test_demo` placeholder, and `getStripe()` from `../lib/stripe.js`, which must reject when `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is absent in production. Both modules must also load cleanly when given real credentials, when running in development, or when the `ALLOW_DEMO_PAYMENTS=true` escape hatch is set for staging environments that pin `NODE_ENV=production` for parity. The suite mocks Prisma via `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` and uses dynamic `import()` with `vi.resetModules()` plus careful `process.env` save/restore, since the Razorpay guard fires at module-load time rather than at call time. A notable gotcha the tests encode is that the only symptom of the original bug was demo order ids appearing in the database weeks later, which is why the mitigation deliberately crashes the server at boot instead of logging a warning.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payment.servic.summary: This Vitest suite unit-tests `PaymentService` from `payment.service.js`, focusing on Razorpay payment verification, webhook signature handling, and the priest-payout gating rules. It has no exports of its own; the tested surface covers `verifyPayment` (validates the HMAC signature, marks the `payment` record captured and confirms a `pending_payment` booking, while skipping re-confirmation of already-confirmed bookings), `handleWebhookRaw` (verifies the signature against the raw body with a timing-safe length check, then dispatches events), `handleWebhook` (a legacy path that re-serialises the payload with `JSON.stringify` before verification), and `createPriestPayout` (refuses payouts unless the booking is in `video_uploaded` or `delivered` status and the priest has `aadhaarVerified` set). Dependencies are `vitest`, `node:crypto` for computing expected HMAC-SHA256 hex signatures, and `prismaMock` from `lib/__mocks__/prisma.js`, which replaces the real `lib/prisma.js` client so all `payment`, `pujaBooking`, `priest`, and `priestPayout` queries are mocked. A notable mechanic is the `loadService` helper, which calls `vi.resetModules()` and dynamically re-imports the service so that env vars (`RAZORPAY_KEY_ID`, `RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET`, `RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) set in `beforeEach` take effect, relying on the fact that setting the key to `rzp_test_demo` forces the service onto its demo proxy rather than a live Razorpay client. The payout tests double as a regression lock for business rule "no video proof → no priest payout," explicitly enumerating every disallowed booking status including the dangerous `completed` case, plus checks for missing priest records and unverified Aadhaar.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payout.service.summary: This Vitest test suite verifies the behavior of the payout.service module by mocking its Prisma data layer and notification dependency. It covers the exported functions getPayoutBalance, getKycStatus, requestPayout, and processPayout, testing that balances correctly partition commissions into available, pending (in-flight), and paid-out amounts; that KYC gating rejects payout requests lacking bank details, verification, or withdrawable balance; and that processPayout marks commissions PAID on completion, releases them back to PENDING on rejection, and is idempotent for already-completed payouts. Key dependencies mocked via vi.mock are the internal ../lib/prisma.js client (including commission, payoutRequest, and user models plus $queryRawUnsafe and $transaction) and the notifyUser function from ../routes/notifications.js. Notable design choices include using vi.hoisted to define the prismaMock before module import, mocking $transaction to invoke its callback with a partial client, and reading KYC status via raw SQL against a provider_kyc table rather than a Prisma model, indicating KYC data lives outside the Prisma schema.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\outreach.servi.summary: This file is the outreach engine for the Darshya API: it sends cold first-touch and follow-up messages to scraped leads over email and WhatsApp, and persists every attempt to the `OutreachLog` table for audit and dedup. Its main exports are `sendEmail` (which renders an HTML template, injects click-tracking link rewrites plus a 1×1 open pixel keyed by a `logId`, and sends via the Resend SDK), `sendWhatsApp` (which posts a plain-text message to the Meta Graph API at `graph.facebook.com`), `recordOutreach` and `incrementContactCount` (Prisma helpers that log the send and bump `Lead.contactCount`/`lastContactedAt`), `firstTouchTemplateKey`/`followupTemplateKey` (which map lead roles — TEMPLE, PRIEST, ASTROLOGER, WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR, GAUSHALA — to template names for day-3/7/14 follow-ups), and the `outreachConfig` capability summary. It depends on the internal `prisma` client from `../lib/prisma.js`, `@prisma/client` types (`Lead`, `OutreachChannel`, `OutreachStatus`), the external `resend` package, and the WhatsApp Cloud API, plus filesystem templates loaded (and cached in a `Map`) from `../templates/outreach`. Notable design choices include graceful degradation — missing `RESEND_API_KEY` or `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`/`WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID` returns `{skipped: true}` rather than throwing — bilingual Hindi-first template resolution with English fallback (`<key>.<lang>.html` → `<key>.html` → `<key>.en.html`), and hardcoded bilingual subject lines in the `SUBJECTS` map. Compliance is a deliberate concern: unsubscribe links are exempted from click-tracking wrapping, every email carries `List-Unsubscribe` one-click headers, and the footer cites IT Rules 2021/CAN-SPAM/CASL. Gotchas worth flagging: `normalisePhone` assumes Indian numbers (prepends 91 to 10-digit inputs), WhatsApp bodies are truncated at 1000 characters, tracking is only injected when the caller pre-creates an `OutreachLog` id and passes it as `logId`, and `recordOutreach` accepts a caller-supplied id precisely so tracking URLs can reference the row before it exists.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\panchang.servi.summary: This service dynamically computes a complete Hindu panchang (daily almanac) for any date and city, producing tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana, Rahu Kaal, sunrise/sunset times, festivals, and vrat observances. Its main export is `computePanchang(date, city)`, which derives the four lunar limbs from sidereal longitudes using shared astronomy helpers (`julianDay`, `moonLongitudeSidereal`, `sunLongitudeSidereal`, `nakshatraFromLongitude`) from `../lib/muhurat.js`, and it also imports `prisma` and the `cached`/`CACHE_TTL` wrappers from `../lib/cache.js` for persistence/caching in the truncated portion. The math follows the Lahiri ayanamsa and drikpanchang conventions, and notably evaluates longitudes at IST sunrise (00:30 UTC via `jdAtIstSunrise`) rather than midnight so the limbs reflect the day's prevailing values. Karana handling encodes the drikpanchang rule where the four fixed karanas (Kimstughna, Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga) occupy positions 0, 57, 58, 59 while the seven movable karanas cycle through the rest. Rahu Kaal is computed properly by splitting the sunrise-to-sunset span into eight segments indexed by weekday (`RAHU_KAAL_SEGMENT`), though a legacy static `RAHU_KAAL_BY_DAY` table remains in the file. Key constraints: sunrise/sunset come from an approximate static `CITY_TIMES` table covering only ten cities with a case-insensitive lookup that silently falls back to Delhi, and festivals come from a hardcoded `FESTIVALS_DB` covering only 2025–2026, so dates outside that range or cities outside the list yield degraded results. Vrat rules are heuristic, triggered by tithi name matches (Ekadashi, Purnima, Amavasya, Krishna Chaturthi) plus weekday-based deity notes appended for Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payout.service.summary: This file implements a unified payout engine that generalizes what was previously a priest-only payout path (PriestPayout) to all provider roles — astrologers, wellness instructors, store owners, temple managers, and gaushala managers — via the exported ProviderRoleKey union type. Its core design treats the Prisma Commission ledger as the source of truth: a provider's withdrawable balance is the sum of PENDING commissions with no payoutRequestId, and money movement flows through a PayoutRequest lifecycle rather than direct transfers. The key exports are getPayoutBalance (computes available/in-flight/paid-out totals), getKycStatus (raw SQL check against the provider_kyc table for verified bank details), requestPayout (KYC-gated, atomically creates a PayoutRequest and links the underlying commissions in one transaction to prevent double-spends), processPayout (admin action that either marks commissions PAID with a transfer reference or releases them back to PENDING on reject/fail, idempotent on completed requests), plus listMyPayouts and listPayoutRequests for provider and admin views. Dependencies are minimal: the shared prisma client from ../lib/prisma.js and notifyUser from ../routes/notifications.js for fire-and-forget status notifications. Notable constraints: Commission.amount already represents the provider's net 80% share (percentage stores the platform rate), actual settlement is external — Razorpay Route, UPI, or manual bank transfer — with only the reference string recorded for reconciliation, targeting a weekly T+7 batch cadence. One gotcha: getKycStatus's hasUpi flag is identical to hasBank since both read the same bank account record, and requests always sweep the full available balance rather than a chosen amount.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\provider.servi.summary: This Vitest test file verifies ProviderService from apps/api/src/services/provider.service.ts, mocking the Prisma client via prismaMock from lib/__mocks__/prisma.js so every suite runs without a real database. It covers ProviderService.getProviders, asserting that queries for pandit, astrologer, and gaushala route to the correct Prisma models (panditProfile, astrologerProfile, gaushalaProfile) with the right where clauses — approved-only gating, case-insensitive city contains, minRating gte, specialty has-filter, pagination skip/take math, and per-type sort defaults like totalCows desc for gaushalas. A central design decision under test is the mock fallback: when Prisma throws, the service silently degrades to in-memory mock providers and mockReviews, still applying city and rating filters, which means the public API keeps working during DB outages but may serve stale demo data. The getProviderById tests encode two security invariants flagged in comments as P0 tickets PUB-07 and PUB-01: unapproved providers must return null (so the route 404s), and PII fields (userId, gstNumber, commission, aadhaarVerified) must be stripped from public responses, with reviews attached via prisma review.findMany keyed by providerType. The addReview tests confirm reviews are created through prisma review.create with a "Review submitted" message and fall back to a demo-flagged in-memory store on failure, while updateProvider tests verify ownership enforcement — the mock fallback returns null when the caller's userId doesn't match the profile owner and merges updates only when it does. One gotcha documented inline: updateProviderProfile calls findUnique before update, so tests must seed findUnique with a matching userId or the DB path returns null before the fallback can trigger.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\priest.service.summary: This file implements `PriestService` (exported as the `priestService` singleton along with the filter/input types `PriestBookingsFilters`, `PayoutFilters`, and `UpdatePriestProfileInput`), which backs the priest-facing side of the puja booking platform: dashboard summaries, assigned-booking lists, the booking lifecycle, payout history, and profile management. It builds directly on the Prisma client from `lib/prisma.js` (querying `priest`, `pujaBooking`, and `priestPayout` models), delegates status transitions and video-proof uploads to `BookingService`, and sends devotee notifications via `notifyUser` from `routes/notifications.js` plus `notifyDevotee`/`buildBookingCtx` from `booking-notify.service.js`. `getDashboard` runs parallel aggregate queries to compute total/monthly/pending earnings and booking counts, while `getAssignedBookings` and `getPayoutHistory` provide paginated, filterable lists. The core lifecycle methods are `acceptBooking` and `rejectBooking`: accept moves a `confirmed` booking to `priest_assigned`, and reject releases it back to `confirmed` with `priestId` cleared so it re-enters the assignment queue. A notable gotcha is the double-booking guard — one active booking per priest per (scheduledDate, scheduledTimeSlot) — which is enforced only in application code inside `acceptBooking`, not by a database constraint, so any future assignment path must route through the same check. `startPuja` and `completePuja` merely verify priest ownership before delegating to `BookingService.updateBookingStatus`. All notifications are fire-and-forget (voided promises with swallowed catches) so a push/WhatsApp failure can never fail an accept or reject. Completed-state bookkeeping consistently treats `completed`, `video_uploaded`, and `delivered` as the "done" bucket across dashboard and profile stats.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payment.store-.summary: This Vitest suite covers the store-order payment flows of `PaymentService` from `./payment.service.js`, exercising two methods: `createStoreOrderRazorpay` (initiating a Razorpay checkout for a store order) and `verifyStoreOrderPayment` (confirming payment after checkout). It relies on `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` injected via a module mock of `../lib/prisma.js`, and also mocks `generateInvoice` from `../lib/pdf-invoice.js` and `sendEmail` from `../lib/email.js` because those perform real PDF and SMTP side effects; `node:crypto` is used to compute genuine HMAC-SHA256 signatures for the live-mode tests. The creation tests verify ownership enforcement (forged `:id` guard), the PENDING-status precondition, idempotent reuse of an existing initiated `Payment` row on refresh, and INR-to-paise conversion plus linking via `storeOrder.update`. The verification tests cover HMAC signature rejection and acceptance in live mode, the demo-mode guardrails (order ids must match the `order_demo_` prefix and the `demo` signature sentinel, tagged as security fix P0 #S-05), missing payment/order lookups, the PENDING→CONFIRMED transition with a `statusHistory` append, replay safety for already-CONFIRMED orders, and the commission chain (`storeProduct` → `storeProfile` → `commission.create`). A notable gotcha the suite encodes: the service switches between demo and live behavior based on `RAZORPAY_KEY_ID`, so tests reload the module with `vi.resetModules()` and mutate `process.env` per scenario. Another documented gotcha: invoice emailing is fire-and-forget (`void`), so the test flushes the microtask queue with `setImmediate` before asserting `sendEmailMock` was called — this guards against a prior bug where an unmocked `storeOrder.findUnique` threw a TypeError that was silently swallowed by the invoice path's try/catch, leaving it with zero real coverage.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\priest.service.summary: This Vitest suite unit-tests `PriestService` (from `./priest.service.js`) in isolation, verifying the priest-facing booking lifecycle and account queries without a real database. It stubs persistence via `prismaMock` from `../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js` (wired in with `vi.mock` on `../lib/prisma.js`) and replaces `BookingService` with a hoisted mock exposing `updateBookingStatusMock` and `uploadVideoProofMock`, since `PriestService` delegates status transitions and proof uploads to that service rather than implementing them itself. The `acceptBooking` tests pin down its guard rails: rejecting missing bookings, bookings claimed by another priest, and bookings outside `confirmed`/`priest_assigned` status, plus a double-booking check that uses `pujaBooking.findFirst` to detect another non-cancelled booking for the same priest at the same `scheduledDate`/`scheduledTimeSlot` before allowing the update to `priest_assigned`. `startPuja` and `completePuja` are verified to enforce priest ownership and then delegate to `BookingService.updateBookingStatus` with `in_progress` and `completed` respectively, while `uploadVideoProof` is a pure pass-through. The `getProfile` tests confirm a flattened response merging `priest` fields with nested `user` data, a `temples` list flagged by `isPrimary`, and a `stats` object built from two `pujaBooking.count` calls (total vs completed). `updateProfile` tests assert the service builds a sparse Prisma payload containing only provided fields, including array fields like `specializations` and `languages`. Finally, `getPayoutHistory` tests cover the paginated `priestPayout` query, its optional `status` filter in the where clause, and a summary computed via `aggregate` sums — with the notable gotcha that null `_sum.amount` results must fall back to `0` and `lastPayout` to `null` when no payouts exist.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\puja.service.t.summary: This is the Vitest test suite for PujaService, the API's catalog logic for puja (ritual) types, and it exists to verify the service's query-building and pagination behavior without hitting a real database. It stubs the Prisma client by mocking ../lib/prisma.js with prismaMock from ../lib/__mocks__/prisma.js, resetting mocks in beforeEach before constructing a fresh service. The findAllTypes suite locks in the contract that queries always filter where isActive is true, default to page 1 with limit 20, translate page/limit into skip/take offsets, compute totalPages from prisma.pujaType.count, treat category as an exact match, treat deity as a case-insensitive contains, and expand a search term into an OR across name, description, and deity — all using Prisma's insensitive mode. The findBySlug suite covers the null-not-found path and the response-shaping rule that nested templeOfferings relations are flattened into a temples array exposing offeringId and priceOverride alongside temple details (id, name, slug, city, state). Beyond vitest itself, the suite's only real dependency is the shared Prisma mock module, which means the tests assert on the exact where/skip/take arguments passed to prismaMock.pujaType rather than on any live data. A practical gotcha for maintainers: these tests verify query shape, not SQL correctness, so a broken Prisma schema relation or a wrong mode value would only surface in integration tests, not here.

apps\\api\\src\\services\\payment.servic.summary: This file implements the `PaymentService` class, the central payment-processing layer of the Darshya API, responsible for creating Razorpay orders, verifying checkout signatures, capturing payments, and confirming puja bookings and store orders. `PaymentService` exposes `createRazorpayOrder` and `verifyPayment` for puja bookings plus `createStoreOrderRazorpay` (and, beyond the truncation, webhook handling and refunds per the `WebhookResult`/`RefundResult` types); `verifyPayment` does timing-safe HMAC-SHA256 signature comparison via `node:crypto`, enforces caller ownership with an ADMIN-role bypass (PBO-13), then captures the payment and confirms the booking atomically in a Prisma `$transaction` that also writes the `Commission` ledger row via `writePujaCommissionOnConfirm` (P1-12). It builds on the shared `prisma` client, the `razorpay` SDK, and lib helpers `generateInvoice` (pdf-invoice), `sendEmail`, and `getStripe`/`isStripeDemoMode`, lazily imports `WalletService`, `cancellationService`, `booking-notify.service`, and `dispatchService` for post-confirm work, and uses `findDonationByOrderId`/`finalizeDonationReceipt` from `routes/donations` as a webhook backstop since donations create no payment row. Key design rules: commission writes are idempotent (a `findFirst` guard) and use `Prisma.Decimal` arithmetic because money must never be coerced to a JS Number, while post-commit side effects — invoice emails (`sendPujaBookingInvoice`, `sendStoreOrderInvoice`), the referral reward (`tryRewardReferralForBooking`, credited through `WalletService` with an idempotency key sized by `REFERRAL_REWARD_PAISE`), cancellation-policy snapshot, devotee notification, and dispatch broadcast — are consolidated in `fireAndForgetPostConfirmSideEffects` and deliberately swallow all errors so they can never roll back a captured payment (PBO-12).
