apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\content.ts.summary: This file implements the mobile app's devotee-facing `ContentScreen`, a React Native (Expo Router) screen for browsing spiritual audio content—aartis, chalisas, mantras, and bhajans—with a segmented tab filter, a scrollable list, pull-to-refresh, and a bottom "mini player" bar. Its default export is `ContentScreen`; internally it defines the memoized `ContentItemRow` row component, the `inferContentType` helper that guesses a `ContentType` by string-matching category/title text, and the `ContentItem`/`ContentType` types. It fetches data via the `useContent` hook from `@poojly/api-client`, styled with the shared `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSize` tokens from `../../lib/theme` and icons from `@expo/vector-icons` (`Ionicons`). A notable design quirk: when the API returns no items the screen falls back to a hardcoded `contentData` array, and even when API data exists, missing fields (deity, duration, title) are backfilled from that mock list by index (`i % contentData.length`), with several `as any` casts on the API shape. The "playback" is purely presentational—`playingId` local state toggles play/pause icons and shows the mini player, whose progress bar is a static 45%-wide view, so no actual audio is played. Performance is addressed via `React.memo` on `ContentItemRow` plus a stable `useCallback` toggle handler so only the row whose `isPlaying` changed re-renders, though the inline `renderItem` callback still depends on `playingId` and is recreated whenever playback state changes.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\gurukul-ap.summary: This file defines `GurukulApplyScreen`, a React Native screen in the devotee section of the mobile app that renders an application form for admission to a gurukul program, with the target program supplied via the `programId` route parameter from `expo-router`. It submits a JSON payload (student details, optional guardian details, statement of intent, and consent flag) via a POST to `/api/v1/gurukul-applications` on the base URL provided by the internal `lib/api` module's `apiBase()`, authenticating with the bearer token from `useAuth` in `lib/auth-context`. The screen distinguishes self applicants from parents applying for a child, and conditionally requires guardian fields (name, relation, phone, optional Aadhaar last-4) whenever the student is under 18 or the applicant type is `parent`. Client-side validation blocks submission for unauthenticated users, missing name/age, statements under 20 characters, or an unchecked consent box — the consent text explicitly cites DPDP Act 2023 compliance, and a helper note promises full Aadhaar numbers are never stored. On success the form swaps to a confirmation view with a back-navigation call to action rather than redirecting elsewhere. Styling relies on the shared design tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `lib/theme`, with `Ionicons` from `@expo/vector-icons` and `SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context`. A notable gotcha is that all state is local `useState` — no draft persistence — so navigating away mid-form loses entered data, and the submit button is disabled entirely when signed out rather than prompting a login flow.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\astrology..summary: This file implements the devotee-facing **AstrologyScreen** (an expo-router route in the mobile app), which presents Vedic astrology content: a selectable 4-column grid of the twelve rashis (zodiac signs), a detail card showing the selected rashi's element, ruling planet, lucky color, and daily horoscope, a list of paid astrology services, and an "AI Jyotish Assistant" call-to-action. The default export `AstrologyScreen` is the screen component, while `RashiCard` is a small internal presentational component; the `Rashi` and `AstrologyService` interfaces type the two hardcoded datasets `rashiData` (all 12 signs with Hindi names, symbols, and date ranges) and `services` (Kundli Generation, Kundli Matching, Personal Consultation, Annual Prediction with INR pricing). Remote data comes from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package via the `useAstrologers` and `useHoroscope` hooks, which supply the "astrologers online" count and the daily prediction respectively, while styling pulls from `../../lib/theme` and icons from `@expo/vector-icons`. Navigation uses `expo-router` for in-app routing to `/(devotee)/kundli` and React Native `Linking` to open external `https://darshya.online/astrology` URLs decorated with UTM tracking parameters for non-kundli services and the AI chat CTA. Notable gotchas: rashi and service data are fully hardcoded rather than API-driven, the horoscope query is keyed off the selected rashi's lowercased English name and silently falls back to a canned prediction string when the API returns nothing, and pull-to-refresh only refetches the horoscope if a rashi is currently selected. Prices are formatted with the `en-IN` locale for Indian number grouping, and the service-card tap handler dispatches on a substring match of "kundli" in the service name, which is a fragile coupling between display text and routing logic.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\darshan.ts.summary: This file is the Live Darshan screen for the devotee-facing mobile app, rendering a browsable grid of live and scheduled temple livestream streams under the route `/(devotee)/darshan`. Its default export is the `DarshanScreen` component, supported by an internal `StreamCard` component and a local `DarshanStream` interface that normalizes both API and mock data into one shape (temple name, city, deity, status, viewers, scheduled time). It fetches real stream data via the `useDarshan` hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package, mapping `temple.name`/`temple.city`/`temple.deity`, `viewerCount`, and `scheduledStartTime` into the local interface, and uses `RefreshControl` plus `darshanQuery.refetch()` for pull-to-refresh. Navigation relies on `expo-router`: tapping a live card pushes to `/(devotee)/darshan-player` with `id` and `title` params, while scheduled streams only show an `Alert` dialog. A notable design decision is the hardcoded fallback datasets `liveStreams` and `scheduledStreams`, which are displayed whenever the API returns no streams of that category, so the UI never appears empty but may silently show stale mock content instead of an error or empty state. The grid layout computes `CARD_WIDTH` from `Dimensions.get('window')` at module load, so it won't adapt to orientation changes or window resizing. Other gotchas: the "Enable" notifications button only fires a confirmation `Alert` without requesting actual push permissions, and route paths are cast with `as any`, bypassing expo-router's typed-route checking. Styling comes from the shared `../../lib/theme` module (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) alongside `react-native-safe-area-context` and `@expo/vector-icons`.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\horoscope..summary: This file defines HoroscopeScreen, a React Native screen in the devotee section of the mobile app that displays a daily horoscope reading for a user-selected zodiac sign. It renders a hardcoded SIGNS array of twelve zodiac entries (each with English name, Hindi rashi name, Unicode symbol, and date range) as selectable chips, then fetches the reading via the useDailyHoroscope hook imported from the internal @poojly/api-client package, refetching whenever the selected sign changes or the user pull-to-refreshes. The response is loosely typed through a local HoroscopeBody interface with optional fields (prediction/general, career, love, health, luckyColor, luckyNumber), and each present field is rendered conditionally via small local Section and Chip helper components, with a fallback message when no reading exists. Navigation uses expo-router (router.back and router.push to '/(devotee)/kundli'), icons come from @expo/vector-icons Ionicons, and all styling relies on the shared design tokens from ../../lib/theme (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius). Notable points: the screen defaults to Aries rather than the user's own sign, the typed route push casts to never to bypass Expo Router's type checking, and a promotional banner cross-links to the Kundli screen.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\gurukul-de.summary: This file defines GurukulDetailScreen, an Expo Router screen in the (devotee) route group of the mobile app that renders the full profile of a single gurukul — name, verified badge, location, residential/online/minors tags, description, contact actions, and a list of offered Program cards. It reads the slug via useLocalSearchParams and fetches data from the backend with apiFetch<GurukulDetail>(`/gurukuls/{slug}`), managing loading and error states locally with useState. Its internal dependencies are the lib/api fetch wrapper and the lib/theme design tokens (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius); externally it relies on expo-router for navigation, react-native-safe-area-context for SafeAreaView, @expo/vector-icons for Ionicons, and React Native's Linking API to open mailto:, tel:, and website URLs from the contact rows. Each program card's Apply button pushes to /(devotee)/gurukul-apply?programId={id}, handing off the selected program to the application flow. The Program and GurukulDetail interfaces are local-only types mirroring the API response. Notable details: annual fees are formatted in Indian locale (₹ with en-IN grouping) but are hidden when feeAnnualInr is falsy, which also suppresses a legitimate zero fee; websiteUrl is force-unwrapped inside the Linking handler even though the row is conditionally rendered, and contact rows only render when the underlying field is non-null.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\gurukuls.t.summary: This file defines `GurukulsScreen`, the default-exported React Native screen at the `(devotee)/gurukuls` route in the Expo mobile app, which lets devotees browse and search traditional schools (gurukuls) and their admission-relevant attributes. It renders a searchable, filterable `FlatList` of `Gurukul` records (a locally declared interface with fields like `slug`, `tradition`, `isResidential`, `isOnline`, `acceptsMinors`, and `isVerified`), with chip filters for All, Residential, Online, and Accepts minors, and tapping a card routes to `/(devotee)/gurukul-detail?slug=...` via `expo-router`'s `router.push`. Data comes from the backend through the shared `apiFetch` helper in `lib/api`, hitting the `/gurukuls` endpoint with `URLSearchParams`-built query strings (`q`, `residential`, `online`, `acceptsMinors`), while styling relies on the design tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `lib/theme` plus `@expo/vector-icons` and `react-native-safe-area-context`. A notable gotcha is that the `useEffect` refetches on every change to `q` or `filter` with no debounce, so each keystroke in the search box triggers a network request. Loading, error, and empty states are all handled inline (spinner tinted `colors.saffron[600]`, inline error text, and a "No gurukuls match" placeholder), and filtering is entirely server-driven—the chips only translate to query parameters rather than filtering the fetched list client-side.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\knowledge-.summary: This file defines `KnowledgeArticleScreen`, the default-exported Expo Router screen in the `(devotee)` route group that displays a single knowledge-base article. It reads `category` and `slug` from route params via `useLocalSearchParams`, fetches the article with `apiFetch` from `../../lib/api` against the `/knowledge/{category}/{slug}` endpoint, and types the response with the local `Frontmatter` and `ArticleData` interfaces (title, summary, optional subTopic, readingMinutes, sources, and a markdown body). Rendering is handled by a hand-rolled `renderMarkdown` helper that splits the body into lines and emits styled `Text` blocks for h1–h3 headings, bullet items, blockquotes, and paragraphs — a notable limitation is that it supports no inline formatting such as bold, links, or code, and multi-line paragraphs are joined with spaces. The UI layers a back header using `router.back()` and `Ionicons`, loading and error states, and a `ScrollView` showing the frontmatter metadata plus a sources list, all styled with the shared `colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, and `borderRadius` tokens from `../../lib/theme`. One small gotcha: if `category` or `slug` is missing, the effect returns early and the screen stays on the loading spinner indefinitely.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\knowledge..summary: This file defines `KnowledgeHubScreen`, the Expo Router screen at `app/(devotee)/knowledge.tsx` that serves as the entry point to the app's Knowledge Hub for devotee users. It renders a scrollable list of navigation cards: three static `categories` (sanskrit, ved, sanatan) defined via the `CategoryCard` interface, each pushing to `/(devotee)/knowledge-category?category=<key>`, plus fixed cards routing to `/(devotee)/learn-sanskrit` and `/(devotee)/gurukuls`. The screen is gated by the `EXPO_PUBLIC_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED` environment flag — when false, it renders a "Knowledge Hub launching soon" placeholder with a construction icon instead of the card list, so the feature can ship dark. It depends on the internal `lib/theme` module for `colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, and `borderRadius` tokens, and on `expo-router` (`router.push`), `@expo/vector-icons` (`Ionicons`), and `react-native-safe-area-context` (`SafeAreaView`) externally. Notable gotchas: `GURUKUL_ENABLED` is read from the environment but never actually used, so the Gurukuls card always renders even if that feature is meant to be flagged, and the category colors include defensive fallbacks (`colors.amber[600] ?? colors.saffron[700]`), hinting that the `amber` and `green` palettes may not exist in the theme. Card accent styling is done via a left border and a tinted icon background built by appending a hex alpha suffix (`${c.color}18`) to the theme color, which assumes all theme colors are hex strings.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\knowledge-.summary: This file defines `KnowledgeCategoryScreen`, the default-exported Expo Router screen for the `(devotee)` route group at `knowledge-category.tsx`, which lists knowledge-base articles for a single category. It reads the `category` route param via `useLocalSearchParams` (defaulting to `sanskrit` and supporting `ved` and `sanatan` through a hardcoded `labels` map), fetches articles from the backend endpoint `/knowledge/{category}` using the internal `apiFetch` helper from `lib/api`, and renders loading, error, and empty states around a `FlatList` of results. Articles are grouped client-side by their optional `subTopic` field (falling back to a `General` bucket) into sections, with each row showing title, summary, and optional `readingMinutes`; tapping a row pushes to the sibling route `/(devotee)/knowledge-article` with `category` and `slug` query params. Dependencies are limited to React Native core components, `expo-router` for navigation, `react-native-safe-area-context` for the top-inset `SafeAreaView`, `@expo/vector-icons` (`Ionicons`) for chevrons, and the shared theme tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `lib/theme`. Notable details: unknown category strings fall back to displaying the raw param as the header title, grouping uses a plain `reduce` plus a nested `map` inside `FlatList` rather than `SectionList`, and there is no pull-to-refresh or pagination, so the fetch runs only when the category param changes.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\gurukul-po.summary: This file defines `GurukulPortalScreen`, the default-exported React Native screen where gurukul operators manage their institutions and review admission applications. It presents two tabs: a "Gurukuls" list showing each owned `Gurukul` with its verification badge, tradition, location, and program count, and an "Applications" list showing each `Application` (student name, age, guardian contact, personal statement) with color-coded status chips driven by the `STATUS_COLORS` map and a submitted → forwarded → accepted/rejected/withdrawn workflow. Data comes from two authenticated REST endpoints built on `apiBase()` — `GET /api/v1/gurukuls/mine/list` and `GET /api/v1/gurukul-portal/applications` — fetched in parallel with the bearer token from `useAuth()` in `lib/auth-context`, while decisions are sent via `decide()`, which PATCHes `/api/v1/gurukul-portal/applications/:id` and merges the returned application into local state. Internal dependencies are limited to `lib/auth-context`, `lib/theme` (colors, spacing, typography), and `lib/api`; external ones are `expo-router` for navigation (back, `/(onboard)/become-gurukul` registration, `/(devotee)/gurukul-detail` public pages), `react-native-safe-area-context`, and `@expo/vector-icons`. Notable design choices include gating the whole screen on `isAuthenticated` with a sign-in prompt, using a single `busyId` flag to disable action buttons while a PATCH is in flight, and hiding action buttons entirely once an application reaches a terminal status. A key gotcha is that `confirmDecide` collects accept/reject notes via `Alert.prompt`, which is iOS-only in React Native, so note entry silently won't work on Android; additionally, router paths use `as any` casts to bypass typed-route checking, and the withdrawal status exists in the type union but is never settable from this UI.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\index.tsx.summary: This file defines `HomeScreen`, the default landing page for the devotee section of the Expo/React Native mobile app, rendered at the route `/(devotee)/`. It greets the signed-in user (via `useAuth` from `lib/auth-context`), shows a search bar, quick-action shortcuts to the Kundli, Horoscope, Yatra, Weddings, and Upgrade screens, a "Today's Panchang" card, and horizontally scrollable "Live Darshan" and "Popular Pujas" sections, with pull-to-refresh refetching all data. Data comes from the shared `@poojly/api-client` hooks `useDarshan`, `usePujas`, and `usePanchang`, while navigation uses `expo-router` and styling uses the design tokens exported from `lib/theme`. A key design decision is the graceful-degradation strategy: hardcoded `FALLBACK_DARSHAN` and `FALLBACK_PUJAS` arrays (plus default panchang strings like "Dwadashi (Shukla Paksha)") are shown whenever the API is unreachable or returns empty, so the home screen never looks broken. A notable gotcha is that the `PujaType` returned by `usePujas` lacks pricing, ratings, and review counts (those live on `TemplePujaOffering`), so the component deliberately splices fallback prices and ratings onto real puja names and deities by array index. Unauthenticated users additionally see a waitlist promo card linking to `/(onboard)/waitlist`, and two small local presentational helpers, `QuickAction` and `PanchangItem`, round out the file.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\learn-sans.summary: This file defines `LearnSanskritScreen`, the React Native screen for the devotee-facing "Learn Sanskrit" feature in the Expo mobile app, which lists Sanskrit lessons grouped by difficulty level and shows the user's learning streak and earned badges. It exports a single default component and two local types (`Lesson`, `ProgressResponse`); the lesson catalog itself is a hardcoded `STATIC_CATALOG` array of three beginner lessons (Devanagari vowels/consonants, namaste etymology), while per-user completion, streak, and badge data are fetched live. It depends on internal modules `../../lib/theme` (colors/spacing tokens), `../../lib/auth-context` (`useAuth` for the session access token), and `../../lib/api` (`apiBase()`), plus `expo-router` for navigation and `@expo/vector-icons`. On mount it calls `GET {apiBase()}/api/v1/lessons` with a Bearer token, but degrades gracefully: if the user is unauthenticated or the request fails, it falls back to empty progress rather than an error state. Completed lessons are matched against the static catalog by `lessonId` and rendered with a green checkmark state, and tapping a lesson routes to `/(devotee)/lesson?id=<id>`. A notable gotcha is that the catalog is client-side static while progress is server-driven, so new lessons require an app update, and the intermediate/advanced groups currently render nothing since no such lessons exist in the catalog.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\messages.t.summary: This file defines the messages screen for the devotee section of the React Native mobile app, following Expo Router's file-based routing convention (the `(devotee)` route group means it serves the `/messages` route within that role's navigation). Its only export is the default `DevoteeMessages` component, which renders the shared `Inbox` component imported from `apps/mobile/lib/inbox` with the `role` prop set to `"devotee"`. The sole dependency is that internal `lib/inbox` module; there are no external libraries or services referenced here. Notably, the file is a deliberately thin wrapper: all messaging logic, data fetching, and UI live in the reusable `Inbox` component, with the route file responsible only for passing the role so the same inbox can presumably be reused across other user roles. Any changes to inbox behavior should be made in `lib/inbox`, not in this screen.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\kundli.tsx.summary: This file defines `KundliScreen`, the default-exported React Native screen for the Expo Router route `app/(devotee)/kundli.tsx` in the Poojly mobile app, which lets a devotee generate a free Vedic birth chart (kundli) by submitting birth date, time, place, and an optional name. The screen calls the `useGenerateKundli` mutation hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package and renders the returned `KundliResult` — summary, ascendant, moon/sun signs, nakshatra, current dasha, and a planetary positions list — via small local presentational helpers `FormField` and `ResultRow`. Dependencies include `expo-router` for back navigation, `react-native-safe-area-context` for layout, `@expo/vector-icons` (Ionicons), and the app's shared theme tokens from `../../lib/theme`. Notably, birth date and time are validated only with regexes (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `HH:MM`) rather than real date pickers, so malformed-but-pattern-matching values like month 99 would reach the API. The result is loosely typed with an `as KundliResult | null` cast and every field is optional, so rendering is defensively conditional. The footer states the chart uses the Lahiri ayanamsa and cross-promotes booking an astrologer in the Astrology tab, marking this as a lightweight lead-in feature rather than a full astrology product.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\profile.ts.summary: This file defines the devotee role's Profile tab in the Expo Router mobile app, rendering the signed-in user's identity card, account stats, and navigation menus, or a guest sign-in/create-account prompt when unauthenticated. The default-exported `ProfileScreen` pulls session state (`user`, `isAuthenticated`, `signOut`) from the internal `useAuth` hook in `lib/auth-context` and fetches live counts via `useBookings` and `useUserAddresses` from the `@poojly/api-client` package, with pull-to-refresh refetching both queries. Navigation content is data-driven through the `QuickLink` interface and the static `quickLinks`/`moreLinks` arrays rendered by the presentational `LinkRow` component, while `ONBOARD_OPTIONS` drives an expandable "List your business" section routing to provider-onboarding flows (list-temple, become-priest, become-astrologer, become-wellness, list-gaushala, become-gurukul, gurukul-portal). Styling comes entirely from the shared `lib/theme` tokens (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius), with Ionicons for iconography and SafeAreaView for layout. Notable gotchas: only bookings, messages, and consultations links actually navigate—addresses shows a count alert and everything else falls through to a "Coming Soon" alert, the static `badge: '3'` on the bookings link is dead data immediately overwritten by the real `bookingCount`, and sign-out confirms via Alert then hard-replaces the stack to `/(auth)/login`. The `getInitials` helper derives a two-letter avatar fallback defaulting to "D" for anonymous devotees.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\lesson.tsx.summary: This file is the lesson detail screen for the devotee-facing Expo mobile app, rendered at the `(devotee)/lesson` route, and it walks a user through reading a Sanskrit lesson, taking a multiple-choice quiz, and viewing a score. It exports a single default component, `LessonScreen`, which resolves the lesson via `useLocalSearchParams` against a hardcoded local `CATALOG` (three lessons on Devanagari vowels, consonants, and "namaste", typed by the `Lesson` and `QuizQ` interfaces) and drives a three-phase state machine (`read`, `quiz`, `done`) using `useState`. Internally it depends on `lib/theme` for styling tokens, `lib/auth-context`'s `useAuth` for the session token, and `lib/api`'s `apiBase()` to POST completion results to `/api/v1/lessons/complete`; externally it builds on `expo-router`, `react-native-safe-area-context`, and `@expo/vector-icons`. A key design decision is that lesson content is bundled client-side rather than fetched from the backend, so adding lessons requires an app update, and only the completion score is synced to the server. The quiz locks each answer after selection and immediately color-codes correct versus incorrect choices (green/red), with optional per-question explanations that none of the current catalog entries actually populate. A notable gotcha: `submitProgress` is invoked inside `nextQuestion` right after `setAnswers`, so the `score` it sends is computed from the stale `answers` state and omits the final question's result. Unknown lesson ids short-circuit to a plain "Lesson not found" message, and save failures surface only as an `Alert` without retry.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\store.tsx.summary: This file implements `StoreScreen`, the default-exported Expo Router screen for the devotional goods storefront at the `(devotee)/store` route in the mobile app, rendering a header with a cart button, horizontal category filter chips, and a two-column product grid with pull-to-refresh. It fetches catalog data via the `useProducts` hook from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package, but falls back to a hardcoded `productsData` array of eight items when the API returns nothing, and even when API data exists it borrows ratings, review counts, and tags from that fallback list by index. The `Product` type and `StoreCategory` union ('all', 'puja-items', 'idols', 'books', 'rudraksha', 'clothing') drive filtering, while `inferStoreCategory` maps API products to categories using keyword heuristics on the handle/title, defaulting to 'puja-items'. `ProductCard` renders each item with a discount badge computed from price/originalPrice, a category icon placeholder instead of real images, and an Add button; notably, every purchase interaction — product tap, add-to-cart, and cart icon — delegates to the web storefront by calling `Linking.openURL` against `https://darshya.online/store` URLs with UTM tracking parameters rather than implementing in-app checkout. Styling comes entirely from the shared `lib/theme` module (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius), with `Ionicons` from `@expo/vector-icons` for iconography. Gotchas include the hardcoded cart badge count of "2", `(p as any)` casts when reading price fields off API products, a synthesized originalPrice of 1.4× when missing, and grid card widths computed from `Dimensions.get('window')` at module load time.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\pujas.tsx.summary: This file implements `PujasScreen`, the "Book a Puja" browsing screen in the devotee route group of the Expo Router mobile app, rendering a category-filterable list of puja services with prices, ratings, temple locations, and feature badges (video proof, prasad delivery). The default export `PujasScreen` fetches live data via the `usePujas` hook from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package, while the memoized `PujaCard` component renders each item and routes booking taps to an external web URL (`https://darshya.online/pujas/book`, with UTM params) via React Native `Linking` rather than a native checkout. A notable hybrid-data gotcha: because the API only supplies names, deities, durations, and descriptions, API results are merged by index modulo against the hardcoded `pujasData` fallback array to borrow prices, ratings, and temples—so live pujas display arbitrary fallback pricing—and the screen falls back entirely to `pujasData` when the API returns nothing. The `inferCategory` helper assigns each puja to a `PujaCategory` (shiva, vishnu, devi, ganesh, navagraha) by substring-matching the deity name, defaulting unknowns to 'shiva', which risks misclassification. NRI pricing is derived inline by dividing the INR `nriPrice` by a hardcoded exchange rate of 83. Other dependencies include `@expo/vector-icons` (Ionicons), `react-native-safe-area-context`, and shared theme tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `../../lib/theme`; pull-to-refresh is wired to `pujasQuery.refetch()`.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\support.ts.summary: This file defines `SupportScreen`, the devotee-facing support ticket screen for the Poojly mobile app, rendered as the default export of the `(devotee)/support` route. It lists the user's existing support tickets with status pills and provides a slide-up `Modal` form for creating new ones, requiring only subject and message body before submission. Data comes from the shared `@poojly/api-client` package via the `useSupportTickets` query hook (with pull-to-refresh wired through `ticketsQuery.refetch`) and the `useCreateSupportTicket` mutation hook, which is called with `mutateAsync` inside a try/catch that surfaces errors via React Native `Alert`. Rendering is built on the shared `PortalScreen` wrapper and `EmptyHint` placeholder from `lib/portal-screen`, with all colors, spacing, and radii taken from the `lib/theme` design tokens. Status pill colors are chosen by the local `statusColor` helper, which does lowercase substring matching on the status string (e.g. "resolv", "progress") rather than strict enum comparison, so unexpected statuses fall back to a neutral stone color. A notable gotcha is that the ticket shape is a locally declared `TicketRow` interface with all-optional fields, cast from the loosely typed query response, so missing fields degrade to placeholders like "(no subject)". Another loose end: category and priority are free-text `TextInput`s with placeholder hints instead of pickers, so users can submit arbitrary values for what are presumably enumerated fields. On successful submission the form resets to defaults and the modal closes, but the list relies on the mutation's cache invalidation (or manual refresh) rather than refetching directly.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\upgrade.ts.summary: This file defines UpgradeScreen, the default-exported Expo Router screen at the (devotee)/upgrade route, which markets the "Darshya Premium" NRI annual subscription ($49/year) and initiates checkout. It pulls subscription state and the checkout mutation from the shared @poojly/api-client package via the useIsPremium and useCreateStripeAnnual hooks, and gets the current user from the local lib/auth-context useAuth hook, with styling tokens from lib/theme. When the user taps the CTA, onUpgrade calls createCheckout.mutateAsync to obtain a Stripe-hosted checkout URL and opens it externally with React Native's Linking API rather than an in-app purchase, falling back to an alert showing the raw URL if it cannot be opened. Unauthenticated users are prompted to sign in and routed to /(auth)/login, while already-premium users (premiumQuery.data?.isPremium === true) see a confirmation card directing them to manage billing on the web at darshya.online. A pull-to-refresh control re-fetches premium status, presumably so returning from the Stripe browser session reflects a completed upgrade. Notable gotchas: the price, benefits list (BENEFITS), and INR comparison are hardcoded client-side rather than driven by server pricing, and payment completion is never confirmed in-app—the screen relies on manual refresh to detect it.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\weddings-m.summary: This file defines `WeddingMuhuratScreen`, a devotee-facing Expo Router screen in the mobile app for finding auspicious Hindu wedding dates (muhurats) within a chosen date range. It collects a from-date, to-date, and optional city through plain text inputs, validates them client-side with a strict `YYYY-MM-DD` regex plus a range-ordering check, and calls the backend via the `useFindMuhurats` mutation hook and `WeddingMuhurat` type from the shared `@poojly/api-client` package. Results are rendered as cards showing each date's weekday, tithi, nakshatra, yoga, and reason, with a circular score badge colored green for `isShubh` dates and amber otherwise. The screen depends on `expo-router` for back navigation, `@expo/vector-icons` for Ionicons, `react-native-safe-area-context` for layout, and the app's internal `lib/theme` tokens (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius). Notable details: the response parsing is defensive, accepting either a bare array or an object with a `muhurats` array since the API shape may vary; errors surface as `Alert` dialogs rather than inline UI; the empty state only appears after a successful query; and a local `Field` helper component wraps label-plus-input pairs.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\temples.ts.summary: This file implements the devotee-facing "Sacred Temples" screen (`TemplesScreen`, the default export) in the Poojly mobile app, rendering a searchable, pull-to-refresh list of temple cards that either deep-link into the in-app live darshan player or open the temple's page on darshya.online via `Linking`. Data comes from the `useTemples` hook in `@poojly/api-client`, but a hardcoded `templesData` array of five famous temples serves both as an offline/empty-state fallback and as a gap-filler: when real API records exist, mock entries are blended in by modulo index to supply viewer counts, `liveDarshanEnabled` defaults, and descriptions the API may lack. The memoized `TempleCard` component renders each temple with LIVE and verified badges, a five-star rating derived from `trustScore` (computed as API `rating * 20`, rendered by the `renderStars` helper with half-star support), and Indian-locale viewer counts. Navigation uses `expo-router` to push to `/(devotee)/darshan-player` with untyped (`as any`) params when live darshan is available; otherwise it builds a UTM-tagged external URL. Search filtering is purely client-side across name, city, and deity only. Notable dependencies beyond the API client are `react-native-safe-area-context`, `@expo/vector-icons` (`Ionicons`), and the shared design tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `../../lib/theme`. The main gotcha is that the displayed list may be a hybrid of live and mock data, so fields like viewer counts and trust scores can be fabricated placeholders rather than real metrics.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\wellness.t.summary: This file implements the Wellness screen for the mobile app's devotee section (route `apps/mobile/app/(devotee)/wellness.tsx`), offering a three-tab experience covering Yoga, Meditation, and Ayurveda content. The default-exported `WellnessScreen` manages tab state and renders three internal sub-components: `YogaContent` (a daily-challenge progress card plus a horizontal carousel of session cards with live and difficulty-level badges), `MeditationContent` (quick-start duration buttons and a tappable list of guided tracks with a purely visual play/pause toggle), and `AyurvedaContent` (a dosha-quiz call-to-action and a list of wellness tips). It fetches live session data via `useWellnessSessions` from the `@poojly/api-client` package, mapping API sessions onto the local `YogaSession` type with the helper `mapWellnessLevel`, while theming comes from the app's internal `lib/theme` module and icons from `@expo/vector-icons`' `Ionicons`. A notable design decision is the heavy reliance on hardcoded fallback data: the `yogaSessions`, `meditationTracks`, and `ayurvedaTips` arrays are static mocks, and even when API data exists it is merged with mock entries for fields like `participants`, while Meditation and Ayurveda tabs never use the query at all. Gotchas include the fact that no actual audio/video playback exists (playing state is just a UI toggle, and most interactions fire placeholder `Alert` dialogs, e.g. "Quiz coming soon"), the 21-day challenge progress is hardcoded at 57%, and `isLive` is derived naively by checking whether `startTime` is in the past.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\yatra.tsx.summary: This file defines `YatraScreen`, the default-exported React Native screen at the `(devotee)/yatra` route in the Expo mobile app, which presents curated pilgrimage tours as two scrollable sections — API-driven "Packages" and a "Destinations" list — each rendered as tappable cards with duration, region, and starting price in INR. It fetches data through the `useYatraPackages` and `useYatraList` hooks from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package, supports pull-to-refresh by refetching both queries in parallel, and navigates via `expo-router`'s `router.push` to `/(devotee)/yatra-detail` passing a `slug` plus a `source` param distinguishing "package" from "destination". A notable design decision is the hardcoded `FALLBACK_DESTINATIONS` array (Char Dham, Kashi Vishwanath, Tirupati, Shirdi), which is substituted — via an `as unknown as` type cast — whenever the API yatra list returns empty, so the screen never appears bare if the backend has no data. Styling relies on shared theme tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `../../lib/theme`, with `SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context` and `Ionicons` from `@expo/vector-icons`. Gotchas include the loading spinner only showing when both queries are loading and no cached or fallback data exists, and several `as never` casts on router calls that bypass Expo Router's typed-route checking.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\weddings.t.summary: This file defines `WeddingsScreen`, the "Darshya Weddings" inquiry screen in the devotee section of the Expo mobile app, where users request wedding planning services (pandits, decor, muhurats). It renders a package picker built from the hardcoded `PACKAGES` constant (basic/premium/royal tiers, typed via `PackageTier`, defaulting to premium) plus a contact-and-details form whose fields are prefilled from the authenticated user obtained through `useAuth` from `lib/auth-context`. Submission goes through the `useCreateWeddingInquiry` mutation hook from the shared `@poojly/api-client` package, and a tappable banner routes to the sibling `/(devotee)/weddings-muhurat` Vedic date-finder screen via `expo-router`. Styling uses the internal `lib/theme` tokens (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius), and a small local `Field` component wraps label-plus-input rows. Validation is entirely client-side: regex email check, a ten-digit-minimum phone check, required name and city, and an optional date that must match YYYY-MM-DD, with failures surfaced as `Alert` dialogs. Notable gotchas: `guests` and `budget` are parsed with `parseInt` and omitted (undefined) when blank, `weddingDate` and `message` are likewise optional, the muhurat route push is cast `as never` (indicating the typed-routes config may not know that path), and success shows an alert whose Done action calls `router.back()`. The submit button reflects `inquiry.isPending` with an `ActivityIndicator` and disables re-taps while the mutation runs.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\yatra-deta.summary: This file defines `YatraDetailScreen`, an Expo Router screen in the devotee section of the mobile app that shows details for a pilgrimage (yatra) and lets the user either reserve a bookable package or request concierge planning for a curated destination. It reads `slug` and `source` route params via `useLocalSearchParams`, then branches between `useYatraPackage` and `useYatra` queries from `@poojly/api-client`, normalizing their differing shapes (e.g. `name` vs `title`, `price_inr` vs `priceFromInr`, `duration_days` vs `durationDays`) into common display fields. For packages it renders a booking form (travellers, email, phone, special requests) that validates input client-side and submits through the `useBookYatraPackage` mutation, showing the returned `bookingNumber` and `totalInr` and promising WhatsApp payment instructions; for destinations it renders a concierge card instead. Prefilled contact fields come from `useAuth` in `../../lib/auth-context`, and all styling uses the design tokens in `../../lib/theme`. Notable gotchas: `onBook` contains a WhatsApp deep link with a hardcoded placeholder number (`919999999999`), but the concierge button actually rendered for destinations ignores it and just shows an Alert, so that code path is currently dead. Traveller count is clamped to 1–20 and booking errors surface as generic alerts, while pull-to-refresh is supported via `RefreshControl` wired to the active query's `refetch`.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\dashboard.summary: This file defines the `GaushalaDashboard` React Native screen, the landing view for the cow-shelter (gaushala) portal route `app/(gaushala)/dashboard.tsx` in the Expo mobile app. Its job is to surface at-a-glance welfare and donation metrics plus a short list of recently added cows, with pull-to-refresh support. It fetches cow data through the `useCows` hook from the shared `@poojly/api-client` package (wrapping the query's `refetch` in local `refreshing` state), and renders entirely via shared primitives from `../../lib/portal-screen` (`PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, `EmptyHint`) styled with `colors` and `spacing` tokens from `../../lib/theme`. The "Total Cows" and "Adopted" stats derive from the live query—adoption is detected by a case-insensitive substring match on `c.adoptionStatus`—while the "Donations (Mo)" (`₹64,200`) and "Volunteers" (`12`) cards are fully hardcoded placeholders. A notable gotcha is the `cows.length || 42` and `adopted || 18` fallback pattern, which silently substitutes dummy numbers when real counts are zero, masking genuinely empty data. The recent-cows section is capped at five entries via `slice(0, 5)` and shows an `EmptyHint` when no cows are registered, color-coding each row's status badge green or amber based on the same substring check.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\cows.tsx.summary: This Expo Router screen (route group `(gaushala)`) renders the Gaushala portal's cow registry, listing cows and letting staff register new ones. The default-exported `GaushalaCows` component fetches data via the `useCows` hook from `@poojly/api-client` and displays rows through shared `PortalScreen`, `ListRow`, and `EmptyHint` primitives from `../../lib/portal-screen`, styled with the local `theme` module. A slide-up modal contains the `CreateCowForm` (tagNumber, name, breed, ageYears, gender, healthStatus, notes), built from local `Field` and `SegmentRow` helper components, and submits via `api.post` to `/api/v1/gaushala-portal/cows`, then invalidates the `['gaushala', 'cows']` React Query cache. Notable gotchas: when the API returns zero cows the screen silently falls back to a hardcoded `FALLBACK` array of six demo cows, so the list may show fake data; the "adopted" status color is derived by substring-matching `'adopt'` on `adoptionStatus`; and a 409 response is string-matched from the error message to report duplicate tag numbers. Validation requires tagNumber and name, coerces ageYears to a number constrained to 0–40, and the modal blocks dismissal while `submitting` is true.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(devotee)\\_layout.ts.summary: This file defines the root tab layout for the devotee role section of the Expo mobile app, wiring up the bottom navigation shell that all devotee screens render inside. Its default export, `TabLayout`, wraps an expo-router `Tabs` navigator in a `RoleGuard` restricted to `allowedRoles={['devotee']}`, so the entire route group is inaccessible to other user roles; a small internal `TabIcon` helper renders `Ionicons` glyphs for each tab. Five tabs are visible — Home (`index`), Pujas, Darshan, Store, and Profile — while roughly two dozen additional screens (messages, temples, astrology, bookings, donations, darshan-player, kundli, horoscope, yatra, weddings, upgrade, the knowledge/learn-Sanskrit flows, and the gurukul journeys) are registered with `href: null` so they participate in the tab navigator but are only reachable via push navigation, a pattern the comments attribute to a "TD10" feature-parity effort. Dependencies are minimal: `expo-router` for routing, `@expo/vector-icons` for icons, the internal `lib/theme` `colors` palette (saffron active tint, stone inactive tint), and the internal `lib/role-guard` component. Notable gotchas: the tab bar height and padding are platform-conditional (taller with extra bottom padding on iOS to clear the home indicator), headers are globally hidden via `headerShown: false`, and any new devotee screen must be registered here with `href: null` or it won't resolve within this navigator.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\messages..summary: This file defines the GaushalaMessages screen for the mobile app's "(gaushala)" route group, serving as the messaging inbox for gaushala (provider) users. It is a thin Expo Router route component whose only job is to render the shared Inbox component from ../../lib/inbox, passing role="provider" so the inbox is scoped to the provider side of the messaging experience. The only dependency is the internal Inbox component; all messaging logic, data fetching, and UI live there rather than in this file. The key design point is the role prop: the same Inbox is presumably reused across user roles, so this route's sole responsibility is fixing the role context for the gaushala user segment.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\donations.summary: This file is the Gaushala donations screen in the Expo Router mobile app (`apps/mobile/app/(gaushala)/donations.tsx`), rendering a pull-to-refresh list of donation records plus a summary stat card for the gaushala portal. Its default export, the `GaushalaDonations` component, fetches data via the `useGaushalaPortalDonations` hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package and renders it using shared portal primitives — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, and `EmptyHint` from `../../lib/portal-screen` — with palette values from `../../lib/theme`. Two local helpers support presentation: `relTime` buckets ISO timestamps into "today/yesterday/Nd ago/Nmo ago" labels (using 30-day months), and the `STATUS_COLOR` map assigns green to paid/received, amber to created/pending, red to failed, and `colors.stone[600]` as a fallback. A notable gotcha: the "Paid Total" stat is stored in a variable named `monthTotal`, but it actually sums `amountInr` across every fetched donation with a paid or received status, with no date filtering, so the label may overstate a monthly figure. Refresh handling wraps `donationsQuery.refetch()` in local `refreshing` state rather than using the query's own flags, and loading, error, and empty states each render a distinct `EmptyHint`. The component is defensively coded with nullish defaults (`d.donor ?? 'Anonymous'`, `d.amountInr ?? 0`, `d.status ?? 'created'`) so malformed records still render. Minor cleanup note: `spacing` is imported from the theme but never used.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\_layout.t.summary: This file is the layout for the `(gaushala)` route group in the Expo mobile app, defining the bottom-tab navigation shell for gaushala (cow shelter) managers via expo-router's `Tabs` component. The default export `GaushalaLayout` wraps the entire navigator in `RoleGuard` (from `../../lib/role-guard`), restricting access to users with the `gaushala_manager` role. It registers six screens — `dashboard`, `cows`, `donations`, `volunteers`, `profile`, and `messages` — where the first five appear as tabs labeled Home, Cows, Donations, Team, and Profile with Ionicons glyphs supplied by a small `TabIcon` helper, while `messages` is registered with `href: null` so it is navigable as a route but hidden from the tab bar. Styling pulls from the shared `colors` theme in `../../lib/theme`, using a hardcoded amber active tint (`#92400E`) alongside `colors.stone` for inactive and border tones. Notable details: headers are disabled globally (`headerShown: false`), and the tab bar height and padding branch on `Platform.OS` to accommodate iOS safe-area insets versus Android.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\become-pri.summary: This file defines the `BecomePriestScreen`, the onboarding/landing screen shown to prospective pandits in the Darshya mobile app under the `(onboard)` Expo Router group. Its default export renders the shared `OnboardScreen` component from the sibling `_form` module, configuring it with `role="PRIEST"`, marketing copy, a `BENEFITS` list (steady bookings, video proof, weekly payouts, Ask-Pandit consultations), and the apply CTA label. Through the `renderExtras` render prop it injects two role-specific fields built with `ExtraTextField` — a required numeric `yearsExperience` input and a required free-text `specialties` input — whose values are read from and written back into the shared `extras` form state via `setExtra`. All actual form logic, validation, and submission live in `_form`, so this screen is purely declarative configuration; notable details include the hard-coded earnings pitch (60-80% revenue share, Monday payouts after Aadhaar verification) and the assumption that `extras` values may be absent, hence the `?? ''` fallbacks.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\profile.t.summary: This file defines `GaushalaProfile`, the default-exported profile screen for the gaushala (cow-shelter) role group in the Expo Router mobile app, letting a shelter manager view their organization details and sign out. It pulls the signed-in user from `useAuth` (in `../../lib/auth-context`) and fetches shelter records via the `useGaushalas` hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package, then heuristically matches the user to a gaushala by comparing `fullName`/`email` against each record's name and email — a fragile coupling since there's no direct user-to-gaushala ID link. The screen is composed with shared building blocks: `PortalScreen` and `Section` from `../../lib/portal-screen` provide the layout with pull-to-refresh (wired to `gaushalasQuery.refetch`), `MessagesEntry` from `../../lib/inbox` embeds the messaging entry point for the `gaushala` role group, and styling constants come from `../../lib/theme`. It conditionally renders location, cow count, and description from the matched record, falling back to the auth user's name. Sign-out is gated behind a destructive `Alert.alert` confirmation before calling `signOut` and replacing the route with `/(auth)/login` (note the `as any` cast bypassing typed routes). Notably, the "Registration" section's 80G tax-exemption and Animal Welfare Board badges are hardcoded rather than data-driven, so they display for every gaushala regardless of actual certification status.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(gaushala)\\volunteer.summary: This file is the Volunteers screen for the gaushala section of the React Native (Expo Router) mobile app, rendering the active volunteer roster with a summary stat and pull-to-refresh support. The default-exported `Volunteers` component fetches data through the `useGaushalaVolunteers` hook from `@poojly/api-client`, a React Query–style hook whose `data`, `isLoading`, `isError`, and `refetch` drive the screen's loading, error, empty, and populated states. It composes shared portal UI primitives from `../../lib/portal-screen` — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, and `EmptyHint` — plus theme tokens from `../../lib/theme`, and a local `formatJoined` helper renders each volunteer's `joinedAt` ISO date as a short "Mon YYYY" string in the en-IN locale. Notably, filtering is done client-side with `v.active !== false`, so records missing the `active` flag are treated as active, and the "Active" stat is just the length of that filtered array rather than a server-provided count. Pull-to-refresh is implemented by wrapping the query's `refetch` in local `refreshing` state rather than using the query's own fetching flags. Rows degrade gracefully with fallbacks like "No phone" when `v.phone` is absent. One minor gotcha: `spacing` is imported from the theme but never used.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\become-wel.summary: This file defines the wellness-instructor onboarding screen for the mobile app, rendered at the Expo Router route `(onboard)/become-wellness`. Its sole default export, `BecomeWellnessScreen`, is a thin presentational wrapper that delegates all logic to the shared `OnboardScreen` component from the sibling `./_form` module, supplying role-specific content: the `role` of `"WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR"`, marketing copy, a `BENEFITS` list (live sessions on Jitsi with an 80% instructor payout, capacity pricing, placement on the `/wellness` listing, and resellable recordings), and the CTA label "Apply to teach on Darshya". Through the `renderExtras` render prop it injects two role-specific fields into the generic form: a required `ExtraSelectField` for `sessionType` (options defined in `SESSION_TYPES`: yoga, meditation, pranayama, vipassana, other) and an optional `ExtraTextField` for `certifications`, both writing into the shared `extras` state via `setExtra`. The design decision to keep the screen purely declarative means validation, submission, and navigation all live in `_form`, so this file contains no state, hooks, or side effects of its own. Gotchas: both extra fields defensively cast `extras` values `as string` with an empty-string fallback, so the `extras` bag is loosely typed, and adding new wellness-specific fields requires editing this file's `renderExtras` rather than the shared form.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\become-ast.summary: This file defines the astrologer-facing onboarding route for the Darshya mobile app, an Expo Router screen at `(onboard)/become-astrologer` whose default export `BecomeAstrologerScreen` serves as the route component. It is purely declarative: all form state, validation, and submission logic lives in the sibling `_form` module, from which it imports the shared `OnboardScreen` component plus the `ExtraTextField` and `ExtraSelectField` primitives. The screen configures `OnboardScreen` with `role="ASTROLOGER"`, marketing copy, a module-level `BENEFITS` list (per-minute pricing from ₹10, Jitsi-based chat/video, daily payouts after ₹5,000 lifetime earnings, and Aadhaar/qualification verification), and a `renderExtras` render prop that injects two astrologer-specific fields: a required `astrologyType` select (vedic, tarot, numerology, palmistry, other from `ASTROLOGY_TYPES`) and a numeric `yearsExperience` text input. Extra field values are stored in a loosely typed `extras` bag and read back with `as string` casts, so type safety depends on `_form`'s handling rather than this file. Notably, the copy is localized for the Indian market (INR pricing, Aadhaar verification), and the file's design keeps content separate from mechanics so sibling role screens can reuse the same onboarding shell with different configuration.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\become-gur.summary: This file defines `BecomeGurukulScreen`, the default-exported React Native screen for the `(onboard)` route group in the Expo mobile app, which lets an authenticated founder register a new gurukul listing. The screen renders a long form covering basic details (name, URL slug, description, city/state/country, tradition), contact info, mode flags (residential, online, accepts minors), and a dynamic list of `ProgramDraft` entries that the user can add or remove, each with duration, fee, mode of study, age range, and description. It depends on `useAuth` from `lib/auth-context` for the session access token, `apiBase` from `lib/api` for the backend URL, design tokens from `lib/theme`, plus `expo-router` for navigation, `react-native-safe-area-context`, and `@expo/vector-icons`. Submission performs client-side validation (required fields, 50-character minimum description, at least one program with a 20-character minimum description), then POSTs the payload to `/api/v1/gurukuls` with a Bearer token; on success it shows an alert and routes to `/gurukul-portal`, since listings go live only after admin review. Notable details: the `TRADITIONS` and `MODES` option sets are hardcoded constants, the slug input is forcibly sanitized to lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` on every keystroke, and numeric fields like duration, ages, and fees are held as strings in local state and coerced via `Number()` only at submit time, so non-numeric input would silently become `NaN`. A small internal `CheckRow` component renders the custom checkboxes, and the submit button is disabled whenever the user is unauthenticated or a request is in flight.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\list-templ.summary: This file defines `ListTempleScreen`, the Expo Router route at `apps/mobile/app/(onboard)/list-temple.tsx` that pitches the Darshya platform to temple trusts and collects their application during onboarding. It is a thin presentation layer over the shared `OnboardScreen` component imported from the sibling `./_form` module, which it configures with `role="TEMPLE"`, marketing copy, a hard-coded `BENEFITS` array (live darshan reach, online puja bookings, 80G donation receipts, and devotee CRM analytics), and the CTA label "Apply to list my temple". Its only temple-specific logic lives in the `renderExtras` render prop, which injects two required `ExtraTextField` inputs — `templeName` and `deity` — whose values are stored in the generic `extras` bag managed by `OnboardScreen` and cast to string at read time. The design keeps this screen declarative and free of state or submission logic, delegating form handling, validation, and API work entirely to `_form`, so the only coupling is the expected shape of the `extras` record and the `setExtra` setter. Notably, the benefits content is static marketing text rather than data-driven, and both extra fields are marked required, meaning submission gating depends on `OnboardScreen` honoring that flag.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\_layout.ts.summary: This file defines the shared navigation layout for the onboarding flow in the mobile app, wrapping all screens under the `(onboard)` route group in a single stack navigator. Its default export, `OnboardLayout`, is a React component that renders a `Stack` from the `expo-router` library and registers seven named screens covering the app's partner and role onboarding paths: `list-temple`, `become-priest`, `become-astrologer`, `become-wellness`, `list-gaushala`, `become-gurukul`, and `waitlist`. The only dependency is `expo-router`, which supplies file-based routing and the stack navigator. Notable choices include hiding the header globally (`headerShown: false`), meaning each screen must handle its own navigation UI, setting a shared warm off-white background (`#FAFAF9`) for visual consistency, and using a `slide_from_right` transition animation. The explicit `Stack.Screen` declarations serve purely to register the screens in a defined order; they add no per-screen options, so all configuration lives in the shared `screenOptions`.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\list-gaush.summary: This file is the gaushala-listing onboarding screen for the mobile app, located at the Expo Router route `(onboard)/list-gaushala`, and its purpose is to pitch the Darshya platform to cow shelters and collect their application details. Its single default export, `ListGaushalaScreen`, renders the shared `OnboardScreen` component imported from the local `./_form` module, configuring it with the role `"GAUSHALA"`, marketing copy, a `BENEFITS` array of four selling points (Razorpay donations with auto-emailed 80G receipts, a verified badge, cow-count photo proof, and recurring monthly seva subscriptions), and the CTA label "Apply to list my gaushala". The screen supplies role-specific fields through the `renderExtras` render prop, using `ExtraTextField` for a required gaushala name and numeric cow count, plus `ExtraCheckboxField` for an 80G-registration declaration, storing values under the keys `gaushalaName`, `cowCount`, and `has80G` via the `extras`/`setExtra` callback pattern. All form state management, submission logic, and shared layout live in `_form`, so this file is purely declarative configuration with no direct dependencies beyond that module. A notable gotcha is that `cowCount` is captured as a string (numeric keyboard only), and the 80G checkbox is only a self-declaration — the copy explicitly notes "we'll verify," implying actual verification happens elsewhere in the backend flow.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\bookings.ts.summary: This file defines `PriestBookings`, the React Native screen that lets a priest view and manage their assigned bookings in the mobile app. It fetches data through the `usePriestBookings` hook from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package and performs mutations via that package's `api` client, hitting REST endpoints `/api/v1/priest/bookings/:id/start`, `/complete`, and `/video`, then invalidating the `['priest', 'bookings']` React Query cache via `useQueryClient` from `@tanstack/react-query`. The UI is built on shared internal components `PortalScreen` and `EmptyHint` plus the `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSize`/`borderRadius` theme tokens from `../../lib/portal-screen` and `../../lib/theme`. Bookings are filtered client-side with chips for all/pending/confirmed/in_progress/completed, using loose substring matching on lowercased status strings (e.g. `includes('progress')`) rather than exact status equality, which is a potential fragility if new statuses overlap. Action availability (Start, Complete, Upload Video) is similarly derived from status substrings plus the `videoUploadedAt` flag, and a per-card `busyId` state disables buttons while a request is in flight. A notable gotcha: video upload relies on `Alert.prompt`, which only exists on iOS, so Android users are shown a fallback message directing them to the web portal to upload video proof.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\messages.ts.summary: This file defines the messages screen for the priest-facing section of the Expo Router mobile app, living at the route `(priest)/messages`. Its sole default export, `PriestMessages`, is a thin route component that renders the shared `Inbox` component from `../../lib/inbox` with the `role` prop set to `"provider"`. The heavy lifting—conversation listing, message state, and any backend wiring—lives entirely in the shared `Inbox` module, making this file pure route glue. The notable design decision is role-based reuse: the same `Inbox` implementation serves multiple user types, with the `role` prop (here `"provider"`, presumably distinguishing priests from regular users) driving behavior differences. The `(priest)` path segment is an Expo Router route group, so it scopes navigation/auth layout without appearing in the URL. There is no local state, styling, or logic here—any bug in message display should be investigated in `lib/inbox`, not in this file.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\dashboard.t.summary: This file is the priest-facing home screen of the Poojly mobile app, an Expo Router route at `app/(priest)/dashboard.tsx` whose default export is the `PriestDashboard` component. It pulls live data through the `usePriestDashboard` and `usePriestBookings` hooks from the internal `@poojly/api-client` package, rendering summary stats (today's bookings, daily and monthly earnings, rating, pending video uploads) and the first five upcoming bookings. All UI is composed from the shared portal primitives in `../../lib/portal-screen` — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, and `EmptyHint` — styled with `colors` and `spacing` tokens from `../../lib/theme`, with no direct dependency beyond React and React Native itself. Pull-to-refresh is wired by a local `refreshing` state that awaits `Promise.all` on both queries' `refetch` methods. A notable gotcha is the hardcoded `FALLBACK` object of plausible-looking stats that is shown whenever the dashboard query has no data, meaning users may see fake demo numbers during loading or API failures with no visual distinction. Amounts are formatted with the `en-IN` locale and a ₹ prefix, and the booking status chip color is chosen by a fragile string check for "confirm" in the status label, defaulting everything else to amber.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\waitlist.t.summary: This file is the waitlist signup screen for the Darshya mobile app, living at the `(onboard)/waitlist` route; it collects an email (the only required field) plus optional full name, phone, and city, along with `panchangOptIn` (defaulted on) and `whatsappOptIn` (defaulted off) checkboxes, then submits the payload to the backend's `POST /waitlist` endpoint tagged with source `mobile_waitlist_screen`. The default-exported `WaitlistScreen` component drives submission through a `@tanstack/react-query` `useMutation`, using the internal `apiPost` and `apiFetch` helpers from `lib/api`, and styling comes from the shared `lib/theme` tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`). On success it expects a `referralCode` in the `WaitlistResponse` and then makes a best-effort follow-up GET to `/waitlist/stats?code=...` for `WaitlistStats` (rank, total, referralCount), rendering a success view with the referral code, position stats, and a back-to-home button. Navigation uses `expo-router`'s `router`, icons come from `@expo/vector-icons` `Ionicons`, and layout uses `SafeAreaView` plus `KeyboardAvoidingView` for iOS. Notable gotchas: a missing `referralCode` in an otherwise successful response is surfaced as an error, the stats fetch failure is silently swallowed (stats render as null), optional fields are trimmed and omitted entirely when empty, there is no email format validation beyond a non-empty check, and the home navigation uses a `router.replace('/' as any)` cast to bypass typed-route checking.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\profile.tsx.summary: This file defines the default-exported `PriestProfile` screen component for the priest section of the Expo mobile app, rendering a priest's profile details, verification status, and sign-out action. It fetches profile data via the `usePriestProfile` hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package, casting the loosely typed response into a local `PriestProfileShape` interface covering display name, bio, languages, specializations, experience, and Aadhaar/bank/GST verification flags. Layout is built from shared in-house primitives — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, and `EmptyHint` from `../../lib/portal-screen`, `MessagesEntry` from `../../lib/inbox` (rendered with `roleGroup="priest"`), and theme tokens from `../../lib/theme` — while auth state and `signOut` come from `../../lib/auth-context`, with navigation handled by `expo-router` and icons by `@expo/vector-icons`. Pull-to-refresh is wired manually through a local `refreshing` state flag that calls `profileQuery.refetch()`. Notable choices include defensive null-coalescing defaults (verification flags default to false/`pending`, name falls back from profile to auth user to 'Pandit'), an error hint shown only when the query fails and no cached profile exists, and a destructive sign-out confirmation via React Native's `Alert` that replaces the route with `/(auth)/login` using an `as any` cast on the typed route. The screen is read-only — there is no editing capability despite displaying rich profile data.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\payouts.tsx.summary: This file defines the priest-facing "Payouts" screen in the Poojly mobile app, rendered via Expo Router at the route group `(priest)/payouts`, and exists to show a priest their earnings history with summary stats and a list of individual payouts. The default export `PriestPayouts` fetches data through the `usePriestPayouts` hook from the `@poojly/api-client` package, then computes client-side aggregates — total earned via `reduce`, and pending versus paid counts via a case-insensitive status filter — displayed in two `StatCard` components. The payout list is rendered with shared portal UI primitives imported from `../../lib/portal-screen` (`PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, `EmptyHint`), with visual styling driven by theme tokens (`colors`, `spacing`) from `../../lib/theme`. Pull-to-refresh is wired manually through local `refreshing` state that calls `payoutsQuery.refetch()`. Notable details: all amounts are hardcoded to Indian formatting (₹ symbol with `en-IN` locale), payout status coloring branches on whether the lowercased status equals `"paid"`, rows without a `bookingId` are labeled "Manual payout," and identifiers are truncated to their first eight characters for display.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(onboard)\\_form.tsx.summary: This file provides the shared self-onboarding form used by the role-specific screens in the mobile app's `(onboard)` route group, letting temples, priests, astrologers, wellness instructors, and gaushalas apply to join Darshya. Its main export, `OnboardScreen`, is a parameterized React Native component driven by an `OnboardRole` ('TEMPLE' | 'PRIEST' | 'ASTROLOGER' | 'WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR' | 'GAUSHALA') plus eyebrow/title/subtitle copy, a benefits list, and a `renderExtras` render prop through which sibling route files inject role-specific fields built from the exported `ExtraTextField`, `ExtraSelectField`, and `ExtraCheckboxField` helpers. The component collects name, email, phone, city, and state in local state, merges in arbitrary string/boolean extras, and submits via a `@tanstack/react-query` `useMutation` that calls `apiPost` from `../../lib/api` against the `/leads/self-onboard` backend endpoint. On success it swaps to a confirmation view showing the returned `leadId` as a reference and navigates home with `expo-router`'s `router.replace`; failures surface either the server's `error` message or a network fallback in an inline error box. Styling comes entirely from the shared `../../lib/theme` tokens (colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius), with `Ionicons` from `@expo/vector-icons` and `SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context`. Notable details: payload construction trims all strings and lowercases email, silently drops empty-string and `false` extras, and the `required` flag on extra fields is purely visual — validation only enforces the five base fields. Also worth noting are the iOS-only `KeyboardAvoidingView` behavior and the `router.replace('/' as any)` cast that bypasses typed-route checking.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\services.ts.summary: This file defines the "My Services" screen for the priest-facing section of the mobile app, letting priests view their puja offerings and toggle which ones are active. The default-exported `PriestServices` component fetches live data via the `usePujas` hook from `@poojly/api-client`, normalizing inconsistent API field names (`name`/`title`, `basePrice`/`basePriceInr`) into a local `ServiceOffer` interface, and falls back to a hardcoded `FALLBACK` catalog of six pujas (Rudrabhishek, Satyanarayan Katha, etc.) when the API returns nothing. Rendering is done through shared layout primitives `PortalScreen`, `Section`, and `EmptyHint` from `../../lib/portal-screen`, styled with design tokens (`colors`, `spacing`, `fontSize`, `borderRadius`) from `../../lib/theme`. Pull-to-refresh triggers `pujasQuery.refetch()`, and the header shows an "X of Y active" count derived from the toggle states. The main gotcha is that enable/disable toggles are stored only in a local `overrides` state map—nothing is persisted to the backend, so changes are lost on remount and don't actually affect availability. The `{ limit: 20 } as never` cast on the query also signals a type mismatch being suppressed rather than resolved.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\reviews.tsx.summary: This file defines the priest-facing Reviews screen (`PriestReviews`, default export) in the Expo Router route group `(priest)`, showing a priest's average rating, total review count, and a list of recent devotee feedback. It pulls live data via the `usePriestDashboard` and `usePriestBookings` hooks from the `@poojly/api-client` package, and renders through shared portal primitives — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, and `EmptyHint` from `../../lib/portal-screen` — styled with tokens from `../../lib/theme`, with star ratings drawn by a small internal `Stars` component using `Ionicons` from `@expo/vector-icons`. A key design compromise: there is no dedicated reviews API, so the screen synthesizes `Review` objects from completed bookings (matched by status containing "complet", capped at 10), hardcoding a 5-star rating and a placeholder comment for each. If there are no completed bookings, it instead shows hardcoded `FALLBACK_REVIEWS` sample data — which means the `EmptyHint` branch is effectively unreachable, a gotcha worth knowing when wiring up a real reviews endpoint. Summary stats prefer server values (`dash.rating`, `dash.ratingCount`) and only fall back to averaging the displayed reviews when dashboard data is missing. Pull-to-refresh triggers a parallel `refetch()` of both queries.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\subscriptio.summary: This file is the Expo Router route entry for the priest-facing subscription page in the mobile app, living under the `(priest)` route group in `apps/mobile`. Its sole export is the default React component `PriestSubscription`, which does nothing more than render the shared `SubscriptionScreen` component from `lib/subscription-screen` with `role="priest"` passed as a prop. The only dependencies are React itself and that internal `SubscriptionScreen` module, which is where all the actual subscription UI and logic reside. The design follows a thin-route-wrapper convention: route files stay nearly empty and delegate to reusable screen components in `lib`, so behavior is centralized rather than duplicated per route. The `role` parameterization indicates `SubscriptionScreen` is intended to serve multiple user roles (with a sibling route presumably passing a different role), so any priest-specific behavior must be driven by that prop inside the shared component. Note that the `(priest)` parentheses mark an Expo Router route group, meaning "priest" segments the file structure without appearing in the URL path itself.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(priest)\\_layout.tsx.summary: This file defines the tab navigation layout for the priest-facing section of the Expo mobile app, using expo-router's `Tabs` component. Its default export, `PriestLayout`, wraps the entire tab navigator in a `RoleGuard` (from `lib/role-guard`) restricted to the `priest` role, so every screen in this group inherits priest-only access control. Six tabs are exposed in the bar — dashboard ("Home"), bookings, services, payouts, profile, and subscription ("Plan") — each rendered with an `Ionicons` glyph via the local `TabIcon` helper, while the reviews and messages screens are registered with `href: null` so they remain routable but hidden from the tab bar. Styling comes from the shared `colors` palette in `lib/theme`, using saffron for the active tint and stone for inactive icons, and the tab bar height and padding are adjusted per platform (taller with extra bottom padding on iOS to clear the home indicator). A notable gotcha is that `headerShown` is disabled globally, so each child screen must render its own header if one is needed.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(store-admin)\\dashbo.summary: This file defines `StoreDashboard`, the default-exported React Native screen for the store-admin section of the Expo Router mobile app, giving store owners an at-a-glance summary of sales, orders, stock, and catalogue health. It pulls data through the shared `@poojly/api-client` hooks `useProducts` and `useStoreAdminDashboard`, then renders stat cards (today's sales, today's orders, month sales, low-stock count), a messages entry point via `MessagesEntry`, and the five most recent orders and products as `ListRow` items. All layout primitives — `PortalScreen`, `Section`, `StatCard`, `ListRow`, and `EmptyHint` — come from the local `lib/portal-screen` module, while `colors` and `spacing` come from `lib/theme`. A local `inr` helper formats currency using the `en-IN` locale with a rupee prefix, reflecting the app's Indian market focus. Pull-to-refresh is implemented with a local `refreshing` state that refetches both queries in parallel via `Promise.all`. The code is defensively written with null-coalescing defaults (`?? []`, `?? 0`, `?? {}`) so it renders gracefully before data loads, and it hard-truncates both lists to five entries since the screen is a summary rather than a full listing. Low-stock and sales figures are accented with `colors.red[600]` and `colors.green[600]` respectively to draw attention to problems and performance.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(store-admin)\\revenu.summary: This file defines StoreRevenue, the store-admin revenue dashboard screen in the Expo mobile app, which displays lifetime sales aggregates (today, this month, this year) alongside a ranked list of top-selling products. It fetches data via the useStoreAdminRevenue hook from the shared @poojly/api-client package, and renders through the app's internal portal primitives: PortalScreen (which supplies pull-to-refresh scaffolding), Section, StatCard, and EmptyHint from ../../lib/portal-screen, styled with tokens from ../../lib/theme. Amounts are formatted as Indian rupees with a local inr() helper using en-IN locale grouping, defensively defaulting undefined values to zero. Notable details: pull-to-refresh manually wires the React Query refetch into a local refreshing state; the top-products section handles three explicit empty states (loading, error, and no paid orders yet); and each product row shows rank, name, units sold, and per-product revenue.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(store-admin)\\messag.summary: This file is an Expo Router route screen that serves as the messages inbox for store administrators, exposed at the `/messages` path inside the `(store-admin)` route group (the parentheses keep the group name out of the URL while scoping the screen under that section's layout). Its only export is the default component `StoreAdminMessages`, which Expo Router requires as the default export for file-based routing. The screen itself contains no logic; it simply renders the shared `Inbox` component imported from `../../lib/inbox` (i.e., `apps/mobile/lib/inbox`) with the prop `role="provider"`. The key dependency is therefore the internal `Inbox` module, which owns all message-list behavior, and the `role` prop indicates `Inbox` is a role-aware component reused across different user types, so any behavioral differences for store admins versus other roles are driven from inside `Inbox`, not here. A notable gotcha: because this is a thin wrapper, searching for inbox logic in this file will be a dead end — changes to rendering, data fetching, or permissions must be made in `lib/inbox` and may affect other roles that consume it.

apps\\mobile\\app\\(store-admin)\\orders.summary: This file is the store-admin orders screen of the mobile app, rendering the `StoreOrders` component (the default export) so staff can browse incoming orders, filter them by fulfillment stage, and advance each order's status.
