It depends on the sibling module `_lib.mjs` for `fetchText`, `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, and the `TODAY` date constant, plus `node:fs` for state persistence; it requires no authentication and is designed for a polite daily cadence. The main entry point `run()` iterates the hardcoded `FEEDS` list, parses each response with `parseItems`, diffs against persisted state, and writes the report via `writeReport('competitor-watch', ...)` with a one-line summary logged through `upsertLog`. `parseItems` is a deliberately minimal regex-based RSS/Atom extractor that handles both `<item>` and `<entry>` blocks, CDATA-wrapped titles, and links expressed either as element text or an `href` attribute, capping results at 20 items per feed. Seen-item state lives in `docs/agent-reports/_competitor-watch-state.json` as a map of link URL to first-seen date, managed by `loadState`/`saveState`, which silently recover from a missing or corrupt state file by starting fresh (meaning the first run reports everything as new). Gotchas: fetch failures are recorded as per-feed error rows rather than aborting the run, the report table is truncated to 40 rows with pipe characters in titles sanitized, and titles/dates are hard-truncated to keep output compact.

scripts\\agents\\content-pipeline.mjs.summary: This script is a daily "content agent" that auto-generates three article draft outlines (deity-of-day, Veda angle, Sanatan theme) plus a Sanskrit shloka social card, writing the result as a Markdown report to `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-content-draft.md` via the shared `writeReport` helper. It exports nothing; it runs as a standalone CLI (`run()` invoked at the bottom) built entirely on the sibling module `_lib.mjs`, from which it imports `fetchJson`, `writeReport`, `TODAY`, and `API_BASE`. Its only external dependency is the Darshya backend's `GET /api/v1/panchang/today` endpoint, which it queries with hardcoded New Delhi coordinates (lat 28.6139, lng 77.2090) to ground the drafts in today's panchang. Content selection is purely deterministic rotation: the `TOPICS` map is keyed by weekday abbreviation (`Mon`→Shiva, `Tue`→Hanuman, etc.), while `SANSKRIT_SLOKAS`, `VED_ANGLES`, and `SANATAN_THEMES` are indexed by day-of-month modulo array length, so the cycle repeats monthly with no memory of what was previously published. The generated Markdown is heavily marketing-oriented — each draft embeds SEO keyword clusters, recommended slugs under `/sanatan` and `/ved`, and CTAs for Darshya products (puja booking, Sanskrit course, weekly digest) — plus a distribution checklist targeting MDX content in `apps/web/content`. Notable gotchas: the panchang payload is defensively unwrapped (`p.json?.panchang || p.json`) and truncated to 1200 characters, and a panchang fetch failure will crash the whole script since there is no fallback around `fetchJson`.

scripts\\agents\\cac-tripwire.mjs.summary: `scripts/agents/cac-tripwire.mjs` is a weekly monitoring agent (Node ES module, intended for cron) that computes blended paid-install customer acquisition cost across Meta UAC and Google UAC India campaigns and raises a strategic alert when CAC exceeds the ₹40 ceiling for two consecutive weeks past launch day 14. Its `fetchMeta()` pulls last-7-day spend and `mobile_app_install` counts from the Meta Graph API v19.0 insights endpoint, while `fetchGoogle()` is a deliberate stub that always reports unavailable because the Google Ads GAQL query is deferred pending OAuth refresh-token wiring. `loadState()`/`saveState()` persist a rolling 10-week history plus a `breachStreak` counter to `docs/agent-reports/_cac-tripwire-state.json`, and `pastLaunchPlus14()` gates the tripwire on `APP_LAUNCH_DATE_ISO` (which falls back to a 2026-08-01 placeholder). The script builds on shared helpers `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `REPORT_DIR`, and `TODAY` from `./_lib.mjs` and emits dated Markdown reports into `docs/agent-reports/`. Key gotchas: every credential env var is optional — with none configured the script writes a NO-OP report rather than failing (expected pre-launch), the tripwire fires only when both the two-week streak and the launch+14-day conditions hold, and the top-level catch soft-fails by writing an error report and exiting 0 so scheduled runs don't turn red. When the tripwire fires, the generated report prescribes the ROADMAP.md response: pause domestic India UAC on both channels and shift the ₹2L/mo budget to NRI lanes with USD pricing.

scripts\\agents\\content-publisher.mjs.summary: This standalone Node.js script is the content-publisher agent for the Darshya devotional platform: once per day it auto-generates a markdown blog draft into `docs/agent-reports/blog-drafts/` so the founder has a review queue, deliberately using curated templates with TODO placeholders rather than any paid AI generation. It has no exports; the internal pipeline is `run()` calling `pickKeyword()` (which deterministically selects one of 15 long-tail India-devotional SEO entries in the `KEYWORDS` catalog via day-of-year modulo), `slugify()`, and `draft()` (which interpolates the keyword into a front-matter-plus-body template with significance, vidhi, samagri, FAQ, and CTA sections, switching the call-to-action based on the keyword's commercial vs. informational intent). Its only internal dependency is `./_lib.mjs`, from which it imports `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, and `TODAY` to emit the daily `YYYY-MM-DD-content-publisher.md` report and log line; otherwise it uses just `node:fs` and `node:path`, and the generated drafts deep-link to live darshya.online pages (`/pujas`, `/panchang`, `/shlokas`, `/donations`). A notable safety guard: `run()` refuses to overwrite a draft that appears human-edited — detected by a missing `status: draft` marker or content more than 20% longer than the template — marking it "skipped — human-edited" instead. Gotchas include the 15-day keyword rotation repeating indefinitely, hardcoded pricing claims (₹501–₹5,100) and 80G receipt language embedded in the template, and the fact that drafts require manual founder review and relocation to `apps/web/content/blog/` before publishing. Any fatal error is caught, logged, and exits with code 1 so scheduled runs fail loudly.

scripts\\agents\\fleet-integrity-check.m.summary: `fleet-integrity-check.mjs` is a CI guard script that verifies every probe URL embedded in `schema-validator.mjs` actually resolves to a real Next.js route, replacing an inline heredoc that previously lived in the `pr-checks.yml` workflow. It exports nothing itself; instead it statically reads the source of `schema-validator.mjs` with `node:fs` and extracts probe targets via a regex over `url: '...'` literals, rather than importing the module. It then builds a route manifest from the `apps/web/app` directory using `buildRouteManifest` from the sibling `route-manifest.mjs` module, and checks each URL with `resolveProbe`, which understands named dynamic segments like `[month]`, `[chapter]`, `[kanda]`, `[parva]`, `[pada]`, `[slug]`, and catch-all routes. If any probe fails to resolve, the script emits a GitHub Actions `::error::` annotation listing the offending URLs and exits with code 1, failing the PR check; otherwise it logs a success count. The notable design choice is the regex-based static extraction, which keeps the check dependency-free and side-effect-free but means probes constructed dynamically rather than as single-quoted `url:` literals would be silently missed.

scripts\\agents\\cs-sla-tracker.mjs.summary: This script is a daily cron agent that measures customer-support first-response latency against roadmap item R-Q3-CS-001 (P50 under 2 hours across email, WhatsApp, and chat). It reads inbound tickets from the shared JSONL file `docs/agent-reports/_inbound-tickets.jsonl` (the same feed consumed by the `support-intent-triage` agent) and exports three functions: `readInbound` parses the JSONL while skipping malformed lines and records missing `id`/`text`, `percentile` computes interpolated percentiles on a sorted array, and `computeSla` buckets tickets from a rolling 7-day window into normalized channels (via `normalizeChannel`, which maps aliases like mail/resend → email and wa/wa-cloud → whatsapp, falling back to `other`) and calculates per-channel and overall p50/p90, pending counts, and the number meeting the 120-minute `SLA_TARGET_MINUTES`. Only tickets with a valid `firstResponseAt` timestamp count toward latency stats (negative latencies are discarded); unacknowledged tickets are tallied as `pending` instead. The `main` entrypoint writes the snapshot to `docs/agent-reports/_cs-sla-state.json` for the agent-fleet dashboard and the `docs/roadmap/_manual-kpis.yml` refresher (KPI key `cs_p50_response_minutes`), and renders a Markdown verdict report through `writeReport` from the sibling internal module `./_lib.mjs` (alongside `TODAY` and `isoNow` helpers), using only Node built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`) with no external dependencies. Notable gotchas: the script intentionally runs no-op-but-alive until a founder wires an actual inbound source (WhatsApp Cloud webhook, Resend inbound parse, or LiveChatWidget escalation), so zero-data runs emit a "no-data" verdict rather than failing, and execution is gated by a direct-invocation check against `import.meta.url` plus the `CS_SLA_TRACKER_RUN` environment variable so it can also be imported as a library without side effects.

scripts\\agents\\founder-tweet-draft.mjs.summary: This is a scheduled Node.js agent script that generates five ready-to-copy, founder-voice tweet drafts each day and writes them as a markdown checklist to `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-founder-tweet-draft.md` via `writeReport`, with a one-line activity entry recorded through `upsertLog`. It deliberately makes no AI calls: drafts come from a deterministic `TEMPLATES` array of five functions seeded with real product signals — the live sitemap URL count fetched with `fetchText` from `${WEB_BASE}/sitemap.xml` in `getSitemapStats`, the current date `TODAY` (used as the "panchang day" hook), and proximity to the next entry in a hardcoded `FESTIVALS` table of approximate 2026 Indian festival dates, computed by `nextFestival` and `daysUntil`. Each draft is length-checked in the report (✓ under 280 chars, "⚠ premium" under 4000, "✗ too long" otherwise) and the file ends with posting-cadence advice, since the founder is expected to personalize and post manually rather than auto-publish. All shared plumbing — `fetchText`, `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `WEB_BASE`, `TODAY` — comes from the sibling module `./_lib.mjs`, and the content promotes the darshya.online product (puja booking, panchang, shlokas) while name-dropping competitor accounts like @srimandir. Notable gotchas: festival dates are approximate and only cover 2026, with `nextFestival` wrapping around to `FESTIVALS[0]` once all dates pass (which will produce stale hooks after November 2026), and a failed sitemap fetch aborts the whole run via the fatal `run().catch` handler.

scripts\\agents\\dormant-reactivation.mj.summary: This script is a weekly re-engagement agent that runs on a daily cron but self-skips every day except Wednesday (UTC) unless `FORCE=1` is set, fetching users dormant ≥30 days and emailing each a personalized "come book a puja" nudge. Its `main()` pulls the dormant-user list from the backend endpoint `/api/v1/admin/ops/dormant-users?days=30` (authenticated via the `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` query param against `API_BASE`), renders an HTML email via `emailHtml()`, and sends it through `sendEmail()`, which posts directly to the Resend API using `RESEND_API_KEY`. Personalization is fully deterministic: the `NAKSHATRA_HOOKS` constant maps ten nakshatras to recommended sevas, falling back to a Mahamrityunjaya jaap suggestion when the user's nakshatra is missing or unmapped, so no LLM is involved. Deduplication is handled by `loadState()`/`saveState()`, which persist a per-`user_id` timestamp to `_dormant-reactivation-state.json` under `docs/agent-reports` and suppress re-sends for 90 days even if the user stays dormant. It depends internally on `_lib.mjs` for `writeReport`, `TODAY`, `isoNow`, `API_BASE`, and `WEB_BASE`, and always emits a markdown report via `writeReport('dormant-reactivation', …)` covering sends, skips, and failures (log capped at 30 entries). Notable gotchas: it gracefully degrades when `RESEND_API_KEY` is absent by recording the user as "skipped" in state anyway (burning the 90-day window without sending), sleeps 400ms between sends to keep Resend's rate limits predictable, uses a 15-second `AbortSignal` timeout on the feed fetch, and treats malformed state files as empty rather than failing.

scripts\\agents\\funnel-drop-analyzer.te.summary: This file is the regression test suite for the `funnel-drop-analyzer` agent, written with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` to match the style of `route-manifest.test.mjs`. It exists to lock in a fix for a production bug where the analyzer detected a dead funnel (all five stages at zero for 60+ days) but filed zero GitHub issues, because an early `continue` on `baseline === 0` kept the all-zero state from ever reaching the P0 filing branch; the fix routes a dead funnel into a single deduped P0 alert using a stable `:dead` fingerprint bucket. The suite imports `createAnalyzer` from `funnel-drop-analyzer.mjs` and injects fakes via helpers: `deadFunnel()` and `collapsedFunnel()` build synthetic 7-day funnel payloads, `mockGh()` stubs the GitHub issues API while recording POSTs, `mockIo()` captures `writeReport`/`upsertLog` calls so the real `docs/` tree is untouched, and `funnelSource()` returns a fixed payload. Coverage spans six scenarios: a dead funnel files exactly one P0 issue labeled `P0`, `funnel-drop`, and `agent-auto-filed` with a `_fingerprint` marker; filing is suppressed when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is empty; the run is skipped entirely when `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` is missing; a second run with the same fingerprint open files nothing (dedupe); a collapsed funnel with a real baseline still files five distinct per-stage issues via the >70%-drop path; and a healthy funnel files nothing. Notable design points are the full dependency-injection mocking strategy (no network, no real issue filing, no filesystem writes) and the assertions on the log line `findings=5 filed=1` versus the old `filed=0`, which pin the exact observable symptom of the original bug.

scripts\\agents\\daily-devotional-broadc.summary: This cron script pushes a 06:00 IST daily devotional message over WhatsApp, composing deterministic content via `pickToday` from the `VAAR_DEVATA` table (day-of-week deity plus mantra) and a `SHLOKAS` pool of Bhagavad Gita verses indexed by day-of-year, optionally enriched with a panchang/tithi snapshot from `getPanchang`. It builds on the shared `./_lib.mjs` helpers (`writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `fetchJson`, `API_BASE`, `TODAY`), calls two internal endpoints — `/api/v1/panchang/today` and `/api/v1/admin/ops/wa-devotional-opt-ins`, both gated by `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` — and delivers through Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API at graph.facebook.com using `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, and the template named by `WHATSAPP_DEVOTIONAL_TEMPLATE` (default `daily_devotional`). The design is deliberately env-or-noop: if WhatsApp credentials are absent the script skips sending but still writes its Markdown report to `docs/agent-reports/` as a content draft and audit log. It is WhatsApp-only by policy to preserve the Resend 100/day email cap for transactional mail, recipients are truncated to `MAX_WA_RECIPIENTS` (default 500), sends are throttled 200ms apart, and the per-failure list in the report is capped at 20 entries. A subtle gotcha: `pickToday` and the log line use `getUTCDay`/UTC epoch math, so the "today" boundary is UTC rather than the IST the header advertises, and the panchang fetch is best-effort — the broadcast proceeds without tithi/nakshatra if that API fails.

scripts\\agents\\generate-deity-cluster-.summary: This one-off Node script generates 28 SEO blog drafts (4 weeks × 7 weekdays) for the "Daily Devata" content cluster tracked as R-Q1-M-009, writing Markdown files with YAML frontmatter into `docs/agent-reports/blog-drafts/` marked `status: ready-for-founder-review`, meaning a human approves them before they are copied to `/content/blog` for publish. Its core data structures are the `WEEKDAYS` array (mapping each vaar to a deity plus `pujaSlug` and `aartiSlug` for internal links to `/pujas/`, `/aarti/`, `/deity/`, `/nri`, and `/today` routes on the Darshya site) and the `WEEK_ANGLES` table, which gives each weekday four distinct editorial angles and mantras so the four per-weekday articles don't duplicate. Two helper functions do the templating: `buildMeta`, which assembles a 140–160 character `meta_description` from candidate strings (with a crude fallback that pads short strings with " Sacred." or truncates with "..."), and `buildBody`, which interpolates a fixed long-form article skeleton covering vidhi steps, mantras, stories, an NRI corner, and FAQs. It depends only on Node built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url`) and writes files synchronously in a simple nested loop. A notable design decision is that the deity mapping deliberately follows the canonical implementation in `apps/web/app/today/page.tsx` (`DAY_DEITY`) rather than the spec — so Saturday is Hanuman (not Santoshi Maa) and Sunday is Surya, though Sunday reuses the `vishnu` slug and `vishnu-aarti`, which means Surya articles internally link to the Vishnu deity page. Other gotchas: `created_at` dates are hardcoded to February 2026 based on loop position, frontmatter is built via raw string interpolation (no YAML escaping of titles), and the generated prose leans on templated claims about scripture that a reviewer should fact-check before publication.

scripts\\agents\\funnel-drop-analyzer.mj.summary: This file is a daily cron agent (funnel-drop-analyzer) that polls `/api/v1/admin/metrics/funnel?days=7`, compares yesterday's per-stage counts against the 6-day prior median for the stages landing → signup → kyc → booking → payment_success, and files a deduplicated P0 GitHub issue when any stage drops more than the `FUNNEL_DROP_THRESHOLD` (default 70%). Its only export is the `createAnalyzer` factory, which accepts injectable `ghFetch`, `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `getFunnel`, and token parameters so tests can run without network or env access; it returns a `run()` that resolves `{ findings, filed, skipped }`, while the env-driven `main()` entrypoint wires the real implementations and only executes when the script is run directly. Internal dependencies come from `./_lib.mjs` (`writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `fetchJson`, `API_BASE`, `TODAY`), and external services are the app's own admin metrics API (authenticated via the `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` query param with a 15-second `AbortSignal.timeout`) and the GitHub REST API at `api.github.com` (using `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`, defaulting to repo `XI1568-raghav/bhaktisetu` via `GH_REPO`). Dedup works by embedding a `fingerprint` — the stage name plus the drop rounded to the nearest 10% bucket — into the issue body and scanning open issues labeled `agent-auto-filed,P0` before filing. A notable gotcha is the "dead funnel" case: when baseline and yesterday are both zero, all stages share the single `funnel:dead` fingerprint so exactly one P0 is filed, fixing a historical bug where the all-zero state silently filed nothing for 60+ days. The agent degrades gracefully — missing `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` or absent funnel data produces a "skipped" report and exit 0, and a missing `GITHUB_TOKEN` still records findings and the markdown report (under `docs/agent-reports/`) but skips filing — while drops between 30% and the threshold are logged as warnings only.

scripts\\agents\\health-smoke.mjs.summary: This script is the "health-smoke" agent: a scheduled Node script (run every 6 hours via GitHub Actions) that executes the full per-role smoke suite against production and writes a pass/fail digest report. Its single `run()` function uses `spawnSync` from `node:child_process` to invoke `apps/api/scripts/smoke-all-roles.mjs` with the `API_BASE` and `WEB_BASE` URLs, then parses the final stdout line for a "Total: N pass, M fail" summary and collects any lines tagged `[FAIL]`. It depends on the sibling module `./_lib.mjs` for `writeReport`, `TODAY`, `isoNow`, and the base-URL constants, which handle persisting the generated Markdown report. The report includes pass/fail counts, the child process exit status, up to 30 failing endpoint rows, and a 40-line output tail, and is written with an hour-of-day suffix so multiple daily runs don't collide. Notable gotchas: the child process has a 240-second timeout, a missing parse match yields `fail = -1` which is surfaced as "UNKNOWN (parse error)" rather than zero, and the script deliberately calls `process.exit(0)` even when smoke tests fail so the workflow still completes and the failure artifact plus history are preserved.

scripts\\agents\\gsc-submitter.mjs.summary: This agent script exists to nudge search engines into re-crawling the site after new URLs ship, rather than waiting for their scheduled fetches: it verifies the live sitemap, then pings Google's sitemap endpoint and submits a batch of URLs to Bing through IndexNow. Its main functions are `verifySitemap()` (fetches `SITEMAP_URL` and counts `<loc>` entries), `pingGoogle()` (GETs `google.com/ping` with the encoded sitemap URL), `pingBing()` (POSTs a JSON payload of key section URLs — home, `/temples`, `/pujas`, `/shlokas`, `/refer` — to `api.indexnow.org`), and `run()`, which assembles a markdown report. It depends on the sibling `_lib.mjs` module for `fetchText`, `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `WEB_BASE`, and `TODAY`, and talks externally to Google, the IndexNow API, and the site's own `sitemap.xml` hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Notably, because Bing deprecated its `/ping` endpoint in 2022, the script routes Bing traffic through IndexNow using a self-issued key hardcoded as a fallback but overridable via the `INDEXNOW_KEY` env var, with the key file served at `/<key>.txt` by Cloudflare Pages so no owner action is required. Results are written to `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-gsc-submitter.md` via `writeReport` and summarized in a shared log via `upsertLog`; any fatal error prints to stderr and exits with code 1.

scripts\\agents\\investor-pipeline.mjs.summary: This is a standalone CLI agent script that generates a dated markdown report, `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-investor-pipeline.md`, containing a curated fundraising target list and personalized pitch drafts for a pre-seed Indian devotional-commerce startup (positioned as a "#2 to Sri Mandir"). It exports nothing; its single `run()` function assembles the report body from hardcoded data and writes it via `writeReport`, imported from the sibling internal module `./_lib.mjs` along with the `TODAY` and `isoNow` helpers — there are no external dependencies beyond Node itself. The report content is built from three static datasets — `ANGELS` (5 named India-focused angels like Kunal Shah and Naval Ravikant with warm-intro paths), `SEED_VCS` (10 funds with cheque sizes and theses), and `STRATEGIC` (Series-A+ targets like Rainmatter and PeakXV) — plus a `PERSONA_PITCH` map holding three pitch templates (`consumerAngel`, `seedVC`, `strategic`) with placeholders like "[bookings last 30d]" meant to be filled in manually. A notable design decision is that everything is hand-curated public information embedded in the source rather than fetched from any API or CRM, so refreshing the list means editing the arrays, not running the script. The generated report also encodes operational process, not just data: a stage-gate checklist with metric thresholds (e.g., 5K MAU and $5K MRR before pre-seed), a pre-raise checklist, a weekly outreach cadence, and cold-email rules. The script is meant to be run directly (`node investor-pipeline.mjs`), exits non-zero on failure, and logs "Investor pipeline refreshed." on success. One gotcha: the pitch templates reference traction numbers that don't exist yet, so the report is a planning artifact rather than a send-ready document.

scripts\\agents\\growth-metrics.mjs.summary: This is a standalone Node CLI agent that generates a daily growth-metrics snapshot: it counts inventory across eight public API surfaces (temples, priests, astrologers, gurukuls, store products, yatra packages, puja types, content), probes the API `/health` endpoint, and writes a markdown report to `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-growth-metrics.md` via `writeReport`. It exports nothing itself; its key internals are the `TRIPWIRES` constant (NRI Day-30 retention, blended NRI CAC, annual:per-puja ratio thresholds), the `safeCount` helper, and the main `run` routine. All shared plumbing comes from the sibling module `./_lib.mjs` — `fetchJson`, `writeReport`, `TODAY`, `isoNow`, and `API_BASE` — and the only live service it talks to is the production API at `API_BASE` under `/api/v1/*`. A notable design choice is that `safeCount` deliberately degrades gracefully: it heuristically extracts counts from varying response shapes (arrays, `total`/`count`/`totalCount` fields, or known list keys like `gurukuls` and `priests`) and records `0` plus an error note rather than throwing. The big gotcha is that authenticated north-star metrics (MAU, MRR, retention) are stubbed as TBD pending an `/admin/metrics` route, so the tripwires are rendered as review reminders only and are not actually evaluated against live data. The report body also embeds static operational guidance — wiring PostHog, Cloudflare Web Analytics, Google Search Console, Plausible, and Sentry — and references `docs/roadmap-archive.md` for the rule that two same-week tripwire breaches trigger a reduction to NRI-only SKUs.

scripts\\agents\\keyword-rank-tracker.mj.summary: This is a standalone Node.js reporting agent that tracks whether `darshya.online` ranks in the top 30 search results for a hardcoded list of ~25 SEO seed keywords (`KEYWORDS`) covering puja booking, temple yatras, and astrology surfaces, emitting a daily Markdown report via `writeReport` from the shared internal module `./_lib.mjs` into `docs/agent-reports/`. Because the Google Search Console API is OAuth-gated and Google SERP scraping requires a paid provider, it deliberately uses the free DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint (`html.duckduckgo.com/html/`) as a no-API-key fallback, parsing organic results with a regex over `result__a` anchors and decoding DDG `uddg` redirect URLs in `rankFor`. Rank history is persisted to `_keyword-rank-tracker-state.json` via `loadState`/`saveState`, trimmed to a 90-day rolling window, and used to compute 24-hour rank deltas for the report's "Movers" table alongside "Top 10 wins" and "Unranked" sections. Notable constraints: requests run sequentially with a 1.2-second polite delay and the keyword list is capped at 30 to stay within free SERP rate limits, and the regex-based HTML scraping is inherently fragile against DuckDuckGo markup changes. The script depends only on Node built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`, global `fetch`) plus the sibling `_lib.mjs` helper, and exits non-zero on unhandled failure so it can run as a scheduled CI/cron job.

scripts\\agents\\marketing\\nri-mix-trac.summary: This script is the engineering scaffold for roadmap item R-Q4-M-013b: a deterministic tracker that computes the NRI (non-resident Indian) share of revenue—NRI revenue over total India+NRI revenue—and classifies it against thresholds of 35% (approaching), 40% (milestone), and 45% (exceeded), writing a dated markdown report to `docs/agent-reports/` via `writeReport` and logging runs via `upsertLog`, both imported from the shared `../_lib.mjs` helper. Its exports are the pure, unit-testable `calculateMix` function (no DB or network) and two SELECT-only SQL templates, `SQL_LAST_30D` and `SQL_LAST_7D`, which aggregate completed rows from the `Booking` table, treating INR-currency amounts as India revenue and USD amounts as NRI revenue converted at a hardcoded 83 INR/USD rate. The script is env-or-noop by design: without `SUPABASE_DIRECT_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL_READONLY`/`DATABASE_URL`) it emits a no-op report with founder-action notes and enablement instructions, and it lazily imports the `pg` Postgres client only when a DB URL exists, so the dependency is never required for noop runs and the free tier is untouched. Notable constraints: PostHog remains the KPI source of truth per the roadmap, so this DB-side read exists solely for cross-validation, and both sources must agree within ±2 percentage points before the 40% milestone is announced externally; monetary values are handled in paise and divided by 100 only for display; the fixed 83 exchange rate will drift from real FX over time; and the NRI classification heuristic (currency-based, with a spec-mandated alternative of `billing_country != 'IN'`) is documented in `docs/marketing/40pct-nri-milestone-spec.md`, which also lists the acquisition levers the report recommends when below threshold.

scripts\\agents\\lead-gen.mjs.summary: This file is a standalone Node script (`run()` invoked at the bottom, no exports) that acts as a daily "lead-gen agent": it counts how many supply-side entities are currently onboarded per category and writes a Markdown scoreboard to `docs/agent-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-lead-gen.md` via the shared `writeReport` helper from `./_lib.mjs`. The hardcoded `CATEGORIES` array defines six lead categories (Temples, Pandits, Astrologers, Gurukuls, Gaushalas, Wellness instructors) with T1/T2/T3 tier targets and, where available, an API endpoint; `countCategory()` queries each endpoint through `fetchJson(`${API_BASE}...`)` and defensively extracts a count from many possible response shapes (`data[]`, `items[]`, named keys like `temples[]` or `priests[]`, or numeric `total`/`count` fields). The generated report ranks the top three categories by gap-to-T1 and recommends running corresponding scraper scripts such as `apps/api/scripts/leads/scrape-temples.ts` against the hardcoded `PRIORITY_CITIES` list of 25 Indian pilgrimage cities, and it embeds a cold-outreach email template plus free-channel notes (Resend, WhatsApp Cloud API, Twilio). Key gotchas: Gaushalas and Wellness instructors have `endpoint: null`, so they always report zero with a `no-public-endpoint` source; and although the header comment claims leads are pulled from a curated CSV and a database when `DATABASE_URL` is set, the code never does either — `readFileSync` and `existsSync` are imported from `node:fs` but unused, meaning the script currently relies entirely on live API counts.

scripts\\agents\\investor-weekly-digest-.summary: This Node script is a Sunday-only (UTC) automation agent that generates the "Darshya" investor weekly digest: it polls the production endpoint `/api/v1/admin/metrics/investor` for real business numbers—MRR, GMV, retention, CAC, NRI mix—computed server-side from Prisma models BookingPayment, Donation, and User, then renders an investor-ready markdown report to `docs/agent-reports/` for the founder to review and forward. It builds on the shared internal helper module `./_lib.mjs` (importing `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, `fetchJson`, `API_BASE`, `TODAY`), authenticates via the `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` env var passed as a URL query token, and uses `node:child_process`'s `execSync` in `gitWeekStats()` to append engineering velocity (commit counts bucketed by feat/fix/perf) to the report. Key helpers include `fetchMetrics()` (15-second `AbortSignal.timeout`, explicit handling of 404/network failures), `placeholderMetrics()` (null-filled fallback), and currency formatters `fmtINR`/`fmtUSD`/`fmtPct` that work in paise/cents minor units and abbreviate to lakhs/thousands. Notable design decisions: the Sunday gate in `isSundayUtc()` can be overridden with `FORCE=1`, and even a skipped run writes a "skipped" report rather than exiting silently; the script is deliberately fail-soft—if the admin metrics route isn't deployed yet it emits a placeholder report with a warning banner instead of erroring red. Status indicators (🟢/🟡/🔴/⚪) are computed against hard-coded Day-90 targets (₹25k MRR, ₹1L GMV, 100 paying users, 15% NRI mix, 35% D7 / 25% D30 retention, CAC under ₹400). Gotchas include the auth token traveling in the query string, and the template's forward references to a Sprint 3 roadmap, since the metrics endpoint it depends on only ships in sub-batch 4.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-drip.mjs.summary: This script is the content source of truth for Darshya's role-based onboarding email drip campaigns: it hardcodes a `SEQUENCES` map of day-offset/subject/body touches for seven roles (devotee, pandit, temple, gaushala, store_owner, astrologer, wellness), then renders them into a markdown report via `writeReport` from the shared `./_lib.mjs` helper (alongside `TODAY` and `isoNow`). Although it exports a `maybeSend` function that posts to the Resend API (`https://api.resend.com/emails`) using `RESEND_API_KEY`, the `run()` entrypoint never calls it — actual delivery is delegated to `apps/api/src/jobs/outreach-cron.ts`, which reads this file's sequences and sends daily at 9:00 IST to users whose `createdAt` matches each day offset. Key operational dependencies are the `RESEND_API_KEY` and `DARSHYA_FROM_EMAIL` env vars, DNS verification for darshya.online on the Resend dashboard, and a Resend webhook receiver at `/api/v1/webhooks/resend` for open/click tracking. A notable gotcha is that `maybeSend` is effectively dead code in this script's flow, silently returning `{ sent: false }` when the API key is absent; also, all marketing copy, pricing, and URLs live inline as string literals, so content edits require a code change rather than a CMS or template store.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-nudge.mjs.summary: This is a 6-hourly cron script that re-engages self-onboard provider leads who stalled in the NEW state, sending differentiated email nudges at three windows (24h, 72h, 7d) with escalating copy defined in the `COPY` map. Its `main()` fetches abandoned-KYC leads from the internal endpoint `/api/v1/admin/ops/kyc-abandoned` (built on `API_BASE` from the sibling module `./_lib.mjs`, authenticated via the `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` env var), then calls `sendEmail()` to deliver messages through the external Resend API (`api.resend.com`) using `RESEND_API_KEY` and `RESEND_FROM`. Deduplication is handled by `loadState()`/`saveState()`, which persist a `leadId:windowKey` map in `_onboarding-nudge-state.json` under `docs/agent-reports` so no lead receives the same window's nudge twice across cron ticks. Each run ends by writing a markdown summary report via `writeReport()` from `_lib.mjs`, with sends throttled by a 300ms sleep between messages. Notable gotchas: the header comment promises WhatsApp nudges but only email is implemented; leads are recorded in state even when the send is skipped for a missing API key or recipient, meaning they will never be retried for that window once the key is configured; and the state file lives in the same directory as published agent reports, so it may be committed alongside them.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\astrolog.summary: This script is the astrologer-role drip campaign runner in the onboarding-v2 agent suite: it generates personalized welcome messages for new astrologer contacts on darshya.online and writes them to a markdown report for manual sending. It builds entirely on the shared `_onboard-lib.mjs` helpers — `loadState`, `filterByRole`, `shouldFire`, `markTouch`, `renderTemplate`, `writeReport`, and `saveState` — and pulls its message copy from the `TEMPLATES` registry in `templates.mjs` under the `astrologer` role. The campaign currently defines a single touch, `day0_welcome`, fired on day 0, with template variables defaulting to `joinUrl: 'https://darshya.online'` plus per-contact name, city, and phone. Notably, the script does not send anything itself: it drafts messages into a dated report (`writeReport`) and explicitly relies on the founder to review and send each one via WhatsApp manually, making this a human-in-the-loop pipeline rather than an automated mailer. It exits cleanly with code 0 and a log line when no contacts are due, avoiding empty reports. One subtlety: `markTouch` is called as each draft is generated, so touches are recorded in state even though `saveState` only runs after the report is written — meaning a crash between drafting and saving could lose the marks, but a successful run always persists state after the report exists.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\run-all..summary: This file is a batch orchestration entry point for the onboarding-v2 agent pipeline: it sequentially executes a per-role onboarding script for each of the seven roles in its hardcoded ROLES list (pundit, temple, astrologer, gaushala, gurukul, wellness, store). It exports nothing; it is meant to be run directly, e.g. as an npm script. Its only dependencies are execFileSync from node:child_process and the sibling scripts it invokes by convention at scripts/agents/onboarding-v2/<role>.mjs. Each child runs with stdio set to inherit, so output streams live to the parent's console rather than being captured. Notably, a failing role does not abort the batch—the script catches the error, records the role name in an errors array, and continues with the remaining roles. At the end it logs a success ratio summary and exits with code 1 if any role failed, making it suitable for CI gating while still attempting every onboarding. A gotcha is that adding a new role requires editing the ROLES constant here in addition to creating the corresponding script file.

scripts\\agents\\marketing\\youtube-cont.summary: This Node.js CLI script (roadmap item R-Q2-M-009) deterministically generates a 4-week YouTube content slate for the Bhaktisetu channel, persisting a markdown report through `writeReport` and logging the run through `upsertLog`, both imported from the shared agent helper `../_lib.mjs` along with `TODAY`. It makes no LLM or YouTube API calls — all output is templated from two rotating seed lists, `HOWTO_PUJAS` (12 how-to-puja topics carrying deity, samagri, and duration) and `TEMPLE_DARSHAN` (8 temples for live-darshan highlights), selected by modular indexing on `(week + idx)` so the plan advances each week without randomness. `buildSlate` assembles, per week, one darshan video (Tuesday), one how-to video (Saturday), and five weekday Shorts cross-posted from Instagram reels (R-Q2-M-004); `buildHowToDescription` and `buildDarshanDescription` emit paste-ready YouTube descriptions that cross-link to bhaktisetu.com puja, darshan, NRI, and 80G-donation pages, while `buildTags` and `buildDarshanTags` generate long-tail SEO tag sets and thumbnail briefs are simple inline strings. The division of labor is explicit in `renderReport`: the agent only produces schedule and copy, the founder records and uploads, and the report ends with a manual verification checklist plus the KPI target of 500 subscribers by end-Q2. The main gotcha is that weekday labels come from fixed `addDays` offsets relative to the run date, so the Tue/Sat cadence assumes the script is launched at the start of a week, and the rotations silently repeat after 12 weeks (pujas) and 8 weeks (temples) since there is no persisted state between runs.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\gaushala.summary: This script is the gaushala-role branch of the onboarding-v2 drip agent: it drafts personalized WhatsApp onboarding messages for contacts tagged as gaushala (cow shelters) and writes them to a dated markdown report for a human to review and send manually. It defines a two-touch schedule in `TOUCHES` — a `day0_welcome` message and a `day7_adopt_a_cow_setup` follow-up — and a `VARS_DEFAULTS` map supplying a hardcoded `joinUrl` of https://darshya.online. All shared machinery comes from the sibling module `_onboard-lib.mjs` (`loadState`, `filterByRole`, `shouldFire`, `renderTemplate`, `markTouch`, `writeReport`, `saveState`), while message copy lives in `TEMPLATES` from `templates.mjs`, keyed by role and touch key. For each gaushala contact it checks `shouldFire` against the persisted state, renders the template with name, city, and phone, and immediately calls `markTouch` so the touch will not re-fire on subsequent runs. Notably, nothing is actually sent: the script is human-in-the-loop by design, exiting quietly with code 0 when no contacts are due, and otherwise emitting a report that embeds contact PII (phone numbers, cities) in fenced code blocks for the founder to copy into WhatsApp. A subtle gotcha is that `markTouch` runs before the report is even written, but since `saveState` only executes on the non-empty path, a crash mid-run would simply leave touches unmarked and eligible next time.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\gurukul..summary: This script is the "gurukul" role's onboarding drip generator in the onboarding-v2 agent suite: it drafts scheduled WhatsApp messages for newly onboarded contacts rather than sending them automatically. It relies on the shared helpers in `_onboard-lib.mjs` (`loadState`, `filterByRole`, `shouldFire`, `markTouch`, `renderTemplate`, `writeReport`, `saveState`) and pulls role-specific copy from `TEMPLATES` in `templates.mjs`. The drip schedule is defined by the `TOUCHES` array with two touches, `day0_welcome` and `day14_admissions_check`, and `shouldFire` gates each one on the contact's elapsed days while `markTouch` records it in persisted state so messages never repeat. Templates are rendered with per-contact variables (name, city, phone) merged over `VARS_DEFAULTS`, which currently just supplies a hardcoded `joinUrl` pointing to `https://darshya.online`. If no contacts are due, the script logs and exits cleanly with code 0; otherwise it emits a dated Markdown report via `writeReport` listing each draft with the contact's phone and city, then saves updated state. The key design decision is human-in-the-loop delivery: the report explicitly states the founder reviews and sends each message manually over WhatsApp, so the script is a drafting tool, not a sender, with no external messaging API dependencies. One gotcha is that `markTouch` runs before the report is written, so a crash between drafting and `saveState` could theoretically be reconciled only via that single state file.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\store.mj.summary: This script is the store-role variant of the onboarding-v2 drip agent: it generates WhatsApp welcome-message drafts for contacts tagged as stores, but deliberately stops short of sending anything. It loads persisted campaign state via loadState from the sibling module _onboard-lib.mjs, narrows it to the 'store' role with filterByRole, and runs a single touch, day0_welcome (day 0), through shouldFire so each contact only receives a given touch once. For every eligible contact it looks up the matching entry in TEMPLATES from templates.mjs and renders it with renderTemplate, merging per-contact fields (name, city, phone) with VARS_DEFAULTS, which currently just supplies the joinUrl pointing at https://darshya.online. Each fired touch is recorded immediately with markTouch, and saveState persists the updated state so re-runs are idempotent. The output is a single markdown report produced by writeReport, containing each draft in a fenced block with the contact's phone and city, explicitly framed for the founder to review and send manually over WhatsApp. A notable gotcha: if no contacts are ready, the script logs and exits 0 without writing a report or saving state, so empty runs leave no artifacts. The main dependencies are the internal helpers in _onboard-lib.mjs and the message copy in templates.mjs; there are no external service calls at all, since actual delivery is a human step.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\_onboard.summary: This module is a shared utility library for the onboarding-v2 agent scripts, providing state persistence and touch-scheduling helpers for automated contact onboarding campaigns. It manages a JSON state file at `docs/agent-reports/_onboarding-fleet-v2-state.json` via `loadState` (which fails safe to an empty `{ lastRun, contacts }` shape on missing or corrupt data) and `saveState` (which stamps `lastRun` before writing). Scheduling logic centers on `shouldFire`, which gates a named touchpoint on both not having fired before and a `daysSince(contact.joinedAt)` threshold, with `markTouch` recording each fired touch with a timestamp; `filterByRole` selects active contacts of a given role, and `isoToday`/`daysSince` supply the date math. For output, `writeReport` creates the `docs/agent-reports` directory if needed and writes a daily dated markdown report named `<date>-onboard-<role>.md`, while `renderTemplate` performs simple `{{variable}}` substitution that leaves unknown placeholders intact rather than erroring. It depends only on `node:fs` and no internal modules, and a notable gotcha is that `markTouch` assumes `state.contacts[contactId]` already exists, so callers must register contacts before marking touches.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\temple.m.summary: This script is the temple-role variant of the onboarding-v2 drip agent: it drafts a fixed three-touch WhatsApp onboarding sequence (day0_welcome, day3_live_darshan_setup, day7_first_puja_invite) for contacts tagged with the `temple` role, apparently for the Darshya product at darshya.online. It builds entirely on the shared `_onboard-lib.mjs` module, using `loadState`, `filterByRole`, `shouldFire`, `markTouch`, `writeReport`, and `saveState` to track which contacts have received which touches, and pulls message bodies from `TEMPLATES` in `templates.mjs`, rendering them with per-contact variables (name, city, phone) plus a default `joinUrl`. Notably, it does not send anything itself: drafts are written to a dated markdown report via `writeReport`, and the founder reviews and sends each message manually through WhatsApp, making this a human-in-the-loop pipeline. Duplicate sends are prevented by persisting touch state with `markTouch` and `saveState` after each run, and the script exits cleanly with a log line when no contacts are due for a touch. There are no external services or libraries involved beyond Node's console and process.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\wellness.summary: This script is the wellness-role drip agent for the onboarding-v2 pipeline: it drafts day-0 welcome messages for new wellness contacts and writes them to a markdown report for manual sending. It pulls shared helpers from `_onboard-lib.mjs` (`loadState`, `saveState`, `filterByRole`, `shouldFire`, `markTouch`, `writeReport`, `renderTemplate`) and message text from `TEMPLATES` in `templates.mjs`, then iterates contacts filtered to the `wellness` role, checks whether each touch in `TOUCHES` (currently only `day0_welcome`) is due, renders the template with per-contact vars (name, city, phone) plus `VARS_DEFAULTS` (notably the hardcoded `joinUrl` https://darshya.online), and records each fired touch via `markTouch` to prevent re-sends. Rather than sending anything itself, it writes a dated report through `writeReport` and explicitly expects the founder to review and send each draft via WhatsApp manually, exiting early with a log line when no contacts are ready. State persistence is handled by `saveState` after the report is written, so the drip cadence is driven entirely by the shared library's `shouldFire` day-offset logic — adding new touches means appending to the `TOUCHES` array and adding a matching entry under `TEMPLATES.wellness`, since a touch with no template is silently skipped.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\pundit.m.summary: This script generates the scheduled WhatsApp onboarding drip for "pundit" (priest) contacts on the Darshya platform, producing draft messages rather than sending anything itself. It loads shared campaign state via `loadState` from `_onboard-lib.mjs`, narrows it with `filterByRole` to `ROLE` 'pundit', and walks a fixed `TOUCHES` schedule — day0_welcome, day1_aadhaar, day3_first_puja_sim, day7_video_proof_tut, day14_nps — using `shouldFire` to decide which touches are due for each contact. For due touches it renders the matching entry from `TEMPLATES` (in `templates.mjs`) via `renderTemplate`, merging `VARS_DEFAULTS` (darshya.online URLs for joining, Aadhaar KYC, and the video-proof tutorial) with per-contact name, city, and phone, then records the touch with `markTouch` and persists via `saveState`. The design is deliberately human-in-the-loop: output is a markdown digest written by `writeReport` that the founder reviews and sends manually through WhatsApp. It exits 0 without saving when no contacts are due, making it safe for cron/CI runs. A notable gotcha is that touches lacking a matching template key are silently skipped, so drift between the `TOUCHES` schedule and `TEMPLATES` won't surface as an error.

scripts\\agents\\onboarding-v2\\template.summary: This file is the template library for the onboarding-v2 agent, exporting a single `TEMPLATES` constant that maps each Darshya partner role — `pundit`, `temple`, `astrologer`, `gaushala`, `gurukul`, `wellness`, `store` — to a sequence of timed touchpoints written as Hinglish WhatsApp-style messages. Touchpoint keys follow a `day{N}_{event}` convention (`day0_welcome`, `day1_aadhaar`, `day3_first_puja_sim`, `day7_video_proof_tut`, `day14_nps`), which a downstream scheduler presumably matches against to pick the right message for each day of the journey. Each template is a plain string with double-brace placeholders (`{{name}}`, `{{city}}`, `{{phone}}`, `{{joinUrl}}`, `{{aadhaarGateUrl}}`, `{{videoProofTutUrl}}`) meant to be interpolated by a caller — the file itself has zero imports, no rendering logic, and no external dependencies. The `pundit` role carries the full 14-day arc (Aadhaar KYC nudge, demo puja assignment, video-proof tutorial, NPS survey), while `astrologer`, `wellness`, and `store` get only a day-0 welcome, so consumers must tolerate missing touchpoints. The copy hardcodes operational policy — payout gated on Aadhaar KYC ("business rule #4") and mandatory per-puja video proof ("business rule #1") — and deep-links into role portals like `/priest`, `/temple-portal/live-darshan` (offering YouTube Live or Amazon IVS as streaming options), `/gaushala-portal/cows`, and `/gurukul/admissions`. Per the header comment, the founder reviews and sends each message manually, so these are human-approved drafts rather than automated sends. Gotchas: the declared `{{city}}` and `{{phone}}` variables are currently unused by any template, and the "business rule" references are informal inline strings rather than links to any rules module.

scripts\\agents\\outreach-uk-pandits.mjs.summary: This script is a deterministic draft generator for Darshya's UK pandit recruitment campaign (requirement R-Q3-S-006): it produces personalized first-touch emails to UK Hindu institutions but deliberately never sends anything, since institutional outreach must come from the founder's personal account after a cold-blast incident previously got the brand flagged by an ISKCON UK admin. The main flow in `main()` calls `loadRecipients()`, which reads a JSON recipient list from `UK_PANDIT_RECIPIENTS_PATH` (defaulting to `docs/supply/uk-pandit-recipients.json`) and falls back to the built-in `DEFAULT_INSTITUTIONAL_POOL` of six public channels — Hindu Council UK, ISKCON Bhaktivedanta Manor, BAPS Neasden, and Leicester/Birmingham mandirs — following an env-or-noop pattern. `buildOutreachDraft()` assembles each subject and body, branching on whether the recipient is an umbrella body or a temple, and injects hardcoded India-network case studies from `pandit3CaseStudies()` plus founder contact details. Every recipient address is a `{{VERIFY_FOUNDER_*}}` placeholder token, which acts as a forced manual review gate: `main()` scans all drafts, collects the unresolved tokens, and lists them in the report alongside a per-city distribution (London, Birmingham, Leicester) and a founder checklist mandating 7-day spacing between touches and no auto-follow-up. Its only internal dependency is `./_lib.mjs` (`writeReport`, `TODAY`, `isoNow`, `WEB_BASE`), which it uses to emit a markdown report via `writeReport('uk-pandit-outreach', md)`; it uses Node's `fs`/`path` and deliberately makes zero Resend calls, keeping it free-tier. A notable gotcha is that the case-study figures and claim of ~140 UK households are hardcoded marketing copy, so the drafts can go stale, and the script's only real output is a report file — nothing enforces the send cadence or CRM logging it recommends.

scripts\\agents\\pr-outreach.mjs.summary: This standalone Node.js ESM script is the PR outreach agent for Darshya (darshya.online), generating a weekly markdown press kit that pairs a ranked list of ten Indian media outlets with three ready-to-send pitch angles. Its only dependency is the sibling internal module `_lib.mjs`, from which it imports `writeReport`, `TODAY`, and `isoNow`; it calls no external APIs or libraries. All content is hardcoded: the `OUTLETS` array names specific journalists at publications like YourStory, Inc42, TechCrunch India, and The Ken with their best-fit story angle, while `PITCH_ANGLES` defines three hooks — NRI pricing economics, a gurukul admissions marketplace, and video proof of puja bookings — each listing proof metrics that must exist before pitching. The `run()` function assembles these into a markdown report containing an outlet table, angle details, a cold pitch email template, a Mon/Wed/Fri outreach cadence, free tools (HARO, Qwoted, Twitter advanced search), and a founder-owned content schedule, then persists it via `writeReport('pr-outreach', body)`. A key gotcha is that the script fetches no live data, so outlet fit and the "required proof" figures are editorial assertions rather than measured results, and the angles deliberately position against competitor Sri Mandir (AppsForBharat), claiming it lacks USD billing for NRI users. Failures are handled by a top-level catch that logs the error and exits with code 1.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\cfo.mjs.summary: This script auto-generates the weekly CFO advisory markdown consumed by the roadmap Decision Agent. It relies entirely on the shared sibling module `_cxo-lib.mjs` for data access (loadItems, loadKpiCache, loadDeptDoc) and aggregation helpers (filterItemsByOwner, statusCounts, topNByRevenueHourRatio, kpisForMetrics, isoWeek), then persists output via writeAdvisory under the ROLE constant 'cfo'. The buildAdvisory function filters roadmap items owned by the CFO, summarizes their status counts, ranks the top 5 ready-to-ship items by revenue-per-hour ratio, lists founder-blocked items, and pulls live KPI values limited to finance-relevant metrics in RELEVANT_KPI_METRICS (MRR_INR, ARR_INR, runway_months, cf_burn_pct, gh_min_pct, anthropic_tokens_month). It also embeds the first 30 lines of the department doctrine doc 03-cfo.md and emits up to three recommended next-cycle prompts instructing the Decision Agent to spawn a cfo-agent on specific items. Notable design choices: prioritization is purely revenue_impact.amount_inr divided by est_hours, stale KPI cache entries are flagged rather than excluded, and every empty section renders an explicit fallback message (including guidance to run the orchestrator's first cycle when no KPIs exist), so the advisory degrades gracefully rather than failing.

scripts\\agents\\review-harvest.mjs.summary: This script is a daily "review-harvest" agent that scans public conversation surfaces for mentions of the product (queries like "darshya", "puja booking app", "live darshan online", "sri mandir alternative") so the founder gets a pulse on where it's being discussed and who to thank or respond to. It runs two fetchers, `hnSearch` against the HN Algolia API (`hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search`) and `redditSearch` against Reddit's `search.json` endpoint, both free and unauthenticated, then merges results through `dedupe` (keyed on URL), sorts newest-first, and the `run` function renders a Markdown table (capped at 50 rows) plus canned action items. It depends on the shared internal helper module `./_lib.mjs` for `fetchJson`, `fetchText`, `writeReport`, `upsertLog`, and the `TODAY` constant, writing output via `writeReport('review-harvest', md)` and recording a one-line `mentions=N` summary through `upsertLog`. Notable gotchas: the header comment lists Indie Hackers as a source but no fetcher for it is implemented, and it claims cross-run deduplication via the `_review-harvest-log.md` tail while the code only dedupes within a single run, so repeat mentions reappear daily. Reddit failures are tolerated silently (any non-200 status or unparseable body yields an empty list), and the empty-state copy normalizes zero results so the report is always written rather than failing.

scripts\\agents\\referral-nudge.mjs.summary: This standalone scheduled agent script (run daily at 07:00 IST) finds users whose first Darshya booking landed 7–8 days ago and emails each a referral nudge containing a deep link to `/refer` (with UTM params) and a 10%-off offer for the referred friend. It has no exports; its main internal pieces are `main` (orchestration), `sendEmail` (posts to the Resend API at api.resend.com), `emailHtml` and `escapeHtml` (template and sanitization), and `loadState`/`saveState` (dedup persistence). It builds on the shared `./_lib.mjs` module for `writeReport`, `TODAY`, `isoNow`, `API_BASE`, and `WEB_BASE`, and depends on the backend endpoint `/api/v1/admin/ops/recent-first-bookings` authenticated via a `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` query parameter, plus the external Resend email service via `RESEND_API_KEY` and `RESEND_FROM`. Deduplication is per `user_id`, recorded in `docs/agent-reports/_referral-nudge-state.json`, guaranteeing a user receives the nudge at most once. A notable gotcha: state is marked sent whenever `sendEmail` returns `ok` **or** `skipped`, so if `RESEND_API_KEY` is unset the affected users are still recorded as sent and will never be retried. The script degrades gracefully — if `CRON_AUTH_TOKEN` is missing or the feed fetch fails (15s `AbortSignal.timeout`), it writes a markdown report via `writeReport` and exits without error, throttles sends with a 300 ms delay, and truncates the report's send log to 30 entries.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\cmo.mjs.summary: This script generates the weekly CMO (Chief Marketing Officer) advisory report for a multi-agent roadmap system, producing a markdown digest that a "Decision Agent" consumes to decide what to work on next. Its single internal function, `buildAdvisory()`, assembles the report: it loads all roadmap items via `loadItems()`, filters to items owned by the `cmo` role with `filterItemsByOwner()`, computes status counts, picks the top 5 ready-to-ship items ranked by revenue-per-hour ratio (`topNByRevenueHourRatio`), lists founder-blocked items, and pulls live values for marketing KPIs (`MAU`, `organic_traffic_7d`, `indexed_pages`, `social_followers_twitter`, `posthog_signup_funnel`, `press_hits_count`) from a cache via `kpisForMetrics()`. All data access is delegated to the shared sibling module `_cxo-lib.mjs`, which abstracts item loading, the KPI cache, department docs (`02-cmo.md`), and the `writeAdvisory()` persistence call; the script has no external library dependencies and runs as a top-level executable that logs the output path. Notable choices include: the report embeds only the first 30 lines of the department doctrine doc, flags stale KPI values, formats revenue in INR with the `en-IN` locale, and emits graceful fallback text when no items are ready or no KPIs are cached yet. The "Recommended next-cycle prompts" section caps suggestions at three items and defers to the founder when the DAG is fully blocked or in flight, making the output both a status snapshot and a machine-oriented prompt source for downstream agents.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\cpo.mjs.summary: This file is the CPO variant of a family of weekly CXO advisory generators: it produces a markdown briefing that a downstream "Decision Agent" reads to decide which roadmap work to spawn next. Its single exported behavior is the side-effecting script body built around `buildAdvisory()`, which loads roadmap items via `loadItems()`, filters them to the `cpo` owner with `filterItemsByOwner()`, and summarizes them with `statusCounts()`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio()` (top 5 ready-to-ship by revenue-per-hour, rendered in INR), and a list of items carrying a `founder_blocker` flag. It also pulls cached KPI values for `conversion_rate`, `retention_d30`, `nps_score`, and `feature_adoption_rate` via `kpisForMetrics()`, and embeds the first 30 lines of the department doctrine doc `04-cpo.md` for context. All heavy lifting comes from the sibling internal module `./_cxo-lib.mjs` (`loadKpiCache`, `loadDeptDoc`, `writeAdvisory`, `isoWeek`); there are no external service calls—it operates entirely on local cached data files. Notable design choices: the output is explicitly marked "Founder override OK," recommended next-cycle prompts are capped at the top 3 ready items and degrade to "defer to founder" when nothing is ready, stale KPIs are flagged inline, and an empty KPI cache tells the reader to run the orchestrator's first cycle.

scripts\\agents\\pr-review.mjs.summary: This CI script (roadmap item P4.21) performs automated AI code review on pull requests: it fetches the PR diff from the GitHub REST API, sends it to an LLM through the Blackbox proxy using the pinned open-source model blackboxai/z-ai/glm-5.2, and posts the structured verdict back as a PR comment. Its main pieces are the gh() helper for authenticated GitHub GETs, reviewDiff() which posts to the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint with a SYSTEM_PROMPT checklist (secret-egress, render-impact, prisma-footguns, free-tier-cost, commit-msg, tests) that mirrors the darshya-code-review skill so CI review matches local review, plus formatComment() which renders the PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED markdown table and postComment() which publishes it. The file is deliberately self-contained and does not reuse roadmap/_anthropic-client.mjs, because that module is locked to opus-4.7 which 403-rejects on Blackbox's open-source-only endpoint (the reason roadmap-orchestrator CI was failing); it uses only global fetch and node:fs, though the readFileSync import is actually unused. Configuration comes entirely from env vars — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_BLACKBOX_PROXY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, PR_NUMBER, GH_REPOSITORY — with missing config exiting code 2 to skip quietly. The central design decision is that the script always exits 0: the review is advisory and the posted comment is the gate, so even a FAIL verdict, a model 403, or a thrown exception produces an informational comment rather than a failed workflow that would block unrelated PR checks. Robustness gotchas include truncating diffs to 120,000 characters, lenient JSON extraction from the model response (first "{" to last "}"), mapping 403s to an UNVERIFIED verdict, and a redundant discarded GET inside postComment(). The checklist itself encodes project-specific knowledge worth preserving: known pre-existing test failures (canada-pandit-prospector.test.ts, nri-fb-ads-pack.test.mjs, twitter-thread-pack.test.mjs) must not be flagged as regressions, and Prisma migrations must avoid CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and use DIRECT_URL rather than the pooled connection.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\cs.mjs.summary: This script is the Customer Success (CS) member of a CXO advisory-agent suite: it auto-generates a weekly markdown advisory that a downstream "Decision Agent" reads to plan the next work cycle. It relies entirely on the shared helper module `./_cxo-lib.mjs`, importing `loadItems`, `loadKpiCache`, `loadDeptDoc`, `writeAdvisory`, `filterItemsByOwner`, `statusCounts`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio`, `kpisForMetrics`, and `isoWeek`, so all data access and output writing are centralized there. The `buildAdvisory()` function filters roadmap items owned by the `cs` role, summarizes their status counts, selects the top five ready-to-ship items ranked by revenue-per-hour ratio, lists any items carrying a `founder_blocker` flag, and pulls cached live KPIs restricted to `open_tickets`, `p50_response_hours`, and `nps_last_30d`. It also embeds the first 30 lines of the department doctrine file `07-cs.md` so the Decision Agent sees role context alongside metrics. The generated report ends with up to three recommended next-cycle prompts that suggest spawning a `cs-agent` on the highest-leverage items, including each item's KPI current/target values. Notable design choices: the advisory explicitly states "Founder override OK," empty sections degrade to human-readable fallback messages (e.g. deferring to the founder when nothing is ready), and KPI staleness is surfaced via a `STALE` marker rather than filtered out. Running the script writes the advisory via `writeAdvisory('cs', ...)` and logs the output path to the console.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\hr.mjs.summary: This file is the HR-seat advisory generator in the CXO agent suite: it produces a weekly markdown briefing that a downstream Decision Agent reads to decide what to work on next. It delegates all data access to the shared sibling module `_cxo-lib.mjs`, using `loadItems`, `loadKpiCache`, and `loadDeptDoc` for inputs and helpers like `filterItemsByOwner`, `statusCounts`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio`, and `kpisForMetrics` to shape them, then persists output via `writeAdvisory('hr', ...)`. The generated report covers a status snapshot of items owned by the `hr` role, the top five ready-to-ship items ranked by revenue-per-hour (with INR revenue impact, estimated hours, and priority), any items carrying a `founder_blocker` flag, live KPI values restricted to `contractor_count` and `contractor_jds_drafted`, the first 30 lines of the doctrine file `06-talent.md`, and up to three suggested prompts telling the Decision Agent to spawn an hr-agent on specific items. Notable behaviors include graceful empty-state fallbacks — the KPI section explicitly instructs running the orchestrator's first cycle when the cache is empty, and the recommendations defer to the founder when everything is in flight or DAG-blocked — plus a header noting that founder override of the advisory is acceptable. The script is side-effect driven: it runs `buildAdvisory()` immediately at import time and logs the written path.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\legal.mjs.summary: This script is the "legal" instance of a family of per-department CXO advisory generators under scripts/agents/roadmap/cxo; it produces a weekly markdown briefing that a downstream "Decision Agent" reads to decide which legal roadmap work to spawn next. It delegates all data access and formatting to the shared sibling module _cxo-lib.mjs, importing loadItems, loadKpiCache, loadDeptDoc, filterItemsByOwner, statusCounts, topNByRevenueHourRatio, kpisForMetrics, isoWeek, and writeAdvisory. The buildAdvisory function filters roadmap items to those owned by the 'legal' role, computes status counts, picks the top five ready-to-ship items ranked by revenue-per-hour ratio, collects founder-blocked items, and pulls live KPI values for the legal-specific metrics dpdp_compliance_score and contracts_signed. It also embeds the first 30 lines of the department doctrine file 08-legal.md directly into the report. The generated markdown ends with recommended next-cycle prompts instructing the Decision Agent to spawn a legal-agent on the top three ready items, with explicit fallbacks when nothing is ready, no KPIs are cached, or nothing is blocked. Notable details: output is marked auto-generated and founder-overridable, revenue figures are formatted in INR with Indian locale grouping, stale KPI cache entries are flagged, and the script's only side effects are the writeAdvisory call and a console log of the output path.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\it.mjs.summary: This script is the IT-role advisory generator in a CXO agent pipeline: it produces a weekly markdown brief ("IT Advisory") that a downstream Decision Agent reads to decide which work to spawn next. It exports nothing itself; its single entry point is `buildAdvisory()`, which assembles the report, and the module's top-level side effect calls `writeAdvisory(ROLE, ...)` to persist it and logs the output path. All heavy lifting is delegated to the shared sibling module `./_cxo-lib.mjs`, from which it imports `loadItems`, `loadKpiCache`, `loadDeptDoc`, `writeAdvisory`, `filterItemsByOwner`, `statusCounts`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio`, `kpisForMetrics`, and `isoWeek`; it has no external library dependencies. The report filters roadmap items to those owned by the `it` role, summarizes status counts, ranks the top 5 ready-to-ship items by revenue-per-hour ratio (formatted in INR), lists founder-blocked items, and pulls live KPIs restricted to the hardcoded `RELEVANT_KPI_METRICS` set (`uptime_24h`, `render_hours_pct`, `sentry_open_p0`). It also embeds the first 30 lines of the department doctrine file `09-it.md` verbatim and ends with up to three recommended next-cycle prompts instructing the Decision Agent to spawn an "it-agent" on specific item IDs. Notable gotchas: the script is purely side-effect driven (running it writes a file immediately), it degrades gracefully with placeholder text when no items are ready or no KPIs are cached, and the KPI list, role constant, and dept doc filename are hardcoded, so each CXO role presumably has its own near-duplicate script.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\cto.mjs.summary: This executable Node.js script generates the weekly CTO advisory markdown document for a multi-agent roadmap system, producing a snapshot that a downstream "Decision Agent" reads to plan the next work cycle. It builds the report via `buildAdvisory()`, which pulls roadmap items through `loadItems()`, filters them to the `cto` role with `filterItemsByOwner()`, computes status tallies via `statusCounts()`, ranks the top five ready-to-ship items by revenue-per-hour using `topNByRevenueHourRatio()`, and lists any items carrying a `founder_blocker` flag. All data access is delegated to the shared sibling module `_cxo-lib.mjs` (including `loadKpiCache`, `loadDeptDoc`, `kpisForMetrics`, `isoWeek`, and the `writeAdvisory` sink), so this file is essentially a role-specific template wired over that library. The advisory embeds live KPI values for an engineering-focused metric set (`commits7d`, `open_p0_bugs`, `tests_pass_pct`, `deploy_fail_rate7d`, plus CSP-nonce and Razorpay verification coverage flags), marking stale entries, and appends the first 30 lines of the department doctrine doc `01-cto.md` for context. Notable gotchas: the script runs at import time with no exports, revenue is hardcoded to INR formatting, the KPI section degrades gracefully if the orchestrator hasn't populated the cache yet ("run orchestrator first cycle"), and the closing recommendations cap at three prompts derived from the top-five ready list, deferring to the founder when nothing is unblocked.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\run-all.m.summary: This file is an orchestration script that runs the full suite of CXO advisory roadmap generators in one pass. It iterates over the ROLES list (cto, cfo, cmo, cpo, sales, talent, cs, legal, it, hr) and synchronously executes each role's corresponding script (e.g., `scripts/agents/roadmap/cxo/cto.mjs`) via `execFileSync` from `node:child_process`, streaming output directly to the parent console with `stdio: 'inherit'`. Rather than aborting on the first failure, it catches per-role errors into an `errors` array, warns, and continues, then exits with code 1 at the end if any role failed — a fail-late pattern suited to batch report generation. After the runs, it uses `isoWeek()` imported from the sibling module `_cxo-lib.mjs` to locate the current week's output directory under `docs/roadmap/advisory/`, and if that directory exists, writes an `index.md` linking to every generated Markdown file (excluding the index itself) with uppercased role labels and a generation timestamp. Its only dependencies are Node built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:child_process`) and the internal `_cxo-lib.mjs` helper. Notable gotchas: execution is strictly sequential (no parallelism), the index is silently skipped if the week directory doesn't exist, and the final log reports a succeeded/total count so partial failures are visible even when the process exits nonzero.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\item-kill.mjs.summary: This CLI script marks a roadmap item as "killed" and records the aftermath for the docs/roadmap system. Invoked as `item-kill <itemId> <reason>`, it recursively walks `docs/roadmap/items` (via the internal `walk` helper), parses each Markdown file's YAML frontmatter with `js-yaml`, and rewrites the matching item with `status: 'killed'` plus `killed_at`, `killed_reason`, and `updated_at` timestamps while preserving the Markdown body. It simultaneously scans all other items' `depends_on` arrays to build a list of downstream items blocked by the kill, then writes a human-readable alert report to `docs/roadmap/_alerts/item-killed-<itemId>.md` summarizing the reason and the blocked dependents. It depends only on Node's `fs`/`path` built-ins and the external `js-yaml` library, operating purely on local files with no network or service calls. Notable gotchas: YAML parse errors are silently swallowed via an empty catch, the script exits with code 1 if the item ID isn't found, and the reason defaults to 'no reason given' if omitted.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\sales.mjs.summary: This script is the sales-role CXO advisory generator: it auto-produces a weekly markdown brief that a downstream "Decision Agent" reads to decide which sales work to spawn next, and it runs for side effects only (no exports — it immediately calls `buildAdvisory()`, persists the result via `writeAdvisory(ROLE, ...)`, and logs the output path). All heavy lifting is delegated to the sibling internal module `./_cxo-lib.mjs`, from which it imports `loadItems`, `loadKpiCache`, `loadDeptDoc`, `filterItemsByOwner`, `statusCounts`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio`, `kpisForMetrics`, `isoWeek`, and `writeAdvisory`; there are no external library or network dependencies, only local data files and the department doctrine doc `05-sales.md`. The generated report contains an owned-items status snapshot, a top-5 "ready-to-ship" list ranked by revenue-per-hour ratio, a founder-blocked items list, live KPI values for the sales-specific metrics `verified_pandits_count`, `verified_temples_count`, `verified_astrologers_count`, and `iskcon_loi_status`, the first 30 lines of the department doctrine, and up to three recommended next-cycle prompts formatted as "spawn sales-agent on \<item\>" instructions. Notable design choices: work selection is explicitly optimized by revenue impact divided by estimated hours rather than raw priority, KPI entries can be flagged STALE by the cache layer, and the script degrades gracefully with placeholder text when no items are ready, no KPIs are cached, or nothing is founder-blocked. The header notes founder override is acceptable, signaling this advisory is a recommendation rather than an enforced plan.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\talent.mj.summary: This script auto-generates the weekly markdown advisory for the TALENT "CXO" role (hiring/contractors), which is consumed downstream by the Decision Agent to plan the next work cycle. Its single entry point, buildAdvisory, pulls roadmap items, a KPI cache, and the department doctrine file 06-talent.md via helpers from the shared sibling module _cxo-lib.mjs, then filters items owned by the talent role, tallies their status counts, and renders a fixed report template that writeAdvisory persists before the script logs the output path. The report highlights the top 5 ready-to-ship items ranked by revenue-per-hour (via topNByRevenueHourRatio), founder-blocked items, live values for the KPI metrics contractor_count and first_hire_trigger_met, the first 30 lines of the doctrine doc, and suggested prompts telling the Decision Agent to spawn a talent-agent on the top 3 candidates. All data access and formatting utilities (loadItems, loadKpiCache, loadDeptDoc, filterItemsByOwner, statusCounts, kpisForMetrics, isoWeek) live in _cxo-lib.mjs, so this file is one of presumably several thin per-role variants with no direct external service calls. Notable quirks: revenue is hard-coded to INR with en-IN locale formatting, priority display assumes P-prefixed strings stripped via slice(1), stale KPI cache entries are flagged inline, and the template emits graceful fallback text when no items are ready or no KPIs have been cached yet.

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\cxo\\_cxo-lib..summary: This module is a shared utility library for the CXO-level roadmap advisory agents, providing common helpers for loading roadmap data and writing weekly advisory reports. It builds on `../_lib.mjs` (importing `walk`, `parseFrontmatter`, and the `ITEMS_ROOT`/`ROADMAP_ROOT` path constants) and uses only Node.js built-ins (`node:fs`, `node:path`), with no external service dependencies. Key exports include `isoWeek` (ISO-8601 week labels like `2024-W07` used to bucket output), `loadItems` (walks `ITEMS_ROOT` and parses frontmatter from every item file, tagging each with a normalized `_file` path), `loadKpiCache` (reads `_kpi-cache.json` under `ROADMAP_ROOT`, tolerating a missing or corrupt file), and `loadDeptDoc` (reads department markdown from `docs/company`). For analysis it offers `filterItemsByOwner`, `statusCounts`, `topNByRevenueHourRatio` (ranks planned, agent-assignable, non-founder-blocked items whose dependencies are all `verified` by revenue-per-hour), and `kpisForMetrics` (suffix-matches metric names against colon-delimited KPI cache keys). Finally, `writeAdvisory` persists a role's report to `ROADMAP_ROOT/advisory/<iso-week>/<role>.md`, creating directories as needed. Notable gotchas: `loadItems` silently swallows parse errors per file, `topNByRevenueHourRatio` treats a dependency as satisfied only when the depended item's status is exactly `verified`, and `kpisForMetrics` returns at most one entry per metric (the first key ending in `:<metric>`).

scripts\\agents\\roadmap\\orchestrator-p.summary: This file is a small command-line utility in the roadmap agent tooling that pauses or resumes the roadmap orchestrator by flipping a single boolean flag, `orchestratorPaused`, inside the JSON state file `docs/roadmap/_budget-snapshot.json`. It exports nothing; it is executed directly as a script (`orchestrator-pause <true|false>`), taking one positional argument from `process.argv` and exiting with code 1 plus a usage message unless the argument is exactly the string `true` or `false`. Its only dependency is the Node.js built-in `node:fs` module, using `readFileSync` and `writeFileSync` — there are no external libraries or services involved. The implementation reads the entire budget snapshot, mutates the one key, and rewrites the file with two-space pretty-printing, preserving all other fields. Notable gotchas: the snapshot path is relative, so the script must be run from the repository root; the file is fully overwritten rather than patched; and there is no locking or atomic-write handling, so concurrent invocations could race. It presumably pairs with whatever roadmap orchestrator process reads `_budget-snapshot.json` to decide whether to run.
