Each world pairs a 3D "jharokha diorama" image panel (background wash, photograph, and frame ring on separate CSS-perspective planes) with an editorial column showing a Devanagari glyph, English label, descriptor, and a `next/link` CTA, with world metadata and per-category accent colors defined in the `WORLDS` array and the `World` type. Its only dependencies are React hooks, `next/link`, the `ArrowRight` icon from `lucide-react`, and the internal image resolver helpers `getTempleHero`, `getHeroImage`, `getContentImage`, and `getImage` from `../../lib/images`. Key design decisions: the scroll wheel is never hijacked — scroll position is read via a passive, rAF-throttled listener and only transform/opacity are written imperatively to the DOM (kept in refs, never React state) so animation stays on the compositor at 60fps. Hydration safety is handled by rendering byte-identical markup on server and first client render (panel 0 visible, others at opacity 0), then flipping to centered layout and activating the 3D scene only after mount via a `mounted` state and `liveRef`. Users with `prefers-reduced-motion` keep the inert static shape with the first world fully readable, and performance guardrails include lazy/async-decoded ~1280px images, at most three composited layers per panel, and aria-hidden/tabIndex management so inactive panels stay accessible to SEO but out of keyboard flow.

tests\\e2e\\provider-payouts.spec.ts.summary: This Playwright spec provides live end-to-end smoke coverage for the unified provider-payout system (Phase 2), verifying that the payout API routes exist on the deployed backend rather than exercising full authenticated flows. Using `@playwright/test`, the first test probes four endpoints — `GET /api/v1/payouts/balance`, `GET /api/v1/payouts/my`, `POST /api/v1/payouts/request`, and `GET /api/v1/admin/bookings/payout-requests` — and asserts each returns anything except 404, treating 401/403 as proof the route is live behind auth. The second test navigates to the provider-facing `/payouts` page and accepts either the rendered page or an `AuthGuard` login redirect as a pass, failing only on 5xx or a crash. The API base URL comes from the `E2E_API_BASE` environment variable, defaulting to the production `https://api.darshya.online`, with a `/health` probe guarding the endpoint checks. Notable design choices: tests self-skip via `test.skip` when the API or site is unavailable, and the full payout lifecycle (request → admin process → paid) is intentionally omitted because it requires a real provider account with verified KYC and E2E credentials that may not exist. This makes the suite a deployment-verification canary rather than a functional test of payout logic.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Gaushala Manager Portal
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Role-gated dashboard shell for cow-shelter managers: the layout wraps every child page in a client-side AuthGuard (allowedRoles=['gaushala_manager']) and an off-canvas-below-lg sidebar whose CowIcon is still an empty placeholder span. The dashboard fetches /gaushala-portal/dashboard and /provider-kyc and deliberately does NOT skip demo tokens (P0 #AP-07 — skipping left demo managers on zeroed stats and masked backend bugs); the profile page reuses the dashboard payload instead of a dedicated profile GET, converts empty strings to undefined on PATCH, and sends users to /provider/kyc (a provider-portal route) for documents. Volunteers does full refetch after every mutation and relies on browser confirm(); messages is a thin wrapper over the shared Inbox component with role="provider".

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Static SEO Content Hubs
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Four content hubs (Gita's 18 chapters, 10 Hindu philosophies, 12 Hindu symbols, 12 Jyotirlingas) sharing one architecture: a lib/* data module is the single source of truth, rendered as index + [slug] pages with daily ISR and JSON-LD injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Inconsistency to know: gita and jyotirlinga use generateStaticParams + dynamicParams=false (route set locked at build, unknown slugs 404), while philosophies and symbols omit generateStaticParams and render on demand. Gotchas: the gita index builds Tailwind classes by dynamic interpolation (border-${sec.color}-200) which static extraction will purge, and gita's JSON-LD datePublished is a hardcoded '2026-05-27' string that never tracks content changes.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Help Center
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Static support directory plus prerendered multilingual articles. The /help search input is purely decorative — as a server component with no handlers, typing does nothing, and category links just route to /support/faq?q=<question>. The articles page prerenders one route per entry from lib/help-articles with hreflang alternates matched by slug across languages, and renders content through a hand-rolled minimal markdown pipeline (escape HTML first, then only headings/lists/bold/links) injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML — safe only for trusted in-repo content. Edge runtime is deliberately avoided because @opennextjs/cloudflare needs the Node runtime via nodejs_compat.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Marketing Landing Pages
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Standalone conversion pages. /hi is the Hindi landing page whose feature cards deliberately link to canonical English routes (/darshan, /pujas, ...) rather than fabricating untranslated /hi/* paths — an explicit SEO decision — with hreflang alternates to sibling locales. /launch supports a Product Hunt launch; its only interactivity is the shared EmailCapture component rendered with source='launch-nri' for lead attribution.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Global Error Boundary
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: App Router global-error.tsx: because it replaces the root layout during a fatal crash it must render its own <html> and <body>, so ALL styling is inline — Tailwind/global CSS cannot be trusted to load in this state. On mount it reports the error to Sentry (initSentryBrowser + captureBrowserException from lib/sentry) tagged with the Next.js digest, which is also shown in monospace for support. Kept deliberately dependency-light so the error page itself is unlikely to fail.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Thin server page / client component split
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Convention across the gurukul routes: page.tsx stays a server component solely because client components cannot export metadata, awaits the params Promise (Next.js 15 style), and delegates every bit of interactivity to a sibling *Client.tsx. When looking for behavior, always read the Client file — the page.tsx files contain no logic by design.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Client-side auth & API base URL resolution
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: All authenticated browser code pulls session.accessToken from useAuth (lib/auth-context) and sends it as a Bearer token; route protection (AuthGuard allowedRoles) runs client-side, never as a server check, and unauthenticated users see a sign-in prompt rather than a redirect. Two competing base-URL strategies coexist: API_BASE_URL imported from lib/api-config (gaushala-portal, gift) versus reading NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL with a hardcoded https://api.darshya.online fallback and trailing-slash strip (gurukuls, gurukul-portal) — changing one does not affect the other.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Graceful degradation in portal data fetching
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Portal screens intentionally swallow fetch failures: non-OK responses or exceptions leave zeroed stats, blank forms, or stale lists rather than surfacing errors, and mutations trigger a full refetch instead of optimistic updates. The one deliberate counter-move is P0 #AP-07: demo-session tokens are still sent to the API (accepted in non-production) because the old startsWith('demo-') skip left demo managers on zeroed stats and hid real backend bugs.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: ISR + JSON-LD SEO architecture
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Content pages share a fixed SEO recipe: revalidate=86400 (daily ISR), a hardcoded BASE_URL of https://darshya.online baked into canonical/OG/JSON-LD URLs (must be edited everywhere if the domain changes), schema.org blobs injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and cross-links between hubs as a deliberate internal-linking strategy. Where generateStaticParams is combined with dynamicParams=false the route set is locked at build time, which silently turns runtime fallbacks into dead code.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Feature-flagged payment with backend verification
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Payment UX is chosen at runtime by backend feature flags (/gift-puja/config): autoFlowReady selects Stripe Elements via a clientSecret, otherwise an honest inquiry form, otherwise a mailto: — the design prefers degrading to a manual channel over failing. Payment completion is always confirmed by the backend (verify-payment), never by trusting Stripe client state, and downstream delivery gaps (WhatsApp not 'sent') are surfaced with a promised manual follow-up window rather than hidden.

79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.name: Hardcoded fixture data as API stand-in
79fd1f620501b953907a58c06539ae79392f9d6c.summary: Several public pages ship in-file fixture arrays annotated 'matches API' instead of fetching, so the frontend can drift from the backend without any type checking catching it. Combined with dynamicParams=false this produces real dead code (the defaultCow fallback can never render) and missing routes are papered over by linking to existing ones (gaushala cards point at cow detail pages because /gaushala/[gsId] was never built, ticket P1 #214).

2e937dbf20ba2e56b3c84f1bd5b1be672d30aabc.name: Header navigation controls & menus
2e937dbf20ba2e56b3c84f1bd5b1be672d30aabc.summary: Desktop header chrome: overflow/business/library dropdowns plus auth, cart, and language buttons. All dropdowns share one dismissal pattern — window mousedown/keydown listeners attached only while open (chosen over CSS :hover so touch devices work) — and NavAuthButton personalizes its menu by role and hard-navigates on sign-out. Non-obvious gotchas: LanguageSwitcher doubles as the content library's i18n dictionary (CONTENT_LABELS) and writes localStorage even in controlled mode; LibraryMegaPanel's documented flat-items fallback doesn't exist (a category without subGroups renders an empty grid); ListYourBusinessDropdown is hidden below lg, so mobile must surface those onboarding links elsewhere.
